590833454.text: The Capacities Monitoring application has been enhanced with resource-specific consumption cards and charts. These insights help you analyze capacity unit consumption by service, monitor usage trends, and identify major contributors to overall capacity utilization.
590833454.title: Enhanced Capacity Unit Monitoring

590833455.text:
The Capacity Unit Monitoring tool is enhanced with a customizable date and time range filter, enabling analysis beyond the current month. A new Spaces tab provides detailed consumption insights by space for Premium Outbound Integration, object store usage, and total capacity unit consumption.
See [Monitoring Capacity Unit Consumption](ba3d05baac854171914c09d64bed7202.html)
590833455.title: Enhanced Capacity Unit Monitoring

590833456.text:
The total statement memory limit for workloads generated by spaces or groups is now dynamically adjusted based on your tenant’s available free memory. You can still set limits, but the system automatically reduces them when insufficient memory is available. This improves system resilience by preserving sufficient capacity during peak usage without requiring manual intervention.
See [Set Priorities and Statement Limits for Spaces or Groups](d66ac1efb5054068a104c4559b72d272.html).
590833456.title: Dynamic Workload Memory Management to Strengthen Database Resilience

590833457.text:
You can now specify more properties for the database user password policy, including complexity requirements, expiration periods, and reuse restrictions.
See [Set a Password Policy for Database Users](14aedf6cecce474b93b2d5187662a090.html).
590833457.title: Enhanced Configuration for Database User Password Policy

590833458.text:
The Monitoring tool now features an enhanced navigation menu for easier access to key monitoring pages:
- System and Spaces – Monitor system performance, storage, tasks, and out-of-memory issues across all spaces. Track storage consumption and Apache Spark usage.
- Capacities Monitoring – Track monthly and daily capacity unit consumption against your subscription and download detailed hourly data.
- Task Logs – Review task execution history and performance.
- Expensive Statement Logs – Monitor SQL statements exceeding configured thresholds.
- Elastic Compute Nodes - Monitor elastic compute nodes key performance figures.
- Data Integration – Monitor, schedule, and run data replication tasks for remote tables and views. Manage flows and task chains.
See [Monitoring SAP Datasphere](d39b8652994846f9ab80b32fc5b4d671.html).
590833458.title: Improved Monitoring Tool Navigation

590833459.text:
In the System Monitor task logs, new columns for Apache Spark resource monitoring provide insights into memory usage, disk spill, and compute time, helping you to optimize application performance and debug issues efficiently.
See [Monitoring SAP Datasphere](d39b8652994846f9ab80b32fc5b4d671.html).
590833459.title: System Monitor: New Apache Spark Resource Monitoring Columns for Task Logs

590833460.text:
OAuth clients with a Technical User purpose can now use the OData API to consume data from any exposed asset, including those that are protected by data access controls.
See [Consuming Data Exposed by SAP Datasphere](d7d56284bb5148c887ac4054689bfbca.html).
590833460.title: Technical User OAuth Clients Support Data Access Controls When Accessing the OData API

590833461.text:
Administrators can find the Replication/Data Flow NAT IP (egress) and the Replication/Data Flow LB IP (ingress) addresses from the side navigation area by choosing: System  About  More.
See [Obtain SAP Datasphere IP addresses For Allowlisting in Remote Systems](0934f7ed9a534e638299f53ab60866ae.html).
590833461.title: Finding the Replication/Data Flow NAT IP (egress) and the Replication/Data Flow LB IP (ingress) IP Adresses

590833462.text:
For resilience purposes, we are now limiting to 80%, the maximum memory resources for workload generated by spaces, user group users and agent users. The remaining 20% of memory resources are reserved to ensure that the database can respond during high memory consumption periods.
In addition, a single statement cannot use more than 25% of the total memory once the total tenant memory consumption reaches 60% (see [3372747](https://me.sap.com/notes/3372747)).
See [Set Priorities and Statement Limits for Spaces or Groups](d66ac1efb5054068a104c4559b72d272.html).
590833462.title: Prevent Spaces from Consuming All Memory and Ensure Database Resiliency

590833463.text:
Administrators can find the Replication/Data Flow NAT IP (egress) and the Replication/Data Flow LB IP (ingress) addresses from the side navigation area by choosing: System  About  More.
See [Obtain SAP Datasphere IP addresses For Allowlisting in Remote Systems](0934f7ed9a534e638299f53ab60866ae.html).
590833463.title: Finding the Replication/Data Flow NAT IP (egress) and the Replication/Data Flow LB IP (ingress) IP Adresses

590833464.text:
The Users and Roles pages have been redesigned, and you can now:
- Create users and roles within dedicated wizards.
- Filter the list of users and roles in sophisticated ways.
See :
- [Managing SAP Datasphere Users](4fb82cb61ca84d8389e9cb18d94dab26.html)
- [Managing Roles and Privileges](3740dacbc2794f33bb5d8d42216cc3bc.html)
590833464.title: Users and Roles Page Redesign

590833465.text: The URLs of Business Builder objects now include the technical name of the object. Old bookmarks are deprecated and should be updated, but will continue to work for the time being.
590833465.title: Improved Business Builder Object URLs

590833466.text:
The SAP BW∕4HANA import wizard now creates an analytic model for each query imported and provides an option to control whether Business Builder objects are created.
See [Importing SAP BW∕4HANA Models](a3d4a2f91bea4810ba8839ff73577dac.html).
590833466.title: Import Queries as Analytic Models

590833467.text:
"Analytical Dataset" business entities are now renamed to "Facts" to align with the new "Fact" semantic usage available for Data Builder entities.
See :
- [Creating a Business Entity](c912cdc1537d4efbb24b08327ea68918.html)
- [Create a Fact to Contain Measurable Data](30089bd2aa754ab996a62cf5842ae60a.html)
- [Analytical Datasets (Deprecated)](70dab71147834c20b98ead017d7c5d8a.html)
590833467.title: "Analytical Dataset" Business Entities Renamed to "Fact"

590833468.text:
The definition of compound keys is now better supported by the UI.
See [Define a Key](9748bab194d94b9085eae7a139b55097.html).
590833468.title: Compound Keys

590833469.text:
Older perspectives use internal naming conventions for dimensions that are not stable when transporting between tenants.
You can now update these perspectives to make them safe for transport.
See [Define Perspectives](ce26fd3da31b414f9482292d3969340a.html).
590833469.title: Update Perspectives for Transport

590833470.text:
You can now export and import business entities, fact models, consumption models (including perspectives), and authorization scenarios via the  (Transport) app.
See [Transporting Content Between Tenants](df12666cf98e41248ef2251c564b0166.html).
590833470.title: Transport Business Builder Objects

590833471.text: The import of objects into the Business Builder is now executed in parallel and is therefore faster.
590833471.title: Improved Import of Objects into the Business Builder

590833472.text:
In the Business Builder, you can now convert currency values into another currency for business entities and consumption models.
See [Use Currency Conversion](1ba4554f0aaf40f7b5c0e430eb2da510.html).
590833472.title: Currency Conversion

590833473.text: For calculated measures, there are now more complex functions available.
590833473.title: Calculated Measures

590833474.text:
For business entities and fact models you can save the data preview as a consumption model.
See [Previewing Data in Business Builder Objects](3c58d6eb6b8b49e99e25a795f65e7173.html).
590833474.title: Create Consumption Model from Data Preview

590833475.text:
Business entities now support the definition of attributes with texts and language dependent texts. This enables you to display your data with ID and text, or with a language dependent text, when you preview or analyze your data.
See [Define Attributes](270bb3d19df04d96adca12d182bafdfb.html).
590833475.title: Text Associations

590833476.text:
Beside the standard aggregation types (SUM, MIN, MAX, AVG) you can now also use exception aggregation for measures.
See [Define Measures](903acb8d378d4984af8ad4f694d56529.html).
590833476.title: Exception Aggregation

590833477.text: When account dimension members are added, deleted, or updated for classic models, the catalog automatically extracts the latest metadata from the SAP Analytics Cloud source system. This ensures that the catalog assets are current with account dimension member changes.
590833477.title: Automatic Extraction of Account Dimension Members from SAP Analytics Cloud Classic Models

590833478.text:
The data product details page shows the lifecycle status. Consumers can filter by lifecycle status, such as active, provisioning, or data-loading. This information helps data stewards track and manage data products throughout their operational lifecycle.
See [Data Product Details](71f4d1599dba4aa59e6682a314650cf7.html).
590833478.title: Data Product Life Cycle Status

590833479.text:
The data product details page provides improved visibility of object (or entity) and column release statuses. Consumers can use this information to identify deprecated or decommissioned data objects and their recommended successors. This enables proactive migration planning and helps avoid dependencies on obsolete data during modeling and integration activities.
See [Data Product Details](71f4d1599dba4aa59e6682a314650cf7.html).
590833479.title: Release Status Indicators for Data Product Objects and Columns

590833480.text:
The Impact and Lineage Analysis Diagram now includes the target system in the impact of a shared data product. This enhancement provides a clearer view of data impact across all affected systems. You can see how data products are consumed beyond SAP Datasphere installations, which improves impact assessment and strengthens data governance across the entire data ecosystem.
See [Data Product Details](71f4d1599dba4aa59e6682a314650cf7.html).
590833480.title: Impact and Lineage Analysis Diagram Includes Target Systems for Shared Data Products

590833481.text:
The catalog can now extract metadata for the following SAP Analytics Cloud asset types:
- Add-in Workbook
- Analysis Workbook
- Composite
- Content Link
- Dataset
- Uploaded File
The metadata extracted includes the asset's name, the dates when it was created and changed, its container name, path, description, and other. The impact and lineage analysis diagram will be available for these objects in a future release.
See [Connecting to SAP Analytics Cloud Systems](27a4f9620761458dbc60cf9cf853989d.html).
590833481.title: Enhanced SAP Analytics Cloud Asset Type Support

590833482.text:
Natural language search capability is available for assets, terms, and key performance indicators (KPIs). You can formulate complex search queries conversationally instead of manually setting filters, enabling more intuitive discovery of data products through AI-powered query translation.
See [Natural Language Search](ea382a4ecb004cdd8edceebb63c7645b.html).
590833482.title: Search for Assets, Terms, and KPIs Using Natural Language

590833483.text:
The Data Protection and Privacy tag hierarchy is a system-defined tag hierarchy that helps identify data products containing personal data or sensitive personal data. During metadata extraction, the system automatically applies a data protection and privacy tag when it identifies a data product with personal data or sensitive personal data. Note
The catalog doesn't collect or store personal data or sensitive personal data.
See:
- [Using Hierarchical Tags](e5d46e7bcb1e4fb5bbcef852fd35ba87.html)
- [Data Product Details](71f4d1599dba4aa59e6682a314650cf7.html)
590833483.title: Display Data Protection and Privacy Tags in the Catalog

590833484.text:
Data products installed in an SAP Datasphere space now have an Update action, available when new minor versions are released. This improvement streamlines the workflow, providing a more efficient and intuitive process for users tasked with keeping data products current.
See [Requesting Access to Data Products](ea7cb802cbea47b39a441888873c3a49.html) and [Data Product Details](71f4d1599dba4aa59e6682a314650cf7.html).
590833484.title: Update Action Available for Installed Data Products

590833485.text:
A new link type (dashed line) has been added to the Impact and Lineage Analysis diagram for Data Transfer Processes (DTPA) and their associated Transformations (TRFN) across all BW systems. You can gain complete data traceability control by visualizing how one or more transformations are connected to and used within Data Transfer Processes (DTPs), enabling better understanding of data flow and dependencies in your BW environment.
See [Catalog Asset Details](afccc581146542c485a52563167e23cc.html).
590833485.title: Impact and Lineage Analysis Diagram Support for BW Data Transfer Process

590833486.text:
Data products that are created using the Data Sharing Cockpit of an SAP Datasphere system can be installed in modeling spaces in that SAP Datasphere system, as well as being shared to other consumers in your SAP Business Data Cloud formation.
See [Requesting Access to Data Products](ea7cb802cbea47b39a441888873c3a49.html).
590833486.title: Install Your Own Data Products

590833487.text:
When viewing the Impact and Lineage Analysis diagram for an SAP Analytics Cloud model or story that uses data from a live data connect, users will be able to see BW Query (ELEM) objects from SAP BW 7.5 in the analyzed object's lineage.
See [Catalog Asset Details](afccc581146542c485a52563167e23cc.html).
590833487.title: BW Query Objects (ELEM) from SAP BW 7.5 Included in the Impact and Lineage Analysis Diagram for an SAP Analytics Cloud Model or Story

590833488.text:
When searching for data products in the catalog, select the Data Products collection and enter a search string in natural language. The search phrase you enter will be interpreted, and results will be filtered accordingly.
See [Natural Language Search](ea382a4ecb004cdd8edceebb63c7645b.html).
590833488.title: Search for Data Products Using Natural Language

590833489.text:
You can now connect SAP BW 7.5 systems to the catalog and set up a synchronization schedule so that its objects will appear in the catalog.
- ADSO (Advanced DataStore Object)
- ALVL (Aggregation Level)
- AREA (InfoArea)
- DTPA (Data Transfer Process)
- DEST (Open Hub Destination)
- DSUB (Data Subscription)
- ELEM (BW Query)
- FBPA (Open ODS View)
- HCPR (Composite Provider)
- IOBJ (InfoObject)
- LSYS (Source System)
- RSDS (DataSource)
- TRCS (InfoSource)
- TRFN (Transformation)
Catalog administrators will be able to enrich these object types with term, KPI, and tag relationships and then publish them for easy discovery by catalog users.
See [Connecting to BW Systems](b350d7c6e88c4f089d381dfe6feee792.html).
590833489.title: Ability to Connect SAP BW 7.5 Systems to the Catalog

590833490.text:
You can now import and export objects in file spaces via the command line.
See:
- [Manage Spaces and Space Access via the Command Line](5eac5b71e2d34c32b63f3d8d47a0b1d0.html)
- [Manage Modeling Objects and Tasks via the Command Line](6f5c65f209004751aa48f9682ee2ec45.html)
- [Manage Connectivity via the Command Line](3918242966c74f11858db39c8e5228e4.html)
590833490.title: Work with File Space Objects via the Command Line

590833491.text:
You can now configure Cloud Connector for Connections to Confluent Cloud. Cloud Connector acts as a reverse invoke proxy and routes traffic through a TLS tunnel, allowing you to use replication flows to replicate data from or write data to Apache Kafka hosted on Confluent Cloud if it doesn't necessarily have public endpoints.
See [Confluent Connections](d83c08ad4eaf49dba9602b1d51c07a52.html#loiod83c08ad4eaf49dba9602b1d51c07a52).
590833491.title: Cloud Connector Support for Confluent Cloud Connections

590833492.text:
You can export runtime settings for persisted views included run mode and partitions during transport operations. This will ensure consistent runtime behavior across environments.
See [Change Persisted View Settings](d04f5dd6bbda44448407d54d2a7979be.html).
590833492.title: Include Persisted View Runtime Settings in Transport Packages

590833493.text:
You can now use your Oracle wallet to support encrypted communication using SSL and certificate-based authentication via mTLS. SSL support is available both for basic authentication and certificate-based authentication. When using the Wallet authentication type, you can use the connection for replication flows. Remote tables and data flows are not supported with Oracle Wallet.
To be able to use Oracle wallet, a new section Authentication to select the authentication type and an additional field in the Security section to upload the required server certificate when using SSL have been introduced.
If you want to use an existing connection for replication flows with Oracle wallet, you need to edit the connection and complete the SSL properties and credentials.
See [Oracle Connections](c73ae0601d364f47830d339b6e86b7e8.html).
590833493.title: Oracle Connections: Enhanced Authentication Option with Oracle Wallet for Replication Flows

590833494.text:
You can now use Oracle as a source connection in replication flows to replicate data into supported targets with the Initial Only load type.
See:
- [Select Source and Target Connections for Replication Flows](10891192186c4920b08939a7b46adc79.html)
- [Oracle Connections](c73ae0601d364f47830d339b6e86b7e8.html)
590833494.title: Use Oracle as a Source in Replication Flows

590833495.text:
You can now create replication flows from object store sources such as Amazon S3, Microsoft Azure Data Lake Gen2, Google Cloud Storage, SFTP, SAP Hana Data Lake Files, and Microsoft OneLake into local table files.
See [Cloud Storage Provider Sources for Replication Flows](4d481a2c620f4b52ba65b360299d7719.html).
590833495.title: Use Object Store Sources in Replication Flows

590833496.text:
Data Integrators and Modelers can export runtime settings (including SAP HANA run modes, batch configurations, and Spark application configuration) alongside transformation flows during transport operations, ensuring consistent runtinme behavior across environments.
See [Change Transformation Flow Settings](f7da0290f5084e3db17c65b3d7c3140a.html).
590833496.title: Include Transformation Flow Runtime Settings in Transport Packages

590833497.text:
Snowflake is now available as a source connection in replication flows with support for the Initial Only load type.
See: [Snowflake Sources for Replication Flows](af67fc6241d445e9b49ccd2f03d72f9e.html)
590833497.title: Use Snowflake as a Source in Replication Flows

590833498.text:
You can now mask sensitive column data in replication flows from ABAP sources to SAP Signavio targets using the SHA3-256 algorithm. This helps protect sensitive data by replacing original values with hashed strings before they are written to the target.
See [SAP Signavio Targets for Replication Flows](b8f5e28d34b44d71a52f6265e4fc245f.html).
590833498.title: Mask Sensitive Data with Column Hashing in Replication Flows

590833499.text:
You can now configure Cloud Connector for Google BigQuery. Cloud Connector acts as a reverse invoke proxy and routes traffic through a TLS tunnel, allowing you to use replication flows to write data to Google BigQuery target systems that don't necessarily have public endpoints.
See [Google BigQuery Connections](30ed77de13864368bdc596099b37ed70.html).
590833499.title: Cloud Connector Support for Google BigQuery Connections

590833500.text:
In the Local Tables monitor, a new validation message area has been introduced to help you take proactive actions on your local tables—reducing the risk of out-of-memory errors and addressing partitioning issues more effectively. In addition, for SAP Datasphere apps that consume local tables, the validation message area can now display partitioning recommendations tailored to help you optimize performance and maintain system stability.
[Monitoring Local Tables](374046156e5b47599fc9b96c8c3a4dce.html).
590833500.title: Validation Message Area Available in Local Tables monitor

590833501.text:
You can import calculation views from SAP HANA Cloud as remote tables while preserving semantic information. This helps you leverage existing SAP HANA Cloud analytical models without recreating them, maintaining their business context and metadata for consistent data modeling across platforms.
Only calculation views deployed in SAP HANA Cloud version QRC 1/2026 or higher can be imported in SAP Datasphere database version 2025.50 or higher.
To ensure that your calculation view can be imported, deploy the calculation view in the source system with SAP Business Data Cloud Integration Mode set to Flat View or Construction Kit.
See:
- [Importing Entities with Semantics from SAP HANA Cloud](b37282c4c0d142e3bca256a46cd40278.html)
- [SAP HANA Connections](e6b63f176d3640609adcf06297fb37e9.html#loioe6b63f176d3640609adcf06297fb37e9)
590833501.title: Import SAP HANA Cloud Calculation Views

590833502.text:
When creating a replication flow with a Local Table (File) target, the Merge Data Automatically option is now disabled by default. This helps reduce unnecessary merge operations and associated compute workloads. You can still enable the option if automatic merging of new data is required.
See [Creating a Replication Flow](25e2bd7a70d44ac5b05e844f9e913471.html).
590833502.title: Auto-Merge Disabled by Default for Local Table (File) Targets

590833503.text:
You can now run, stop, and obtain the status of replication flows via the command line.
See [Running and Managing Tasks via the Command Line](2b26a31f197444dea314495bc0008eae.html).
590833503.title: Manage Replication Flow Runs via the Command Line

590833504.text:
You can now enable Create Large Files when replicating data to supported cloud object store targets using the Parquet file format. This creates fewer, larger files during the initial load.
See [Cloud Storage Provider Targets for Replication Flows](43d93a27150a4a218e3df14e3abdf456.html).
590833504.title: Create Large Parquet Files for Object Store Targets

590833505.text:
During table replication, the primary key order from the source is preserved in the target to prevent replication failures caused by key order mismatches.
See [Creating a Replication Flow](25e2bd7a70d44ac5b05e844f9e913471.html).
590833505.title: Improved Primary Key Order Handling in Replication Flows

590833506.text:
Uninstalling data products is now faster and all related artifacts including replication flows are removed.
See [Requesting Access to Data Products](ea7cb802cbea47b39a441888873c3a49.html).
590833506.title: Optimized Data Product Uninstallation

590833507.text:
While running an optimize task for your local table (file), you can define Z-order columns to co-locate the data by columns, and thus reduce the amount of data that needs to be read.
See [Merge or Optimize Your Local Tables (File)](e533b154ed3e49ce9a03e4421a5296e7.html).
590833507.title: Define Z-ORDER COLUMNS While Running an Optimize Task

590833508.text:
You can now use the Initial Only and Initial and Delta load types for local table (file) targets when Delta Capture is ON in replication flows.
See [SAP Datasphere Targets for Replication Flows](12c45eb2659f4069b29ef4d69bdd9070.html)
590833508.title: Initial Only Load Type Now Supported for Local Table Targets When Delta Capture is ON

590833509.text:
To avoid a system overload with automated merge tasks, a threshold of 10 consecutive failed merge runs for local tables (file) has been implemented: After reaching that threshold, any further run of a merge task for that Local Table (File) will fail immediately (before creating any Apache Spark workload) with the status FAILED (TOO_MANY_FAILURES).
See [Merge or Optimize Your Local Tables (File)](e533b154ed3e49ce9a03e4421a5296e7.html).
590833509.title: Too Many Merge Task Failures Will Pause the Task

590833510.text:
You can delete records waiting in the inbound buffer of a local table (file), even if a merge task has not run.
See [Delete Data From Your Local Tables (File)](872ad509995a451890bf8b80b73ec0e6.html).
590833510.title: Delete Records Waiting in the Inbound Buffer

590833511.text:
Generic OData connections provide new options applying to remote tables:
- You can select Form Data as OAuth Token Request Content Type to create connections for ODATA service endpoints that expect the OAuth2 token request to be sent using content type multipart/form-data and client credentials to be sent as form-data fields in the request body. Note
If you select Form Data, data flows are disabled for the connection.
- You can use the Support Format Query property to allow specifying the format in which data should be returned (using the $format=<format> query option). The property is enabled by default. If you disable the property, the format query option is ignored, and the connection always returns the default response format of the OData service.This property is available in the Configure Advanced Properties step (when creating connections) or in the Show Advanced Properties section (when editing connection). The advanced properties include the already existing option to add custom HTTP headers.
See [Generic OData Connections](5d36f1aae68a4e59989c424a66d948c9.html).
590833511.title: Generic OData Connections: Select Form Data as OAuth Token Request Content Type And Use Format Query Option

590833512.text:
You can now assign a technical user to schedule data integration tasks. This allows you to minimize the number of users that manage schedules. Additionally, this avoids failed schedules and tasks related to expired consent and authorization.
See [Modify the Owner of a Schedule](4b660c0395454bd0923f732eef4ee4b2.html).
590833512.title: Use OAuth Clients with Specific Privileges and Permissions to Run Schedules

590833513.text:
You can now replicate data stored in parquet files when using the following cloud storage providers as the source of your replication flow:
- Amazon Simple Storage Service
- Google Cloud Storage
- Microsoft Azure Data Lake Gen2
See [Cloud Storage Provider Sources for Replication Flows](4d481a2c620f4b52ba65b360299d7719.html).
590833513.title: Parquet File Format Now Supported for Cloud Storage Sources for Replication Flows

590833514.text:
The algorithm used to generate a unique filename to allow SAP Datasphere to suppress duplicate records in a replication flow is changing. The migration process might affect the suppression mechanism, and you might see duplicate records in your target objects (Cloud Storage Provider Targets).
See[Cloud Storage Provider Targets for Replication Flows](43d93a27150a4a218e3df14e3abdf456.html) .
590833514.title: Suppress Duplicates in Replication Might Fail During Algorithm Migration

590833515.text:
Add new columns to the existing tables of a listed SAP Business Data Cloud data product.
See [Updating Artifacts for Listed Data Products for SAP Business Data Cloud](689aa9d06a494b828ec90b8dc0537c8e.html).
590833515.title: Update Listed Data Product Tables

590833516.text:
Add new tables to the artifacts of a listed SAP Business Data Cloud data product.
See [Updating Artifacts for Listed Data Products for SAP Business Data Cloud](689aa9d06a494b828ec90b8dc0537c8e.html).
590833516.title: Update Listed Data Product Artifacts

590833517.text:
The new API endpoint /dsc/providers/activate is available to activate data provider memberships using activation keys.
For more information, see the API documentation on the [SAP Business Accelerator Hub](https://api.sap.com/api/DataSharingCockpit/overview).
590833517.title: New API Endpoint

590833518.text:
Two new API endpoints are available:
- /consumer/products/{productUUID}/install to install a data product as a consumer.
- /dsc/providers/{providerUUID}/licenses/{licenseUUID}/activationKeys/assignUsers to assign users to a license key.
For more information, see the API documentation on the [SAP Business Accelerator Hub](https://api.sap.com/api/DataSharingCockpit/overview).
590833518.title: New API Endpoints

590833519.text:
Create a SQL view transform to combine and transform data using a SQL editor using Apache Spark SQL. Use this feature to build complex data transformations with auto-complete suggestions, drag-and-drop source objects, real-time validation and data preview capabilities.
See [Create a SQL View in a Transformation Flow on File](06c4e72bcbee46568be499c77a3a0d00.html).
590833519.title: SQL View Transform in Transformation Flows on File

590833520.text:
Intelligent applications are renamed to intelligent content.
Intelligent content includes prebuilt SAP Analytics Cloud stories and MyMetrics (KPIs) for various SAP lines of business or solution areas, along with flows, views, analytic models and other SAP Analytics Cloud objects to prepare data for them.
Intelligent content is built on data products, supports analytics, planning, and AI and machine learning use cases, and can be simply and seamlessly installed from the SAP Analytics Cloud cockpit.
For more information, see [Installing Intelligent Content](344999cbd4ff4d8188fb67b4ca6ea33f.html).
590833520.title: Intelligent Content

590833521.text:
You can now retry failed task chains or cancel running task chains with REST APIs. You can also use new CLI commands to retry and cancel task chains. For more information,
See :
- [Managing Tasks via the REST API](274f2736465c4c48a091c675880502a2.html)
- [Running and Managing Tasks via the Command Line](2b26a31f197444dea314495bc0008eae.html)
590833521.title: Manage Task Chains with REST APIs

590833522.text:
The following request now provides additional information about the definition of variables and filters:
GET https://<tenant_url>/api/v1/datasphere/consumption/relational/<space_id>/<asset_id>/$metadata See [Consuming Data via the OData API](7a453609c8694b029493e7d87e0de60a.html).
590833522.title: OData Consumption API: Improved Metadata

590833523.text:
When running a data flow within a task chain, you can now enable the "Enable Checkup" option to generate a detailed health analysis log. This log provides in-depth analysis to help your support team quickly identify and resolve run errors.
See [Creating a Task Chain](d1afbc2b9ee84d44a00b0b777ac243e1.html).
590833523.title: Enable Checkup Option to Debug Your Data Flow in a Task Chain

590833524.text: For analytic models that use another analytic model as source, you can switch on Show Inherited Elements in the properties panel.
590833524.title: Show Inherited Elements for Analytic Models

590833525.text:
- Local tables: Default is 0 and values must comprise between 0 and 999 days
- Local tables (file): Default is 7 and values must comprise between 7 and 999 days
The default retention period has been updated as follows:See :
- [Deleting Local Table (File) Records](6ec9b8a89dc64b5cac069cee81399c92.html)
- [Delete Data From Your Local Tables (File)](872ad509995a451890bf8b80b73ec0e6.html)
- [Load or Delete Local Table Data](870401f211f94132909bd9f2fafd91b2.html)
- [Controlling Deletion of Local Table Records](2a59b7142e1b4d478b0bf4063084261e.html)
590833525.title: Default Retention Period Updated for Both Local Tables and Local Tables (File)

590833526.text:
In the table editor, you can create partitions on existing SAP-Managed local tables stored in a standard space (with SAP HANA Database (Disk and In-Memory) storage) that already contain data.
See :
- [Partitioning Local Tables](03191f36e9144b2aaa47b8c9eea039c1.html)
- [Partitioning Local Tables for Intelligent Content](07d9768ac03343498ae1d1da41f03241.html)
590833526.title: Create Partitions on SAP-Managed Local Tables That Contain Data

590833527.text:
Additional local table deletion activities for task chains are supported:
- Delete All Records for both Local Tables and Local Tables (file)
- Delete Filtered Records for both Local Tables and Local Tables (file)
See [Creating a Task Chain](d1afbc2b9ee84d44a00b0b777ac243e1.html)
590833527.title: Task Chains Support All Deletion Types for Both Local Tables and Local Tables (File)

590833528.text:
You will automatically receive an email notification before your authorization consent expires. This will help ensure your scheduled tasks will continue without interruption.
See[Changing SAP Datasphere Settings](1084796d09464e78870f32cab8584dfc.html).
590833528.title: Email Notification for Expiring Consent

590833529.text:
You can now share an analytic model to another space, and even multiple spaces. You can then create a new analytic model on top of that in order to consume this model from other spaces.
See [Sharing Analytic Models to Other Spaces](8b84bd8dbbbf498f9dff8add4bff6489.html).
590833529.title: Share Analytic Models

590833530.text:
You can now simply share SQL views containing a currency conversion column to another space, without needing also to share all the supporting currency conversion entities too.
See :
- [Create a Currency Conversion Column in a Graphical View](6e3d8bed7ece4c27ba10e2cc523915fe.html)
- [Enabling Currency Conversion with TCUR* Tables and Views](b462239ffb644d9baab4442a10a72edf.html)
590833530.title: Simplified Sharing of Views Containing Currency Conversion

590833531.text:
You can use output parameters in task chain objects. You can also map output parameters to the task chain from the task object. This will allow for more flexible usage of task chains and nested task chains.
See [.](c6e2e01a9df7454fb23707887470ccf1.html)
590833531.title: Using Output Parameters in Task Chains

590833532.text:
You can now filter on aggregated measure values when creating your OData requests.
For example, to filter for where dimension Partner_IDis equal to 100000005 and measure Value is greater than one million, use the syntax:?$filter=Partner_ID eq 100000005 and Value gt 1OOOOOO
See [Consuming Data via the OData API](7a453609c8694b029493e7d87e0de60a.html).
590833532.title: Filter on Aggregated Measure Values in OData Consumption API

590833533.text:
If your SAP Datasphere is part of an SAP Business Data Cloud formation, you can now create partitions for local tables installed via SAP Business Data Cloud as part of an intelligent application. This enables you to break your data down into chunks, and better manage read-only tables with large volume of data.
See [Partitioning Local Tables for Intelligent Content](07d9768ac03343498ae1d1da41f03241.html).
590833533.title: Partitioning Local Tables for Intelligent Applications

590833534.text:
You can now review a list of past versions of transformation flows, and:
- Open a past version in read-only mode.
- Download a past version to a CSN/JSON file.
- Restore a past version to replace the current version.
See [Reviewing and Restoring Object Versions](4f717cc0d90e4453a072b37f6b043593.html).
590833534.title: Review and Restore Transformation Flow Versions

590833535.text:
When working with transformation flows, out-of-memory errors can be difficult to understand. You can now get more guidance when running a transformation flow directly in the monitoring screen.
For more information, see [Transformation Flows and Memory Consumption](b266bf41f3e845b68519fca2b399a2c0.html).
590833535.title: Transformation Flow: Get More Guidance for Out-of-Memory Errors

590833536.text:
The Data Pipeline Analyzer enables you to monitor complex data models efficiently, allowing you to view and analyze errors, warnings, and data discrepancies in real-time. It quickly identifies data transfer failures, allowing you to take immediate action to resolve them.
See [Data Pipeline Analyzer](54fd00ddd0b24ccc9ce0fa55297bc13d.html)
590833536.title: Use the Data Pipeline Analyzer to Quickly Identify and Resolve Issues With Your Data Model

590833537.text:
Allow up to three automatic retries for a task in a task chain. This feature will automatically retry failed tasks to help complete a task in a task chain and improve resilience.
See, [Creating a Task Chain](d1afbc2b9ee84d44a00b0b777ac243e1.html)
590833537.title: Enable Auto-Retry for a Task in a Task Chain

590833538.text:
You can use REST APIs to run task chains and retrieve task logs and existing task log history. You can also use a new CLI command to get flexible and controlled log information. For more information,
See :
- [Managing Tasks via the REST API](274f2736465c4c48a091c675880502a2.html)
- [Running and Managing Tasks via the Command Line](2b26a31f197444dea314495bc0008eae.html)
590833538.title: Manage Tasks with REST APIs

590833539.text:
The Remove Duplicates operator allows users to efficiently remove duplicate records from their transformation flow in a file space. By sorting records and selecting specific columns for duplicate removal, users can ensure data integrity and streamline their data processing tasks.
See [Creating a Transformation Flow in a File Space](b917baf0431343bea8381fa37e12eeb8.html).
590833539.title: Transformation Flows in File Spaces - Duplicate Records Removal Feature

590833540.text:
The Repository Explorer and other apps where natural language search is available now automatically show the interpretation of your search phrase in the AI-Generated Filter Conditions filter bar.
See [Natural Language Search](04170c64c1004fc58d7f235aea0e4970.html).
590833540.title: Natural Language Search - Access to Interpreted Filter Criteria

590833541.text:
You can now select the new Display Dimension Keys as Node Keys option to display the dimension key values (which are often more informative than the hierarchy node keys), when drilling down into your hierarchy in analytic models and in SAP Analytics Cloud.
Note
After enabling this option, you must redeploy any analytic models that consume it in order to see the dimension keys.
See [Create a Hierarchy with Directory](36c39eee184c485a80ebce9d0fec49ec.html).
590833541.title: Hierarchy with Directory: Improved Hierarchy Node IDs

590833542.text:
If your SAP Datasphere is part of an SAP Business Data Cloud formation, you can now install a single intelligent application multiple times for different source systems. Each source system creates (or re-uses) its own ingestion space to contain its data products. Source-specific preparation and application spaces identified by an alias are created for each instance of the intelligent application.
See [Reviewing Installed Intelligent Content](644648756d334daaaf35d4fc9a0feeda.html).
590833542.title: Installing an Intelligent Application for Two or More Source Systems

590833543.text:
A new validation rule can help resolve the problem of hierarchies with directories which are showing inaccurate data due to data node columns containing values when the node is not a data node.
Note
The hierarchy with directory Set as Leaf option is renamed to Set as Data Node.
See [Validating View Data](ed4063dc7f53436d806ea48f2fd3949a.html).
590833543.title: Data Validation: Misplaced Hierarchy Data Nodes

590833544.text:
You can create partitions on existing local tables stored in a standard space (with SAP HANA Database (Disk and In-Memory) storage) that already contain data.
See [Partitioning Local Tables](03191f36e9144b2aaa47b8c9eea039c1.html)
590833544.title: Create Partitions on Local Tables That Contains Existing Data

590833545.text:
The increased maximum length for technical names in Data Builder objects and elements allows for more descriptive and detailed naming conventions.
The maximum length has changed for the following objects and elements:
- Views, tables, E/R models: 100
- Views with semantic usage Analytical Dataset (Deprecated): 60
- Analytic Models: 60
- Hierarchies created inside a dimension view: 20
- Columns: 100
- Input parameters: 100
See [Rules for Technical Names](982f9a30d4ab49c8b019cfaf3dc08391.html).
590833545.title: Use Longer Technical Names When Creating Data Builder Objects and Elements

590833546.text:
The restriction preventing any permission entity from being itself protected by a data access control or having protected views among its sources is removed. Permissions entities and their sources can now have data access controls attached, though this may impact performance.
See [Securing Data with Data Access Controls](a032e51c730147c7a1fcac125b4cfe14.html).
590833546.title: Protection of Permissions Entities

590833547.text:
When creating an association from a fact to a dimension, you can now choose to apply the dimension's data access controls directly to the fact data.
Applying dimension data access controls directly to facts will resolve an issue where users may see null aggregate values for records that they do not have permission to view.
You can see any data access controls applied in this way in a subsection Applied via Dimensions under the list of Data Access Controls in the side panel.
See [Apply a Data Access Control to a Graphical or SQL View](8f79fc80d6134a89a03837a205d340cd.html)
590833547.title: Application and Visibility of Data Access Controls Applied to Associated Dimensions

590833548.text: You can now define filter conditions to restrict the input and/or lookup records that will be considered for matching in any individual rule.See [Create an Exact Match Rule](897d26c3ffe24efaa27cd0d7262a78ad.html) and [Create a Fuzzy Match Rule](b063518d7a684051b66cc6d9681c8753.html).
590833548.title: Intelligent Lookup: Rule-Level Filtering of Input and Lookup Records

590833549.text:
You can now sort and filter by multiple columns in the right-hand table of lookup entity records on the Multiple and Unmatched tabs in the intelligent lookup rule data preview pane.
See [Process Multiple Match Results](cb2b78a037c346ccad0ade79c6e85c54.html) and [Process Unmatched Results](35fbb44d62e7498bb54461d3a4d460d5.html).
590833549.title: Intelligent Lookup: Improved Sorting and Filtering of Lookup Records in Unmatched and Multiple Match Results

590833550.text:
A new option, Multiple Match Processing, will now auto-select among multiple matches when one match candidate scores conclusively higher than any other. You can disable this default behavior (and review each of your multiple matches manually) by setting this option to Always Review Match Candidates.
See [Create a Fuzzy Match Rule](b063518d7a684051b66cc6d9681c8753.html).
590833550.title: Auto-Select the Best Match Candidate in Intelligent Lookup Fuzzy Match Results

590833551.text:
A number of usability enhancements are available in the intelligent lookup editor:
- The Preview panel is now bigger, by default, when opened and will remember its size if you resize it. In addition:
- The Review tab now supports selecting multiple pairing groups before clicking Confirm or Reject.
- The Multiple tab now lists match candidates in descending order of match score, and includes a Reject button to allow you to select a pairing group for which none of the proposed match candidates is appropriate and move the records to the Unmatched tab.
- You can now filter and sort the left and right tables on the Multiple and Unmatched tabs independently, and the filter is persisted after matching or rejecting a pairing group.
- The Unprocessed tab is moved to the penultimate position (before the Error) tab.
- A new Include Review Records option on the output node is selected by default, but can be disabled to exclude records on the Review tab from your output view.
See [Creating an Intelligent Lookup](8f29f801faea4d48816d0339777f9d16.html).
590833551.title: Intelligent Lookup Usability Enhancements

590833552.text:
The Save  Save As command is now available in the intelligent lookup editor.
See [Saving and Deploying Objects](7c0b560e2cb94eea86219d78d87f9623.html).
590833552.title: Save a Copy of an Intelligent Lookup

590833553.text:
When combining data, there may be no column in your primary entity that contains data to uniquely identify a record in the other entity, and which would thus allow the creation of a standard join. Or, if such a column (a foreign key) exists, its data may be incomplete or unreliable. This can be particularly common when one of the entities comes from outside your organization. It may require a lot of manual work in spreadsheets to join the entities, and the results of this work may not be easy to reuse when new data arrives.
Intelligent lookup is a business-centric, interactive data harmonization environment for subject matter experts, which lets you iteratively join entities by defining rules to match records and then reviewing the results.
See [Creating an Intelligent Lookup](8f29f801faea4d48816d0339777f9d16.html).
590833553.title: Intelligent Lookup

590833554.text:
You can now configure in the user profile settings area if you want to receive system notifications. For example, while creating replication flows or task chains you can configure email notifications to receive a notification when a task is completed.
See [Changing SAP Datasphere Settings](1084796d09464e78870f32cab8584dfc.html).
590833554.title: Enable System Notifications

590833555.text: A change in certificates has been implemented for SAP Datasphere. You need to update your Java VM version used for Cloud Connector. If your connections involving Cloud Connector fail, check your Java VM version and update it to the new version. For more information about the background and required actions, see SAP Note [3556127](https://me.sap.com/notes/3556127).
590833555.title: Check and Update your Java VM Version - relevant if you use Cloud Connector

590833556.text:
Using the new With Grant Option property, a database user can now grant access to the APL and PAL libraries to space users who need to run procedures in the Open SQL schema via a task chain.
See [Create a Database User](798e3fd6707940c3bd2219b2d1ebaac2.html).
590833556.title: Grant Automated Predictive Library (APL) and Predictive Analysis Library (PAL) Access

590833557.text:
To protect your tenant from storage-related outages, SAP Datasphere will now lock all spaces once a critical threshold of disk usage is attained. A message informs you in the Space Management app and in each space page. To continue working with your tenant, you must either increase your tenant disk storage or delete unneeded data.
See [Unlock a Locked Space](c05b6a6d06db427dbdd3041d61fd5840.html) and [Manage Tenant Disk Storage](27d4c686dc9f49c5bd70d826232ee814.html).
590833557.title: Improved Tenant Stability: Critical Storage Threshold

590833558.text:
After a one-year deprecation period, the following parameters in the .json file containing the space definition are now decommissioned:
- priority
- workloadClass.totalStatementMemoryLimit.value
- workloadClass.totalStatementMemoryLimit.unit
- workloadClass.totalStatementThreadLimit.value
- workloadClass.totalStatementThreadLimit.unit
See [The Space Definition File Format](3fcbf619f2774b849fa7df58163b3609.html).
To set priorities and statement limits for spaces or groups, you must use the datasphere workload command (see [Managing Priorities and Statement Limits for Spaces or Groups via the Command Line](9e3537b72e6c445d9f34201df650735b.html)).
590833558.title: Command Line Interface Parameters for Setting Space Priorities and Statement Limits for Spaces Now Decommissioned

590833559.text: A new view is available in the BW modeling tools. In the Manage Transport Objects view, you can collect a large number of local objects in a list and assign them to a transport request.
590833559.title: Manage Transport Objects View

590833560.text: You can now check whether changes have been made to the data flow and then update the data protection template by choosing Sync Template.
590833560.title: Automating the Creation and Processing of Data Protection Worklists

590833561.text:
In the SAP BW Bridge Cockpit in the Process Graph Display app, you can find a graphical display in the form of a Gantt chart that shows all SAP BW processes that ran in the selected period of time. This allows you to see which processes have consumed how many resources.
In addition to the status of the process, the following key figures can be visualized:
- Average CPU Usage (ABAP) A list of process chains, sorted by the average CPU usage caused by processes in ABAP.
- Average Peak Memory (ABAP) A list of process chains, sorted by the average peak memory usage caused by processes in ABAP.
- Average CPU Usage (Database) A list of process chains, sorted by the average CPU usage caused by processes on the SAP HANA database.
- Average Peak Memory Usage (Database) A list of process chains, sorted by the average peak memory usage caused by processes on the SAP HANA database.
See [Process Graph Display](https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_BW_BRIDGE/107a6e8a38b74ede94c833ca3b7b6f51/d8e576798cd842559667598b1d00112e.html)
590833561.title: Process Graph Display

590833562.text: SAP BW bridge is now available for the EU30 (Europe -Frankfurt), IN30 (India - Mumbai), and US30 (US Central -IA) regions running on the Google Cloud Platform (GCP).See [Creating and Configuring Your SAP Datasphere Tenant](2f80b57359254b5cbb4faac794ade90c.html).
590833562.title: Data Center Availability

590833563.text: You can now import tables for delta extraction from an SAP BW bridge connection into an SAP BW bridge space.
590833563.title: Delta Extraction

590833564.text: A process chain for streaming can be started and executed very frequently, and makes it possible to update data in real-time to DataStore objects. Process chains therefore provide a holistic solution for periodic and very frequent scheduling and for streaming. You set whether or not a process chain should be used for streaming using an attribute in the process chain. See [Process Chains for Streaming](https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_BW_BRIDGE/107a6e8a38b74ede94c833ca3b7b6f51/ac029de05e164a12ac1ce08d16180f05.html) in the SAP BW bridge documentation.
590833564.title: Process Chains for Streaming

590833565.text:
In the Me Area in the SAP BW bridge cockpit, you can make launchpad settings.
The SAP Fiori launchpad displays notifications from the Request Management and Process Chains areas that are relevant for you due to your business role.
See [Notifications](https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_BW_BRIDGE/107a6e8a38b74ede94c833ca3b7b6f51/6c5d18f5abbf48d995cf173e979b8ec8.html) in the SAP BW bridge documentation.
590833565.title: Settings and Notifications in the SAP BW Bridge Cockpit

590833566.text: You can use various APIs to load, activate, and delete data. See [APIs for InfoObjects and DataStore Objects](https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_BW_BRIDGE/b3701cd3826440618ef938d74dc93c51/188562b742aa4f1ebd355294086049f6.html) in the SAP BW bridge documentation.
590833566.title: APIs for InfoObjects and DataStore Objects

590833567.text: If you create an InfoObject or a DataStore object and select the package ZLOCAL or a subordinate package, the system issues a warning as objects in the package ZLOCAL cannot be transported.
590833567.title: Creating Objects

590833568.text: It is now possible to overwrite existing objects in SAP BW bridge.
590833568.title: Synchronizing Objects from SAP BW∕4HANA

590833569.text: As an administrator, you want to create a connection to a source system of type ODP in order to extract data from an ODP SOAP (HTTP) source.
590833569.title: Creating Source Systems of Type ODP (SOAP/HTTP)

590833570.text:
In the BW Modeling tools, a new default view is available that displays the ABAP packages with the BW objects assigned to them.
You can also create objects for the selected package here. The package is then preselected for these objects.
This assignment is important in SAP BW bridge because it allows you to recognize the relationship to the software component which is the basis for transport.
590833570.title: Package Explorer View

590833571.text:
New features are now available for anonymizing data records.
- Propagation of updates of anonymized data
- Anonymization of data in data mart DataStore objects
- New formula editor for definition of anonymization rules
- New function for simulating anonymization
See [Anonymizing Data Using the Data Protection Workbench](https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_BW_BRIDGE/107a6e8a38b74ede94c833ca3b7b6f51/214922c4dd93476394f961fde8ad97fc.html?locale=en-US) in the SAP BW bridge documentation.
590833571.title: Anonymizing Data Using the Data Protection Workbench

590833572.text:
For scenarios with a high frequency of data loading, there is now a new way to load data into the corresonding object, the messaging request.
To to use this option, you have to include the new process type PUSH_MSGR, Close messaging request, in your process chain
590833572.title: Loading Data into DataStore Objects and InfoObjects with Write Interface

590833573.text:
In the SAP Datasphere, SAP BW Bridge Cockpit, you can now use the Source Systems – Maintain IDs app to define source system IDs for source systems or groups of source systems.
See [Using Source System IDs](https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_BW_BRIDGE/107a6e8a38b74ede94c833ca3b7b6f51/ccf50027ead14dedab2c37df83c97369.html?version=latest) in the SAP BW bridge documentation.
590833573.title: Assigning IDs to Source Systems

590833574.text:
In the SAP Datasphere, SAP BW Bridge Cockpit, you can now use the Data Load Languages - Maintain app to select which of the languages available in the cloud you want the texts (master data texts) to be imported in.
See [Apps at a Glance](https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_BW_BRIDGE/107a6e8a38b74ede94c833ca3b7b6f51/65fc810abf0549ee861b0d2c7b73ada2.html?version=latest) in the SAP BW bridge documentation.
590833574.title: Selecting Languages for Importing Texts

590833575.text:
In the SAP Datasphere, SAP BW Bridge Cockpit, you can now use the Query app to obtain an overview of all analytical queries available for import.
See [Apps at a Glance](https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_BW_BRIDGE/107a6e8a38b74ede94c833ca3b7b6f51/65fc810abf0549ee861b0d2c7b73ada2.html?version=latest) in the SAP BW bridge documentation.
590833575.title: Overview of Queries Available for Import

590833576.text:
You can now use InfoObjects with a write interface. Texts and attributes are supported by the familiar master data types. The data in these InfoObjects can be moved to the inbound table using a tool such as Data Services or via SAP Cloud Platform Integration (CPI) by PUSH.
See [InfoObject with Write Interface](https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_BW_BRIDGE/107a6e8a38b74ede94c833ca3b7b6f51/18a38e808ce7438eb72700dd9f02d5d4.html?version=latest) in the SAP BW bridge documentation.
590833576.title: InfoObject With Write Interface

590833577.text:
If personal data has been locked or deleted in an application system, it can still be useful for reporting purposes to eliminate the personal data while not deleting the data records completely. You can now use anonymization rules to define how the individual fields are changed if you want a data record to be anonymized.
Anonymization rules are part of the InfoProvider’s metadata and can be edited in the BW Modeling tools in the standard InfoProvider editor. With SAP BW∕4HANA 2021 SPS04, you can define anonymization rules for DataStore objects. The anonymization rules can be created with a selected SQL syntax as formulas.
If you have defined anonymization rules, the Anonymization action is available in the Data Protection Workbench. As part of this action, the data records are changed in accordance with the anonymization rules.
See:
- [Settings for BW Modeling Tools](https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_BW_BRIDGE/107a6e8a38b74ede94c833ca3b7b6f51/3e09128a1e56437a9171f15bb8df87e6.html?version=latest)
- [Define Anonymization Rules](https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_BW_BRIDGE/107a6e8a38b74ede94c833ca3b7b6f51/cda8e5c422e345d1b4c39d79734f536c.html?version=latest)
- [SQL Syntax for Anonymization Rules](https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_BW_BRIDGE/107a6e8a38b74ede94c833ca3b7b6f51/ca8bab950426465a8c136b6729d02566.html?version=latest)
- [Anonymizing Data Using the Data Protection Workbench](https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_BW_BRIDGE/107a6e8a38b74ede94c833ca3b7b6f51/214922c4dd93476394f961fde8ad97fc.html?version=latest)
in the SAP BW bridge documentation.
590833577.title: Anonymizing Data Using the Data Protection Workbench

590833578.text:
You can now structure the SAP BW Bridge cockpit user interface into spaces and pages. We thus deliver suitable spaces and pages for the business role templates that are required for the cockpit. Administrators can either use these spaces and pages or create own ones and then assign them to custom roles.
See [First Steps in the Cockpit](https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_BW_BRIDGE/107a6e8a38b74ede94c833ca3b7b6f51/4fb1a6d41b8247a0bf374e91c497fb21.html?version=latest) in the SAP BW bridge documentation.
590833578.title: Utilizing SAP Fiori Launchpad Spaces and Pages in the SAP BW Bridge Cockpit

590833579.text:
New features are available for the import of SAP BW bridge entities:
- For SAP BW bridge entities, the semantics is now considered, and dependent objects are also imported.
- During the import, the entities are now already shared to a chosen target space.
See [Importing Entities with Semantics from SAP BW∕4HANA or SAP BW Bridge](7bcd3218b4064b898ca367b47ff246e2.html).
590833579.title: Import of SAP BW Bridge Entities

590833580.text:
The SAP BW Bridge Cockpit offers process variant ADSOOLR in the Process Variant Editor - Edit Variant app. You can use this process variant to automatically remove overlapping requests from a DataStore object.
See [Process Variant ADSOOLR](https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_BW_BRIDGE/107a6e8a38b74ede94c833ca3b7b6f51/d32c096532114e23b7ccc1d293743c7e.html?locale=en-US) in the SAP BW bridge documentation.
590833580.title: Process Variant ADSOOLR in SAP BW Bridge Cockpit

590833581.text:
You can now filter by attribute name when selecting navigation attributes in a CompositeProvider.
See [Activating Navigation Attributes](https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_BW_BRIDGE/107a6e8a38b74ede94c833ca3b7b6f51/943825c209ca4cbfb18c86ac8bf9fc15.html?locale=en-US&version=latest) in the SAP BW bridge documentation.
590833581.title: CompositeProvider Usability Enhancement

590833582.text:
You can now import hierarchies from the SAP BW bridge system into SAP Data Warehouse Cloud. For every InfoObject with hierarchies, the system creates the required views: the hierarchy directory view, the hierarchy directory text view, and the hierarchy view.
See :
- [Importing Entities with Semantics from SAP BW∕4HANA or SAP BW Bridge](7bcd3218b4064b898ca367b47ff246e2.html)
- [Add a Hierarchy to a Dimension](218b7e6bd60846dda2f03b789b389cb0.html)
- [Hierarchy](https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_BW_BRIDGE/107a6e8a38b74ede94c833ca3b7b6f51/4a245e22b1160456e10000000a421937.html?version=latest) in the SAP BW bridge documentation
590833582.title: Importing Hierarchies

590833583.text:
In the import wizard, the description of the InfoAreas in the InfoArea tree is shown if the UI setting is set accordingly. For master data, the type is now displayed.
See [Importing Entities with Semantics from SAP BW∕4HANA or SAP BW Bridge](7bcd3218b4064b898ca367b47ff246e2.html).
590833583.title: UI Settings in Import Wizard

590833584.text:
Using remote conversion, you can now transfer data models with data from SAP BW systems to SAP BW bridge. The Transfer Cockpit supports you in migrating selected data models into an SAP BW bridge tenant and to perform a remote data transfer into that tenant.
As a prerequisite, you need to install the DMIS add-on your on-premise SAP BW or SAP BW∕4HANA system.
590833584.title: Remote Conversion

590833585.text:
In the BW Modeling Tools, you can now activate multiple objects at once without requiring individual activation steps and sequences. The following objects are supported:
- InfoObjects
- DataStore objects
- CompositeProviders
- Transformations
- Data transfer processes
590833585.title: Mass activation of objects in BW Modelling Tools

590833586.text:
You can now implement your own simplified process type. This enable you to execute your own ABAP code using a process chain.
See [Execute Customer Process](https://help.sap.com/viewer/107a6e8a38b74ede94c833ca3b7b6f51/latest/en-US/28d42e503f9b4472a8052da75412f6d4.html).
590833586.title: Custom process type in process chains

590833587.text:
You can now schedule and unschedule process chains.
See [Scheduling or Unscheduling](https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_BW_BRIDGE/107a6e8a38b74ede94c833ca3b7b6f51/d430a3fa15324145821f0a7554a0ce75.html?locale=en-US&version=latest).
590833587.title: Scheduling of process chains

590833588.text:
For SAP BW bridge, there is now a troubleshooting guide available. It explains how to identify configuration issues in the connectivity of on-premise source systems to SAP BW bridge.
See [Troubleshooting](21ab1e7bfece4d22a3e58c296abd4340.html).
590833588.title: Troubleshooting Guide

590833589.text:
You can now manually upload currencies, units and fiscal year variants from another SAP system to your SAP BW bridge system.
See [Transferring Global Settings for Currencies, Measures and Fiscal Year Variants from an SAP System](https://help.sap.com/viewer/107a6e8a38b74ede94c833ca3b7b6f51/latest/en-US/4a27adea81661d10e10000000a42189b.html).
590833589.title: Transferring Currencies, Units, and Fiscal Year Variants

590833590.text:
You can now manually upload exchange rates for currencies from another SAP system to your SAP BW bridge system.
See [Transferring Exchange Rates for Currencies from SAP Systems](https://help.sap.com/viewer/107a6e8a38b74ede94c833ca3b7b6f51/latest/en-US/4a27a96a81661d10e10000000a42189b.html).
590833590.title: Uploading Exchange Rates for Currencies

590833591.text: You can now use an OAuth client with a Technical User purpose to manage TLS server certificates and connections using the command line interface. See [Manage Connectivity via the Command Line](3918242966c74f11858db39c8e5228e4.html).
590833591.title: Use OAuth Clients with Specific Privileges and Permissions to Manage Connectivity via the Command Line

590833592.text: You can now use an OAuth client with a Technical User purpose to manage modeling objects using the command line interface. See [Managing Modeling Objects via the Command Line](e3b2cbef9d1f4b38b51c64fe9e88c0aa.html).
590833592.title: Use OAuth Clients with Specific Privileges and Permissions to Manage Modeling Objects via the Command Line

590833593.text: When deleting task logs, you will also delete Apache Spark task logs. Deleting task logs can reduce storage consumption, but the storage level will not go down to zero because some files remain. Running procedures may take longer and incur costs after task log deletion. See [Delete Task Logs to Reduce Storage Consumption](c6902024ecd74956b4ba2d1c67ccb073.html).
590833593.title: Apache Spark Task Logs Included in Task Log Deletion Node

590833594.text: When an elastic compute node is starting or stopping, you can now cancel the process. The data is rolled back and restored to the state that existed before the start or stop process was initially triggered.See [Run an Elastic Compute Node](34b35852f2ff4888bda6b17e08f73ce3.html).
590833594.title: Cancel the Start or Stop Process of an Elastic Compute Node

590833595.text: You can now use OAuth clients with the Technical User purpose to manage tasks via the command line interface based on the roles and spaces you assign to the client. See [Running and Managing Tasks via the Command Line](2b26a31f197444dea314495bc0008eae.html).
590833595.title: OAuth Clients with Technical User Purpose to Manage Tasks via the Command Line

590833596.text:
SAP Datasphere is now integrated into SAP Cloud ALM for job and automation monitoring, which enables you to monitor the tasks run or scheduled in one or more SAP Datasphere tenants from the Job & Automation Monitoring app in SAP Cloud ALM. See [Job & Automation Monitoring](https://help.sap.com/docs/cloud-alm/applicationhelp/job-automation-monitoring) in the SAP Cloud ALM - Application Help.To monitor the tasks in the Job & Automation Monitoring app, you need to enable the feature for your SAP Datasphere tenant as it is disabled by default. See [Configuration](https://help.sap.com/docs/cloud-alm/applicationhelp/configuring-job-monitoring) in the SAP Cloud ALM - Application Help.
Note
As the technical names of SAP Datasphere tasks can be displayed in SAP Cloud ALM, we recommend that you do not include any sensitive business or personal data in them. See [Rules for Technical Names](982f9a30d4ab49c8b019cfaf3dc08391.html).
590833596.title: SAP Datasphere Integrated into SAP Cloud ALM for Job & Automation Monitoring

590833597.text:
Before this version, you could choose between these methods to authenticate to your SAP Datasphere tenant: the default identity provider or your custom identity provider.You can now choose between the following methods:
- For existing tenants: the default identity provider, your custom identity provider (legacy) or the new bundled SAP Cloud Identity Services tenants.
- For new tenants: the default identity provider or the new bundled SAP Cloud Identity Services tenants.
Using bundled SAP Cloud Identity Services tenants allows users to sign in to your SAP Datasphere tenant and to other SAP products via single sign-on (SSO). If you currently use a custom identity provider, we recommend that you migrate to an SAP Cloud Identity Services tenant and configure the tenant to work with your custom identity provider.
See [Managing User Identity and Authentication](48b5c8b637a54fa491594272941855b9.html).
590833597.title: Managing User Identity and Authentication with Bundled SAP Cloud Identity Services Tenants

590833598.text: Use the Enable SAP HANA Multi-Availability Zones option on the Tenant Configuration page to create a synchronous replica of the main system on a system in a different availability zone in the same region. The synchronous replica system has a high-availability setup that can take over processing when necessary. For more information, see [Configure the Size of Your SAP Datasphere Tenant](33f8ef4ec359409fb75925a68c23ebc3.html) and [Creating and Configuring Your SAP Datasphere Tenant](2f80b57359254b5cbb4faac794ade90c.html).
590833598.title: Enable Multi-Availability Zones for SAP HANA Cloud

590833599.text: New monitoring abilities are available for storage consumption in file spaces and usage of Apache Spark application with the Object Store tab. This allows you to understand where storage consumption is the highest in file spaces (or SAP HANA Data Lake Files) and usage of Apache Spark application when running tasks. For more information, see [Monitoring SAP Datasphere](d39b8652994846f9ab80b32fc5b4d671.html)
590833599.title: Monitor the Storage Consumption for SAP HANA Data Lake Files (Apache Spark)

590833600.text:
Administrators can now create the mapping between their SAP Datasphere tenant and their SAP Business Technology Platform account to enable SAP HANA for SQL data warehousing themselves, rather than needing to raise a ticket.
For more information, see [Enable SAP HANA for SQL Data Warehousing on Your SAP Datasphere Tenant](e9a287849ccf41bb8a132d12dd3fdc8f.html).
590833600.title: Self-Service Enabling of SAP HANA for SQL data warehousing on Your SAP Datasphere Tenant

590833601.text: You can now specify the number of API requests separately when configuring object storage.Previously, API calls were bundled under the general Storage option. With the new Requests option, you can define the expected number of API calls per month, giving you more control and accuracy in estimating your object storage needs. See [Configure the Size of Your SAP Datasphere Tenant](33f8ef4ec359409fb75925a68c23ebc3.html).
590833601.title: Object Store Requests License

590833602.text: You can now enable tables from HDI containers and Open SQL Schemas to be replicated to elastic compute nodes.See [Create an Elastic Compute Node](99ad61e1b63a44de8572a49c6f374e8a.html), [Allow the Space to Access the Open SQL Schema](7eaa370fe4624dea9f182ee9c9ab645f.html) and [Prepare Your HDI Project for Exchanging Data with Your Space](a94e1637db484a5c8ec2da83cfa75156.html).
590833602.title: HDI Container and Open SQL Schema Tables Replicated in Elastic Compute Nodes

590833603.text:
You can now create an OAuth client with the new Technical User purpose and assign a global or scoped role to limit its privileges and permissions.Initially, the use of an OAuth client with a Technical User purpose is limited to the following workflows:
- To use the SCIM 2.0 API (see [Managing Users via the SCIM 2.0 API](1ca8c4a9467f43df9ae6d4ed3734f05a.html)).
- To transport content (see [Transporting Content Through SAP Cloud Transport Management](05383980f0704c71ab9872360ce45622.html) and [api/v1/content](https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_ANALYTICS_CLOUD/14cac91febef464dbb1efce20e3f1613/eeace13cc37b4eed96064a7c5d8ee493.html) in the SAP Analytics Cloud REST API Guide).
- To export a log of user activities to a CSV file (see [api/v1/audit/activities/exportActivities](https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_ANALYTICS_CLOUD/14cac91febef464dbb1efce20e3f1613/ca45363ac1de4d669ad4a18115401d5a.html) in the SAP Analytics Cloud REST API Guide).
- To use the datasphere command line interface (marketplace commands only) (see [Accessing SAP Datasphere via the Command Line](3f9a42ccde6b4b6aba121e2aab79c36d.html)).
- To allow SAP Signavio to connect securely to SAP systems such as SAP S/4HANA (see [SAP Signavio Connections](4c367de075a44ad7b7a6db576a4a9c82.html).)
See [Create an OAuth2.0 Client with a Technical User Purpose](88b13468fc3c4ebd972bcb8faa6cafbf.html).
590833603.title: OAuth Clients with Specific Privileges and Permissions

590833604.text: Expensive statements are now automatically traced for new tenants or tenants that had never enabled this option. You can analyze individual SQL queries whose execution exceeds one or more thresholds with the default settings or set your own. See [Configure Monitoring](9cd0691c44a74f2aa47b52f615f74433.html).
590833604.title: System Monitoring: Tracing Expensive Statements

590833605.text: Manage your IP allowlist by importing or exporting your allowlist to the same or a different SAP Datasphere tenant. See [Manage IP Allowlist](a3c214514ef94e899459f68f4c1e2a23.html).
590833605.title: Import or Export IP Allowlist

590833606.text: Audit logs can consume a large quantity of your tenant's disk storage. Until now, audit log entries for database analysis users were kept for 180 days, after which they were automatically deleted. Starting with this version, you can manually delete these audit logs to free up disk storage at any time.Also, database analysis users are now automatically deactivated when their audit logs consume more than a certain threshold of disk storage. Deleting their audit logs will automatically reactivate them.
590833606.title: Delete Audit Logs Generated for Database Analysis Users to Free Up Disk Storage

590833607.text: You can now cancel task runs with the Cancel Task button. Cancelling a task run may be required when it takes too long or if the run impacts negatively other runs by taking too many resources away. See [Monitoring SAP Datasphere](d39b8652994846f9ab80b32fc5b4d671.html).
590833607.title: System Monitor: Cancelling Task Runs

590833608.text:
You can now list, upload, and delete TLS server certificates via the command line or via the REST API.See :
- [Managing TLS Server Certificates via the Command Line](6306da2bbeb04e4fbd944c2dce08629f.html)
590833608.title: Manage Certificates via the Command Line or via REST API

590833609.text: You can now copy a space along with all its Data Builder objects and connections to create a new space in your tenant.See [Copy Spaces and their Contents](73068ac8e1934615b419d8c6c4095a9a.html).
590833609.title: Copy a Space and its Contents

590833610.text: You can upgrade your SAP HANA database patch version via the System   About dialog.See [Apply a Patch Upgrade to Your SAP HANA Database](489dc3b4ba4040b79bd97a1ca236c004.html).
590833610.title: Apply a Patch Release to SAP HANA Database

590833611.text: To improve performance when viewing the data on the Tasks and Statements tabs of the System Monitor, you can now filter by the start date of the tasks and statements. You can use  (Columns Settings) show or hide the Start Date column.See [Monitoring SAP Datasphere](d39b8652994846f9ab80b32fc5b4d671.html).
590833611.title: Start Date Column for Filtering Tasks and Statements Logs

590833612.text: SAP Datasphere is now integrated into SAP Cloud ALM for health monitoring, which enables you to check the health of one or more SAP Datasphere tenants from the Health Monitoring app in SAP Cloud ALM.See [Health Monitoring](https://help.sap.com/docs/cloud-alm/applicationhelp/health-monitoring) in the SAP Cloud ALM - Application Help.
590833612.title: SAP Datasphere Integrated into SAP Cloud ALM for Health Monitoring

590833613.text: Before this version, one tab was automatically created in the System Monitor for each elastic compute node. You can now go in the new tab “Elastic Compute Nodes” and select the elastic compute node that you want to monitor. See [Monitoring SAP Datasphere](d39b8652994846f9ab80b32fc5b4d671.html).
590833613.title: Improved User Experience for Monitoring Elastic Compute Nodes

590833614.text: The new global role DW AI Consumer enables the users assigned to it to use SAP Business AI features, when activated in your SAP Datasphere tenant on the new Configuration  AI Services tab.See [Standard Roles Delivered with SAP Datasphere](a50a51d80d5746c9b805a2aacbb7e4ee.html) and [Enable SAP Business AI for SAP Datasphere](1b3fe45f38df4db1a9cda97a5a7bcdaf.html).
590833614.title: New DW AI Consumer Role

590833615.text: If you have allowed SAP Product support to generate support users based on incidents, the support engineer can now request a support user with an extended global viewer role along with a scoped viewer role which has the spaces required to analyze the incident assigned as scopes. See [Request Help from SAP Technical Support](831a97714dfe4301918afece5a3b380b.html).
590833615.title: Support User with DW Support User and DW Scoped Support User Role

590833616.text: If you're using SAP Datasphere on Microsoft Azure and want to connect to a firewall-protected Microsoft Azure storage account, such as Microsoft Azure Data Lake Store Gen2, within the same Azure region, an Azure administrator must allow the SAP Datasphere's Virtual Network Subnet ID in the Microsoft Azure storage account. You can now find this ID in the SAP Datasphere Dialog About dialog. See [Obtain SAP Datasphere IP addresses For Allowlisting in Remote Systems](0934f7ed9a534e638299f53ab60866ae.html).
590833616.title: For Microsoft Azure Deployments: Virtual Network Subnet ID in About

590833617.text: The Tenant Links tab for linking your SAP Datasphere tenant to an SAP Analytics Cloud Dialog tenant is now available in the Administration app.See [Review and Manage Links to SAP Analytics Cloud and SAP Business Data Cloud Tenants](40db56764bff4f9ab7eace16ac8e7e67.html).
590833617.title: Tenant Linking Now in Administration App

590833618.text: When creating live data tunnel connections on the Data Integration tab of the Configuration tool, the user interface is reduced to the required functions and source system selection. On the Data Source Configuration tab of the Administration tool, when adding or editing a location, you can only see the required options.
590833618.title: Improved User Experience for Managing Tunnel Connections and Location IDs

590833619.text: You can now create, read, update, and delete users and add them to roles via the SCIM 2.0 API.See [Managing Users via the SCIM 2.0 API](1ca8c4a9467f43df9ae6d4ed3734f05a.html).
590833619.title: Create Users and Assign Them to Roles via the SCIM 2.0 API

590833620.text:
The following enhancements are now available:
- New datasphere global-roles commands allow you to list global roles and to add and remove users.
- Role names can now be provided in all relevant commands without a technical prefix.
- The following commands have been harmonized with the interface:
- scoped-roles scopes add replaces scoped-roles scopes assign
- scoped-roles scopes removereplaces scoped-roles scopes unassign
- scoped-roles users add replaces scoped-roles users assign
- scoped-roles users remove replaces scoped-roles users unassign
- The JSON formats for adding and removing users to and from roles and adding roles to users are simplified.
- The JSON format for creating and updating scoped roles now accepts inheritance of the role template as a string.
Note
The assign and unassign commands and old JSON formats are deprecated and will be removed in a future release.
See [Manage Users and Roles via the Command Line](3a3d0ef3d4954797acac12afbcf9ab5d.html).
590833620.title: Command Line Enhancements for Global and Scoped Roles

590833621.text: In Tenant Configuration, you can now reduce the amount of memory allocated to your tenant. See [Configure the Size of Your SAP Datasphere Tenant](33f8ef4ec359409fb75925a68c23ebc3.html).
590833621.title: Downsize Tenant Memory

590833622.text: You can now disable the welcome email from being sent to new users added to your tenant. See [Configure Notifications](4388411066ef476aa99e4f35ce64bab6.html).
590833622.title: Manage Welcome Email Notification

590833623.text:
For resilience purposes, we are now limiting the maximum CPU resources for workload generated by spaces, user group users and agent users to 80%. The remaining 20% of CPU resources are reserved to ensure that the system can respond under heavy load.
You can now configure the total amount of threads that each space can consume up to a maximum of 100% of this 80% of the threads available in your tenant.
Also, statements are now queued when the CPU usage reaches 90% (instead of 80%) of the database capacity. This value, which you cannot change, applies to all spaces, including spaces created before this version.
See [Set Priorities and Statement Limits for Spaces or Groups](d66ac1efb5054068a104c4559b72d272.html).
590833623.title: Improved Resiliency

590833624.text: In Tenant Configuration, you may now increase the size of data lake storage in increments of 1 TB instead of 5 TB.See [Configure the Size of Your SAP Datasphere Tenant](33f8ef4ec359409fb75925a68c23ebc3.html) .
590833624.title: Modify Data Lake Storage in Increments of 1 TB

590833625.text: You can now assign yourself to a scoped role.See [Create a Scoped Role to Assign Privileges to Users in Spaces](b5c4e0b6c462414783ebbfc053815521.html), [Assign Users to a Role](57a78804d8bd48ca9e7e73a0d33e355f.html) and [Control User Access to Your Space](9d59fe511ae644d98384897443054c16.html).
590833625.title: Assign Yourself to a Scoped Role

590833626.text: You can now control the duration of the token and refresh token lifetimes for your OAuth clients.See [Create OAuth2.0 Clients to Authenticate Against SAP Datasphere](3f92b46fe0314e8ba60720e409c219fc.html)
590833626.title: Control OAuth Client Token Lifetimes

590833627.text:
Users with the DW Administrator global role can use the new Authorization Overview page to see all the users, roles, and spaces in the tenant and how they relate to each other. You can filter by user, role, or space to see, for example, which users are assigned with which roles to a particular space.
See [View Authorizations by User, Role, or Space](c6538ea2db884e599072e62bdb03e68c.html).
