590833627.title: New Authorization Overview page

590833628.text:
The new monitoring view SPACE_USERS_V_EXT is deployed in the DWC_GLOBAL schema and tracks information about the user types.
See [Working with SAP HANA Monitoring Views](4ab45090c5684ebf8765757a1dfc4e5d.html).
590833628.title: New Monitoring View SPACE_USERS_V_EXT

590833629.text: You man now enable the SAP HANA Cloud script server in the Tenant Configuration page. See [Configure the Size of Your SAP Datasphere Tenant](33f8ef4ec359409fb75925a68c23ebc3.html).
590833629.title: Enable the SAP HANA Cloud Script Server

590833630.text: When scheduling a new task in the Data Integration Monitor, users now receive a message reminding them to renew their consent if their current consent authorization will expire within the next four weeks. In addition, administrators can view a list of users whose authorization consent will expire within the next four weeks.See [Changing SAP Datasphere Settings](1084796d09464e78870f32cab8584dfc.html) and [Check Consent Expirations](58e4bb2717b1445bba9e1f3d214f5181.html).
590833630.title: Authorized Consent Expiration

590833631.text:
You can now manage users and scoped roles from the command line using the following commands:
- datasphere users - See [Managing Users via the Command Line](72dc33a8f41944f78318138bc1a57307.html).
- datasphere spaces users - see [Managing Space Users via the Command Line](f58c71c028b149088903193b4e1f06da.html).
- datasphere scoped-roles - See [Managing Scoped Roles via the Command Line](85085a35a58a4589bc121fb94efc4876.html).
590833631.title: Manage Users and Scoped Roles via the Command Line

590833632.text: To better understand your IP entries in the Trusted IPs and Trusted Cloud Connector IPs allowlists in  System     Configuration, you can now add a description for each IP entry.See: [Manage IP Allowlist](a3c214514ef94e899459f68f4c1e2a23.html)
590833632.title: Descriptions for Entries in IP Allowlists

590833633.text: The information about the SAP HANA multi-dimensional services (MDS) version is removed from the More section of the  System    About dialog. The information about the Database Release now also applies to the MDS version.
590833633.title: MDS Version Removed from About Dialog

590833634.text:
If you have allowed SAP Product support to generate support users based on incidents, the process of requesting and generating a personalized support user now supports creating the support user with the DW Administrator role.
See [Request Help from SAP Technical Support](831a97714dfe4301918afece5a3b380b.html).
590833634.title: Support User with DW Administrator Role

590833635.text: The monitoring view TASK_LOGS_V_EXT now tracks resource consumption key figures, and collect task chains information.See [Working with SAP HANA Monitoring Views](4ab45090c5684ebf8765757a1dfc4e5d.html)
590833635.title: Enhancement of Monitoring View TASK_LOGS_V_EXT

590833636.text:
To prevent overloading the SAP HANA database, the parameter ADMISSION CONTROL REJECT CPU THRESHOLD is now part of the default configuration (in the Workload Configuration area of a space) with a threshold value set to 99%.
Note
This parameter cannot be changed, and its threshold value applies to all spaces – including spaces created before this version.
See [Set Priorities and Statement Limits for Spaces or Groups](d66ac1efb5054068a104c4559b72d272.html).
590833636.title: Prevent Overloading the Database - Admission Control Rejection Threshold Enabled

590833637.text:
If you’re using a tenant in regions EU10 and US10 for the hyperscaler Amazon Web Services (AWS), you can now choose a larger memory size for your tenant.
See [Configure the Size of Your SAP Datasphere Tenant](33f8ef4ec359409fb75925a68c23ebc3.html).
590833637.title: Larger Configuration Available for Your Tenant in Certain Regions

590833638.text:
Two new roles added for the catalog:
- Catalog Administrator: Allows users set up and implement the catalog in SAP Datasphere.
- Catalog User: Allows users (for example, data modelers) to look for assets and allows users to view it in full or use as part of a data project to build something new.
See [Standard Roles Delivered with SAP Datasphere](a50a51d80d5746c9b805a2aacbb7e4ee.html).
590833638.title: New Catalog Administrator and Catalog User Roles

590833639.text:
Your tenant configuration now includes blocks designated for Data Integration applications, as well as Catalog assets, activities and metadata. The size of the Data Integration and Catalog blocks cannot be modified.
See [Configure the Size of Your SAP Datasphere Tenant](33f8ef4ec359409fb75925a68c23ebc3.html).
590833639.title: Tenant Configuration Page Includes Data Integration and Catalog Blocks

590833640.text:
When you purchase a subscription-based tenant for testing purposes, you can now allocate the capacity units to the storage and compute resources to obtain a configuration that fits your needs, just like for a productive tenant. Note that the minimal configuration provided for SAP Data Warehouse Cloud resources for a test tenant is: 128 GB of storage and 1 compute block.
See [Configure the Size of Your SAP Datasphere Tenant](33f8ef4ec359409fb75925a68c23ebc3.html)
590833640.title: Configuring the Size of Your Test Tenant

590833641.text:
You can now add up to 250 entries in the IP allowlist.
See [Manage IP Allowlist](a3c214514ef94e899459f68f4c1e2a23.html).
590833641.title: Increased Maximum Number of Entries in IP Allowlist

590833642.text:
If you've signed the Cloud Platform Enterprise Agreement (CPEA), you can now directly create SAP Data Warehouse Cloud service instances (tenants) in SAP BTP.
See [Creating and Configuring Your SAP Datasphere Tenant](2f80b57359254b5cbb4faac794ade90c.html).
590833642.title: Creating an SAP Data Warehouse Cloud Service Instance in SAP BTP

590833643.text:
The new System Monitor tool allows administrators to monitor the performance of their system and identify storage, task, out-of-memory, and other issues across all spaces. For example, you can see:
- All the errors (such as failed tasks and out-of-memory errors) that occurred yesterday.
- The top five statements with the highest peak memory consumption.
- An overview of all tasks across spaces.
See [Monitoring SAP Datasphere](d39b8652994846f9ab80b32fc5b4d671.html).
590833643.title: New Cross-Space System Monitor Tool

590833644.text:
With the first login after your tenant has been updated to version 2022.10, we'll perform some maintenance activity for your uploaded third-party ODBC drivers. Your existing connections and data flows won't be affected by this activity. In the exceptional case of an issue, you can re-upload the required drivers.
See [Upload Third-Party ODBC Drivers (Required for Data Flows)](b9b5579054df48c39381d5b17286bf21.html).
590833644.title: Maintenance Activity for Uploaded Drivers

590833645.text:
If you haven’t yet allocated all your capacity units or if you’ve acquired additional capacity units, you can allocate them and increase the sizes of your SAP HANA storage and compute, data lake, and (if no size has yet been allocated) SAP BW Bridge.
See [Configure the Size of Your SAP Datasphere Tenant](33f8ef4ec359409fb75925a68c23ebc3.html).
590833645.title: Increase the Size of Your Tenant

590833646.text:
The new DW Consumer role allows users to consume data from spaces of which they are members, but does not allow them to log onto SAP Data Warehouse Cloud.
This role is intended for business analysts and other users whose only point of contact with SAP Data Warehouse Cloud is using views that are exposed for consumption as sources in SAP Analytics Cloud and other analytics clients.
See [Standard Roles Delivered with SAP Datasphere](a50a51d80d5746c9b805a2aacbb7e4ee.html).
590833646.title: New DW Consumer Role

590833647.text:
When you log into your new SAP Data Warehouse Cloud tenant for the first time, you need to allocate the capacity units to the storage and compute resources to obtain a configuration that fits your exact needs. You do this in a dedicated page of SAP Data Warehouse Cloud.
See [Configure the Size of Your SAP Datasphere Tenant](33f8ef4ec359409fb75925a68c23ebc3.html).
590833647.title: Configure the Size of Your New Tenant

590833648.text:
Deleting old task logs that are no longer needed can be useful to release storage space. This is why SAP Data Warehouse Cloud has now a log deletion schedule activated by default. You can change this schedule defining your own criteria or decide to take immediate deletion actions.
See [Delete Task Logs to Reduce Storage Consumption](c6902024ecd74956b4ba2d1c67ccb073.html).
590833648.title: Scheduled automatic Task Logs Deletion

590833649.text:
A new version of the dwc command line interface is released with various technical improvements. To update to the latest version, run npm install -g @sap/dwc-cli
See [Install or Update the SAP Datasphere Command Line Interface](f7d5eddf20a34a1aa48d8e2c68a44e28.html).
590833649.title: <samp class="ph codeph">dwc</samp> Command Line Interface Update

590833650.text:
Organizations transition to use SAP Business Data Cloud by rewiring their standalone SAP Datasphere and SAP Analytics Cloud systems to SAP Business Data Cloud. Once the SAP Datasphere system is added to an SAP Business Data Cloud formation, the migration of catalog content automatically starts.
If you had previously rewired your systems before this feature was available, you can still migrate the catalog content from the previous setup to the newer setup. Note
During the catalog migration, personal data in the form of user favorites will also be migrated.
See [Migrating Catalog Content to SAP Business Data Cloud](b26705d20f4f4ebba77175276127b48f.html).
590833650.title: Migrate Catalog Content from a Standalone SAP Datasphere Setup to an Integrated Setup with SAP Business Data Cloud

590833651.text:
If entities in a data product are associated with entities in one or more other data products, those associations will only be visible if the related data products are installed.
See [Requesting Access to Data Products](ea7cb802cbea47b39a441888873c3a49.html).
590833651.title: Cross-Data Product Associations

590833652.text:
As users discover data products in the catalog, they can get more information about objects for a data product's API from the data product details page. This additional information will help users better understand a data product before they install it to a SAP Datasphere space or share it to a target system.
See [Data Product Details](71f4d1599dba4aa59e6682a314650cf7.html).
590833652.title: Information about Objects for a Data Product's API is Available

590833653.text:
Enhanced monitoring of metadata extraction for data products helps users with the Catalog Administrator role ensure that the content in the catalog is reliable.
- Metadata extraction errors are detected early and are more visible in the extraction summary logs and on the data product details page.
- Source systems that have data products or APIs with extraction issues are automatically resynchronized with the catalog to update the data products.
- Manually synchronizing source systems will also update data products that have errors.
Catalog users won't be able to install data products that have outdated APIs.
See [Requesting Access to Data Products](ea7cb802cbea47b39a441888873c3a49.html).
590833653.title: Improved Metadata Extraction Monitoring for Data Products

590833654.text: When viewing the Impact & Lineage Analysis Diagram for an object, the container that represents the source system will show a user-friendly business or technical name that is extracted from the source system. Containers for systems not connected to the catalog show the system type and the word "unmonitored".
590833654.title: Display User-Friendly System Name in Impact & Lineage Analysis Diagram

590833655.text:
Data subscriptions (DSUB) created from the Data Product Generator for SAP Business Data Cloud are available in the catalog. These objects are created in SAP BW∕4HANA systems. With data subscriptions, SAP BW data is pushed to SAP Datasphere local tables (see [Publishing Data to SAP Datasphere](https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_BW4HANA/107a6e8a38b74ede94c833ca3b7b6f51/694a1f45e3174756abc6f06ee7d901d3.html) in the SAP BW∕4HANA help documentation).
On the data subscriptions details page, you’ll be able to see its subscription properties and open a link to the target SAP Datasphere local table, where you can further analyze the object by viewing the Impact and Lineage Analysis diagram. Note
To be able to see the DSUB objects in the catalog, implement SAP Note [3601550](https://me.sap.com/notes/3601550) into your systems and make sure you're on SAP BW∕4HANA 2023 SPS04 or newer.
See [Connecting to BW Systems](b350d7c6e88c4f089d381dfe6feee792.html) and [Data Subscription (DSUB)](https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_BW4HANA/ed919380760a44388ab90e6bb3e7480a/5ad3c27c5f8640b39ba26a838cd93c1b.html).
590833655.title: Data Subscription (DSUB) Objects Available in the Assets Collection

590833656.text: After an application upgrade, source systems with detected changes are automatically synchronized with the catalog. Changes may include correcting metadata inaccuracies or resolving errors and bugs within data products. These updates to data products and assets do not update the object’s version number.
590833656.title: Automatic Synchronization after Application Upgrade

590833657.text:
Data products created in the data sharing cockpit with Delta Sharing output port are available in the Data Products collection. This enhancement unifies how catalog users search for and access data products in the catalog.
Delta Share data products are created by data providers that have a profile with the Marketplace Visibility option set to Formations (see [Creating Data Products for SAP Business Data Cloud](b07e95d07a1e4569b87d9bb57b732bcf.html)).
SAP Datasphere systems can now be a source system for both assets and data products. To help users find systems on the Metadata Extractions, the source systems are organized into groups based on the objects extracted: assets only, APIs only, and both assets and APIs (see [Connecting Source Systems](0b5de87f256f466f95b46d4bcaa52640.html)).
590833657.title: Delta Share Data Products Available in the Data Products Collection

590833658.text:
If you have terms or key performance indicators in other applications, you can import them into the catalog via a Microsoft Excel spreadsheet. See these topics:
- [Import Glossary Terms](694ecb26f72e4d0ca8b8f64434da881f.html)
- [View Details About Glossary Term Import](9395b3a445e44ceabf3e0e7ed3bba373.html)
- [Import Key Performance Indicators](adc41e274a344172a7ebecf8350e6d3a.html)
- [View Details About Key Performance Indicator Import](07a5c28b138741f0a86d12f99579932f.html)
590833658.title: Import Terms and Key Performance Indicators

590833659.text:
When viewing the Impact and Lineage Analysis diagram for an SAP Analytics Cloud insight, users will be able to see models from the local SAP Datasphere system in the insight's lineage.Note
For insights saved prior to this update, follow these steps to ensure that the lineage appears as expected.
- In SAP Analytics Cloud, open the insight and save it.
- Wait a few minutes as the catalog extracts the object's metadata and updates the associated asset.
- On the catalog search page, search for the insight and view its details page.
- Select Open Lineage and Impact to see the diagram.
See [Catalog Asset Details](afccc581146542c485a52563167e23cc.html).
590833659.title: SAP Datasphere Models Included in the Impact and Lineage Analysis Diagram for an SAP Analytics Cloud Insight

590833660.text:
The following usability improvements will help users with the appropriate permissions manage assets, terms, and key performance indicators (KPIs) and monitor source systems.
- Updated pages for creating and managing glossary terms and KPIs
- Addition of visual cues for areas where AI-generated content is used for enriching content
- Updated avatar and colors for all objects in the grid view on the catalog search page
- Updated source property groupings for metadata on the asset details page
- Renamed the main monitoring page to Metadata Extractions to match the side navigation
- Renamed the systems table on the Metadata Extractions page to Remote Systems, plus these other updates:
- Reorganized the information so that it's easier to find and understand
- Moved system-specific actions from the toolbar to the system's row (for example, Configure is available only for SAP BW systems)
- Updated the system's details page by adding a toolbar to the header section, which means users can perform actions on the system without having to go back to the main monitoring page (for example, manually synchronizing a system) and reorganizing information in the header section so that it's easier to find and understand
See the following topics:
- [Using Key Performance Indicators](3550f14d4cd74dfaa63ebcaa25b288c2.html)
- [Create and Manage Key Performance Indicators](ca4f04da3afa4f82b85a0835fceb444b.html)
- [Define the Key Performance Indicator Template](b3ead0d4944c40ddbdb1ebae239cc69f.html)
- [Create and Manage a Glossary](e40310c9781848bfad031cce7792f394.html)
- [Create and Manage Glossary Terms](193336a4eba94c978c08fd2cee625a3e.html)
- [Catalog Asset Details](afccc581146542c485a52563167e23cc.html)
- [Connecting Source Systems](0b5de87f256f466f95b46d4bcaa52640.html)
590833660.title: Usability Improvements to Enhance Your Catalog Experience

590833661.text:
The share status for data products will be monitored for changes on the target system every 24 hours and updated in the catalog as needed:
- If the data product share is deleted from the target system, the data product's share status is updated to Shareable.
- If the data product's current share status is In progress for longer than one hour, but the data product was not shared to the target system, the share status is updated to Shareable.
- If the data product's current share status is In progress for longer than one hour, and the data product has been shared to the target system, the share status is updated to Shared.
590833661.title: Improved Share Status Monitoring for Data Products Shared to Target Systems

590833662.text:
When viewing the Impact and Lineage Analysis diagram for an SAP Analytics Cloud story that is based on a live data model, users will be able to see BW Query (ELEM) objects from SAP BW∕4HANA in the story's lineage.
See [Catalog Asset Details](afccc581146542c485a52563167e23cc.html).
590833662.title: BW Query Objects (ELEM) from SAP BW∕4HANA Included in the Impact and Lineage Analysis Diagram for an SAP Analytics Cloud Story

590833663.text: When viewing the Impact and Lineage Analysis diagram for a data product that is from an SAP Datasphere source system, users will be able to see tables from the local SAP Datasphere system in the data product's lineage.
590833663.title: SAP Datasphere Tables Included in the Impact and Lineage Analysis Diagram for a Data Product

590833664.text:
You can now connect SAP BW∕4HANA systems to the catalog and the following objects will be included in the catalog:
- ADSO (Advanced DataStore Object)
- ALVL (Aggregation Level)
- AREA (InfoArea)
- Data Transfer Process (DTPA)
- DEST (Open Hub Destination)
- ELEM (BW Query)
- FBPA (Open ODS View)
- HCPR (Composite Provider)
- IOBJ (InfoObject)
- LSYS (Source System)
- RSDS (DataSource)
- TRCS (InfoSource)
- TRFN (Transformation)
Catalog administrators will be able to enrich these object types with term, KPI, and tag relationships and then publish them for easy discovery by catalog users.
See [Connecting to BW Systems](b350d7c6e88c4f089d381dfe6feee792.html).
590833664.title: Ability to Connect SAP BW∕4HANA Systems to the Catalog

590833665.text:
The ability to share data products to target systems is no longer available when users access the catalog from SAP Datasphere. Sharing data products to target systems will only be available when users access the catalog from SAP Business Data Cloud.
See [Sharing Data Products to Target Systems](https://help.sap.com/docs/business-data-cloud/governing-and-publishing-data-in-catalog/sharing-data-products-to-sap-databricks).
590833665.title: Ability to Share Data Products Only in SAP Business Data Cloud

590833666.text: When installing a data product to your space, you can choose the appropriate data access method. See [Requesting Access to Data Products](ea7cb802cbea47b39a441888873c3a49.html).
590833666.title: Select Appropriate Data Access Method for Installed Data Products

590833667.text:
When reviewing the details page for a data product, users can open the Impact and Lineage Analysis diagram to see how the installed data product impacts SAP Datasphere objects.
See [Data Product Details](71f4d1599dba4aa59e6682a314650cf7.html).
590833667.title: Impact of Installed Data Products on SAP Datasphere Objects Included in the Impact and Lineage Analysis Diagram

590833668.text:
To ensure the extracted metadata for all SAP Datasphere, SAP BW bridge objects is up-to-date, you can create a synchronization schedule for the source system. See [Connecting to BW Systems](b350d7c6e88c4f089d381dfe6feee792.html).
In the catalog, users will be able to discover Data Transfer Process (DTPA) objects.
590833668.title: Improvements for SAP Datasphere, SAP BW bridge Systems

590833669.text:
When searching for data products in the catalog, the following collections have been renamed:
- The SAP Business Data Cloud Data Products collection is now Data Products
- The Marketplace Data Products collection is now Data Products (Marketplace)
590833669.title: Improved Experience when Working with Data Products

590833670.text:
Access to features and functionality for the catalog and data marketplace have been unified under a single access point in the side navigation. Users can select  (Catalog & Marketplace) to access the catalog:
- Search for and evaluate data and assets in the catalog (see [Discovering Data Products and Assets in the Catalog](6df42e3675324d73bd35c2e70d46a7ee.html))
- Manage their marketplace data products installations, activate licenses, and choose contexts they want to be a member of (see [Managing Marketplace Data Products](5d725beb848e432a91eb8de29875d7e2.html))
- Connect and manage source systems and monitor metadata extraction (see [Connecting Source Systems](0b5de87f256f466f95b46d4bcaa52640.html))
590833670.title: Unify the Side Navigation for Catalog and Data Marketplace

590833671.text:
When enriching catalog assets on the asset details page, use the SAP Business AI features for adding custom summary and custom long descriptions and assigning tag relationships.
See
- [Governing Catalog Assets](1218c12e72c34cfd96293e566badb60c.html)
- [Enriching and Managing Catalog Assets](7ed60a094f2a464da6a8d75e5bfed9d5.html)
- [Manage Hierarchies and Tags](0c167fa12afc47eeac9f018fe975b73f.html)
- [Manage Tag Relationships for Assets](bb608dd2a4dc402889351c4303a173a4.html)
590833671.title: Use SAP Business AI features to Enrich Catalog Assets

590833672.text:
When reviewing the details page for a marketplace data product, users can open the Impact and Lineage Analysis diagram. This enhancement allows data providers to easily access the diagram, where they can gain a better understanding of a data product.
See [Marketplace Data Product Details](f59e912bf1ee45cf90375fd86109b952.html).
590833672.title: Ability to Open the Impact and Lineage Analysis Diagram from Marketplace Data Products

590833673.text:
The lineage for marketplace data products are visible in the Impact and Lineage Analysis diagram.
If you know the assets that are impacted by or in the lineage of a certain data product, you can access the Impact and Lineage Analysis diagram from the assets details page. See [Catalog Asset Details](afccc581146542c485a52563167e23cc.html).
590833673.title: Marketplace Data Product Lineage Available in the Impact and Lineage Analysis Diagram

590833674.text:
If after an application upgrade the status for a source system becomes Outdated, the catalog administrator must run a manual synchronization.
See [Manually Synchronizing a System](48c11915d74b41fcb8c07dd4bf1c4c86.html).
590833674.title: Manually Synchronize Source System After Application Upgrade

590833675.text:
The layout of the pages for data marketplace data product details and data provider profiles has been updated so that the look and feel is harmonized to the catalog asset details pages. This improved layout provides visual consistency among all objects available in the catalog. Also, information about the data products and data providers is easier to find in the updated layout.
See [Installing Marketplace Data Products](92c35efd6a4945a1a78250539aee9a51.html) and [Reviewing Data Provider Profiles](9ce49dcb70df4065880342beec03e25e.html).
590833675.title: Improvements to the Data Marketplace Data Product Details and Data Providers Profile Pages

590833676.text:
Organizations don't need separate enrichment and publishing steps. They can choose to automatically publish objects from the source system to the catalog. When the catalog synchronizes with the source system, assets will be automatically published to the catalog where catalog users can discover them.
See [Publishing Content to the Catalog](f31d2d97afb0482a874acb0ec61465fe.html), [Connecting Source Systems](0b5de87f256f466f95b46d4bcaa52640.html), and [Manually Synchronizing a System](48c11915d74b41fcb8c07dd4bf1c4c86.html).
590833676.title: Automatically Publish Assets to the Catalog

590833677.text:
You can access additional third-party data products from various data providers on the Datarade website.
See [Searching for Data Products and Assets in the Catalog](09bc571a876f448bb526a33d1ad00c61.html)
590833677.title: Access third-party data from Datarade

590833678.text:
In SAP Analytics Cloud, objects can be saved to subfolder locations. When these objects are part of the impact and lineage diagram, their folder hierarchies appear as a series of nested containers.
See [Accessing Catalog Assets](dc061a23484241b1b791f5540b1f38e3.html).
590833678.title: Folder Hierarchy for SAP Analytics Cloud Objects Appears in the Impact and Lineage Diagram

590833679.text:
The layout of the asset details page has been improved so that information about the asset (including details, relationships, and enrichments) is easier to find and manage.
See [Accessing Catalog Assets](dc061a23484241b1b791f5540b1f38e3.html) and [Enriching and Managing Catalog Assets](7ed60a094f2a464da6a8d75e5bfed9d5.html).
590833679.title: Improvements to the Asset Details Page

590833680.text:
Use the new Data Provider collection or the Data Provider filter when searching for data providers. A data provider is a person or company that offers one or multiple data products through the Data Marketplace.
See [Searching for Data Products and Assets in the Catalog](09bc571a876f448bb526a33d1ad00c61.html)
590833680.title: Search for Data Providers

590833681.text:
Assets from SAP Datasphere, SAP BW bridge source systems appear in the impact and lineage diagram.
See [Accessing Catalog Assets](dc061a23484241b1b791f5540b1f38e3.html).
590833681.title: Assets from SAP Datasphere, SAP BW bridge Available in the Impact and Lineage Diagram

590833682.text:
You can add an SAP Datasphere, SAP BW bridge system to the catalog. With this addition, metadata for the following objects from SAP BW Cloud systems are monitored and extracted to the catalog.
- ADSO (Advanced DataStore Object)
- AREA - (InfoArea)
- HCPR (Composite Provider)
- IOBJ (InfoObject)
- LSYS (Source System)
- RSDS (DataSource)
- TRCS (InfoSource)
- TRFN (Transformation)
Once extracted, you can publish these objects as assets to the catalog.
See [Connecting to BW Systems](b350d7c6e88c4f089d381dfe6feee792.html).
590833682.title: Ability to Add an SAP Datasphere, SAP BW bridge as a Source System

590833683.text: When a manual synchronization is run on an existing source system, only the objects that have been added or changed since the last manual synchronization are updated in the catalog. This ensures that only the necessary resources are used for the synchronization.
590833683.title: When Running a Manual Synchronization, Metadata from Only the Objects that Have Changed is Extracted

590833684.text:
Data products are data purchased from a third-party provider. Listed data products available in data marketplace are searchable in the catalog.
See [Catalog Tools and Features](bfc939d764c5490b96c5b1684f10a9cf.html).
590833684.title: Include Data Products in the Search Results

590833685.text:
On the Roles page, you can now see the individual privileges for the standard Catalog User and Catalog Administrator roles. These privileges allow you to:
- Read, create, and edit glossary and glossary terms, key performance indicators (KPIs), and tag hierarchies.
- Add enrichments to asset metadata.
- Manage and monitor source systems.
Also, instead of assigning the standard application roles to users to access and manage the catalog, you can now include the individual privileges for accessing and managing the catalog to your custom roles.
See [Standard Roles Delivered with SAP Datasphere](a50a51d80d5746c9b805a2aacbb7e4ee.html), [Privileges by App, Tool, Object, and Task](2d8b7d04dcae402f911d119437ce0a74.html), and [Create a Custom Role](862b88eed50244049d41361ba3290456.html)
590833685.title: Privileges for Catalog Access Can Be Added to Custom Roles

590833686.text:
The Monitoring page improvements aim to provide you with a better experience when creating and monitoring connections to all your source systems. You can now do the following tasks:
- Connect to more than three SAP Analytics Cloud tenants.
- See an overview of all system types and their statuses in a single table.
- See advanced systems details for a selected source systems:
- The extraction summary of all data and analytic objects.
- The extraction logs for automatic and manual synchronizations, where you can see which object failed to synchronize.
See [Connecting Source Systems](0b5de87f256f466f95b46d4bcaa52640.html).
590833686.title: Monitoring Page Improvements

590833687.text:
When you create a connection to a source system, you must authenticate a user for the source system. The purpose of this user is for customizing the scope of objects that will be extracted from the source system to the catalog.
Note
For all connections to source systems created before version 2023.24, a user for the source system must be authenticated. If a user is not authenticated for the source system, automatic metadata extraction for that source system will stop. For more information, see SAP note [3344922](https://launchpad.support.sap.com/#/notes/3344922).
See [Connecting Source Systems](0b5de87f256f466f95b46d4bcaa52640.html).
590833687.title: System User Needed for Extracting Metadata from Source System

590833688.text:
Catalog administrators can add term and KPI relationships to the detailed metadata (columns, attributes, measures, etc.) for an asset. For example, when reviewing the Details tab of an asset, you can create relationships between a specific measure and a term or KPI. After the detailed metadata of the asset is enriched, the catalog user can review the relationships when they evaluate the asset.
See [Enriching and Managing Catalog Assets](7ed60a094f2a464da6a8d75e5bfed9d5.html) or [Accessing Catalog Assets](dc061a23484241b1b791f5540b1f38e3.html).
590833688.title: Ability to Add KPI and Term Relationships to the Detailed Metadata for the an Asset

590833689.text:
You can connect the local SAP Datasphere tenant and multiple external SAP Datasphere tenants to a single catalog.
See [Connecting to SAP Datasphere Systems](16d4e71b8dd545b0be1b956c26e652cd.html).
590833689.title: Ability to Connect Multiple SAP Datasphere Tenants to the Catalog

590833690.text:
To help catalog administrators better manage the assets, improvements have been made in how you maintain glossary terms, tags, and KPIs, and how you apply them to assets. There are also improvements from the main catalog page to access other areas of the catalog. To help catalog users, improvements have been made to how property information in the asset details is organized. To help both users, performance has improved with caching.
See:
- [Manage Tag Relationships for Assets](bb608dd2a4dc402889351c4303a173a4.html)
- [Enriching and Managing Catalog Assets](7ed60a094f2a464da6a8d75e5bfed9d5.html)
- [Accessing Catalog Assets](dc061a23484241b1b791f5540b1f38e3.html)
- [Using the Business Glossary](224f6bf5e5054c0697cbf26ff770358d.html)
- [Create and Manage a Glossary](e40310c9781848bfad031cce7792f394.html)
- [Create and Manage a Glossary Category](e9ce9f6e36384517b531f6e9cf88f498.html)
- [Create and Manage Glossary Terms](193336a4eba94c978c08fd2cee625a3e.html)
- [Create and Manage Key Performance Indicators](ca4f04da3afa4f82b85a0835fceb444b.html)
- [Create and Manage Key Performance Indicator Categories](bc3b630394494381b83bf406b262a598.html)
- [Define the Key Performance Indicator Template](b3ead0d4944c40ddbdb1ebae239cc69f.html)
- [Publishing Content to the Catalog](f31d2d97afb0482a874acb0ec61465fe.html)
590833690.title: Usability Improvements to Enhance Your Catalog Experience

590833691.text:
In this release, we’ve introduced the new SAP Datasphere catalog. The catalog provides an effective data governance strategy and is the central place to identify, enrich, publish, and promote the use of your organization’s trusted data and analytic assets. To get started, check out: [Governing and Publishing Data in the Catalog](de29b96a9438439682715a93212ae4f4.html).
- Manage Source Systems
You can use the Monitoring page to connect to data sources, monitor the data source extractions, and remove or restore data sources.
See:
- [Connecting Source Systems](0b5de87f256f466f95b46d4bcaa52640.html)
- [Monitoring Metadata Extractions](6a03ef378f7b4dffaff5ef0e3aa7f5d5.html)
- [Deleting Connections to Source Systems](d07b3e27cb1e46dea507c3d0cb7c43eb.html)
- Glossary Terms, Tags, and KPIs
You can manage glossary terms, tags, and KPIs and link them to assets.
See:
- [Using the Business Glossary](224f6bf5e5054c0697cbf26ff770358d.html)
- [Enriching and Managing Catalog Assets](7ed60a094f2a464da6a8d75e5bfed9d5.html)
- [Using Key Performance Indicators](3550f14d4cd74dfaa63ebcaa25b288c2.html)
- Discover Content
The catalog is the central place where you find data from your data sources.
See:
- [Searching for Data Products and Assets in the Catalog](10478251045b43e782fa15e0f3e113b0.html)
- [Accessing Catalog Assets](dc061a23484241b1b791f5540b1f38e3.html)
590833691.title: SAP Datasphere Catalog

590833692.text: You can now replicate data from ODP data sources with load type Initial+Delta without primary key. See [SAP S/4HANA and Other ABAP Sources for Replication Flows](3f70579c92434f4f88471bba2bd70893.html).
590833692.title: Load type Initial and Delta now available for ODP Data Sources

590833693.text:
When using ABAP RFC streaming with Data Provisioning Agent version 2.7.0.0 or higher, you can now specify a list of hosts for streaming batch jobs.
Each time a streaming query on an ABAP table is executed, the system assigns the corresponding streaming batch job to a target server chosen randomly from this list.
If you don't specify a list of execution targets, the source system assigns the target servers.
See:
- [SAP ABAP Connections](a75c1aacf951449ba3b740c7e46da3a9.html)
- [SAP S/4HANA On-Premise Connections](a49a1e3cc50f4af89711d8306bdd8f26.html)
590833693.title: Define Execution Targets When Using ABAP RFC Streaming With SAP ABAP and SAP S/4HANA Connections

590833694.text:
You can reuse a target local table (with or without delta capture enabled) of a replication flow as a source table in another replication flow. It will create a relationship between the two replication flows.
See [Reusing Objects as Source or Target in Several Replication Flows](d570eee0045a4b9ab5d47ac70140d60a.html).
590833694.title: Reuse a Target Table of a Replication as a Source Table of Another Replication Flow

590833695.text: You can increase the maximum number of parallel jobs up to 16 to run replication flows.See [Configure the Size of Your SAP Datasphere Tenant](33f8ef4ec359409fb75925a68c23ebc3.html) and [Sizing, Capacity Planning, and Load Balancing for Replication Flows](5a3419f3be6e49f794248f20331b255b.html).
590833695.title: Increase Maximum Parallel Job

590833696.text:
You can now enable RFC fast serialization for SAP ABAP connections when replicating data using replication flows. This can help improve replication flow performance, particularly in cases of large data volumes.The Fast Serialization property is available in a new Replication Flow section. For new SAP ABAP connections, the default is On. For existing connections, the default is Off.
See:
- [SAP ABAP Connections](a75c1aacf951449ba3b740c7e46da3a9.html)
- [Prepare Connectivity to SAP ABAP Systems](76c9ac1a318c4de2bea29e72c64be8a0.html)
590833696.title: Improved RFC Performance for Replication Flows (SAP ABAP Connections)

590833697.text: Delete records or versions of a local table (File), creating a direct task or using a schedule, and free up storage by allocating the required amount of compute resources that the file space can consume when processing these tasks.See [Delete Data From Your Local Tables (File)](872ad509995a451890bf8b80b73ec0e6.html).
590833697.title: Delete Data From Your Local Tables (File)

590833698.text: From the Flows monitor or the replication flow editor, you can change the run settings once you have deployed the replication flow in your tenant. Update the Source and target thread limit, and change the delta load frequency if needed for your use case. See [Configure the Run Settings of a Replication Flow](3f5ba0c5ae3944c1b7279bb989a2a5b5.html) and [Working With Existing Replication Flow Runs](da62e1ee746448e8bc043e1be4377cbe.html)..
590833698.title: Update the Run Settings for Your Replication Flow

590833699.text: From the Replication Flow editor or the Flows monitor, you can setup an email notification to stay informed when the replication of an individual object fails in a replication flow.See [Configure Email Notification for Replication Flow Failure at Object Level](5dc4db23d3894b10aca6ade3c666554d.html) and [Working With Existing Replication Flow Runs](da62e1ee746448e8bc043e1be4377cbe.html) .
590833699.title: Configure Email Notification for Replication Flow Failure at Object Level

590833700.text:
You can now use Microsoft OneLake and the corresponding connection type to add sources to replication flows and replicate data in CSV format from the source. See:
- [Cloud Storage Provider Sources for Replication Flows](4d481a2c620f4b52ba65b360299d7719.html)
- [Microsoft OneLake Connections](057fa4b51c734e679dd70eec9514839d.html)
590833700.title: Use Microsoft OneLake as a Source for Your Replication Flow

590833701.text:
You can now use X.509 client certificates for authentication when creating connections to Microsoft Azure SQL Databases in a more secure way. The new authentication type is supported for replication flows. If you want to use it for replication flows and you want to access the same Microsoft Azure SQL Database instance with remote tables or data flows using basic authentication (user name and password), you must create separate connections.
For new connections, X.509 Client Certificate becomes the default authentication type. For existing connections, you can't change the authentication type from User Name and Password to X.509 Client Certificate.
Note that we've also removed the Version selection field from the Create Connection creation wizard and the Edit Connection dialog because Microsoft Azure SQL Database has only one version, making the field unnecessary.
See [Microsoft Azure SQL Database Connections](46343fc1c4544fa9a075d97f84d39826.html).
590833701.title: X.509 Client Certificate Support for Microsoft Azure SQL Database Connections

590833702.text: The View Monitor in the Data Integration Monitor now provides quicker access to views that have been recently run and persisted views. There are also additional task log details to help make more informed decisions and improvements.See [Persisting and Monitoring Views](9af04c990f294fd28c00f46763dd8b0d.html).
590833702.title: Improved Monitor Features for Persisted Views

590833703.text:
Break large transformation flow datasets into batches to avoid Out-Of-Memory (OOM) errors when using SAP HANA runtime. This feature enhances performance and reliability, ensuring efficient data integration and processing.
See [Monitoring Flows](b661ea0766a24c7d839df950330a89fd.html).
590833703.title: Define Batches on Transformation Flows when Using SAP HANA Runtime

590833704.text: You can now use X.509 client certificates or certificate chains for authentication when creating connections to SAP HANA Cloud, Data Lake Relational Engine in a more secure way. For new connections, X.509 Client Certificate becomes the default authentication type.See [SAP HANA Cloud, Data Lake Relational Engine Connections](40763e2e3e33440db0c37f6bcbe650f0.html).
590833704.title: X.509 Client Certificate Support for SAP HANA Cloud, Data Lake Relational Engine Connections

590833705.text:
For the connection types SAP S/4HANA Cloud and SAP ABAP (Web Socket RFC protocol), you can now use authentication with X.509 Client Certificate for data federation with remote tables via the ABAP SQL service.See:
- [SAP ABAP Connections](a75c1aacf951449ba3b740c7e46da3a9.html)
- [SAP S/4HANA Cloud Connections](a98e5ffdf47c44d9a845dca01a18bd82.html)
590833705.title: X.509 Client Certificate Authentication Supported for Data Federation with ABAP SQL service

590833706.text: Options in the task chain editor toolbar have been rearranged and a new Layout option was added. The new Layout option allows you to rearrange the visual display of a task chain on the canvas, from top-to-bottom (the default), or left-to-right.See [Creating a Task Chain](d1afbc2b9ee84d44a00b0b777ac243e1.html).
590833706.title: New Layout Option in Task Chain Toolbar

590833707.text: In the Local Tables (File) Monitor, two new columns help you monitor the size and file count information for data waiting in the inbound buffer. Thanks to these columns, you can track whether your automated merge has failed or if the merge needs to be run manually.See [Monitoring Local Tables (File)](6b2d0073a8684ee6a59d6f47d00ec895.html).
590833707.title: Monitor the Size and File Count for Data Waiting in the Inbound Buffer

590833708.text: You can export objects from and import objects to file spaces.See [Transporting Content Between Tenants](df12666cf98e41248ef2251c564b0166.html).
590833708.title: Transport Objects Between File Spaces

590833709.text: A new load type, Delta Only is available to run your replication flows: If your business case does not require an initial load of data, you can skip it with this new load type to replicate only delta changes.See [Creating a Replication Flow](25e2bd7a70d44ac5b05e844f9e913471.html), [Configure the Run Settings of a Replication Flow](3f5ba0c5ae3944c1b7279bb989a2a5b5.html) and [Modify Replication Flow Object Schemas and Settings](a24c71f3ba7548909534d4cb52cefbfc.html).
590833709.title: Delta Only Load Type in Replication Flow

590833710.text:
You can now enable RFC fast serialization for SAP S/4HANA Cloud connections when replicating data using replication flows. This can help improve replication flow performance, particularly in cases of large data volumes.For new SAP S/4HANA Cloud connections, the default of the Fast Serialization property is On. For existing connections, the default is Off.
See:
- [Prepare Connectivity to SAP S/4HANA Cloud](abb159e027184c98a54fc1b2a88dd3f5.html)
- [SAP S/4HANA Cloud Connections](a98e5ffdf47c44d9a845dca01a18bd82.html)
590833710.title: Improved RFC Performance for Replication Flows (SAP S/4HANA Cloud Connections)

590833711.text:
Persisted views with Data Access Control now re-attach persistence upon deployment in newer versions of SAP Datasphere and HANA. For views with Data Access Controls with structure "Single Values" that were set to persisted before SAP Datasphere version 2025.10 and SAP HANA version 2025.2.8, the persistence is removed when the view is deployed. You will need to persist the view again.
This feature ensures data continuity, eliminating the need to manually re-persist views after deployment.
See [Persisted Views and Data Access Control](7a4a983611cc4efb9415e6f3db310eaa.html).
590833711.title: Enhanced Persistence for Views with Data Access Control

590833712.text:
You can now replicate data from a file storage using a secure file transfer protocol (SFTP) connection for secure and reliable file transfers to a supported target. See:
- [Secure File Transfer Protocol (SFTP) Sources for Replication Flows](a832ef4cee9d4d3aa1210869743b6173.html)
- [Generic SFTP Connections](b645de78a8374c24871ab6169be40d35.html)
590833712.title: Secure File Transfer Protocol (SFTP) as Source for Your Replication Flow

590833713.text: You can create a replication flow with an SQL view or a script view as a source. However, you must fulfill some conditionsSee [SQL and Script View Source Objects for Replication Flows](a215f8f8257d4cf88a9ef927b8b101c5.html).
590833713.title: SQL and Script Views as Source Objects for Your Replication Flows

590833714.text: Analysis in View Analyzer now considers all entities from other spaces in partition adviser.See [Creating Partitions for Your Persisted Views](9b1b595054c34da5b67ac07595093f82.html) .
590833714.title: Enhanced Cross-Space Analysis when Defining Partition

590833715.text: We have harmonized the terminology in the Data Integration Monitor for a consistent user experience among the different monitors. See [Managing and Monitoring Data Integration](4cbf7c7fc64645bfa364332827557267.html).
590833715.title: Terminology Updates in Data Integration Monitor

590833716.text:
You can now use the datasphere command line interface to create connections or update connection details (including credentials) for the following additional connection types: Amazon Athena, Amazon Redshift, Hadoop Distributed File System, Microsoft Azure Blob Storage, Microsoft Azure SQL Database, SAP BW∕4HANA Model Transfer, SAP HANA Cloud, data lake Files, and SAP HANA Cloud, data lake Relational Engine.
See [Manage Connectivity via the Command Line](3918242966c74f11858db39c8e5228e4.html).
590833716.title: Manage Additional Connection Types via the Command Line

590833717.text:
You can now create replication flows to replicate data from supported source systems into Secure File Transfer Protocol (SFTP). See:
- [Secure File Transfer Protocol (SFTP) for Replication Flows](5a14eb1709a24a35821d1618285d021d.html)
- [Generic SFTP Connections](b645de78a8374c24871ab6169be40d35.html)
590833717.title: Secure File Transfer Protocol (SFTP) as Targets for Your Replication Flow

590833718.text: One source object can be reused in several replication flows.See [Add the Source for a Replication Flow](749638060e8746e48b0f9bf0e50c6d0c.html).
590833718.title: Use a Single Source Object in Several Replication Flows

590833719.text:
You can now use the ABAP SQL service for SQL-level remote access to data from published, ABAP-managed CDS view entities in SAP S/4HANA (on-premise) and SAP S/4HANA with connection type SAP ABAP. To facilitate this way of accessing data, we've added a new section called Remote Tables in the connection properties of the SAP ABAP connection type. In this section, you can choose between different data provisioning options. For the RFC protocol, the existing Data Provisioning Agent selection moved from the Features section to the Remote Tables section. To use the ABAP SQL Service for federated access to CDS view entities, you select data provisioning option Cloud Connector (for RFC protocol) or Direct (for Websocket RFC protocol).
Using the ABAP SQL service is supported for basic authentication with user name and password. For on-premise systems, the SAP Logon connection type must be application server and Cloud Connector must be used.
See:
- [SAP ABAP Connections](a75c1aacf951449ba3b740c7e46da3a9.html)
- [Using ABAP SQL Services for Accessing Data from SAP S/4HANA](4d7474595a5b41bb986616262ff44a3a.html)
- [Using ABAP SQL Services for Accessing Data from SAP S/4HANA Cloud or SAP BTP ABAP Environment](ef2b2238154f4cd78a08df360447c1d5.html)
590833719.title: Use Connection Type SAP ABAP for Data Federation With Remote Tables Using the ABAP SQL Service in SAP S/4HANA or SAP S/4HANA Cloud

590833720.text: As an administrator in SAP BW or SAP BW∕4HANA, you can now push data into SAP Datasphere as local tables (file). These tables are stored in the object store and can be used for your business case.See [Integrating Data from SAP BW and SAP BW∕4HANA with the Data Product Generator for SAP Business Data Cloud](cca4744c85b14788babe7cb6b77c9973.html).
590833720.title: Integrate SAP BW data into SAP Datasphere

590833721.text:
You can now use the datasphere command line interface to create connections or update connection details (including credentials) for the following additional connection types: Amazon Simple Storage Service, Apache Kafka, Cloud Data Integration, Confluent, Generic JDBC, Generic OData, Generic SFTP, Google BigQuery, Google Cloud Storage, Microsoft Azure Data Lake Store Gen2, Microsoft SQL Server, Oracle, SAP ABAP, SAP BW, SAP ECC, SAP HANA, SAP SuccessFactors, SAP S/4HANA Cloud, and SAP S/4HANA On-Premise
See [Manage Connectivity via the Command Line](3918242966c74f11858db39c8e5228e4.html).
590833721.title: Manage Additional Connection Types via the Command Line

590833722.text:
You can now use OAuth 2.0 authentication with client credentials for SAP ABAP (on-premise) and SAP S/4HANA connections. The OAuth 2.0 authentication type is available when the following conditions are met:
- You use Cloud Connector to enable the SAP ABAP or SAP S/4HANA connection for replication flows and data flows.
- For SAP ABAP connections: You use the RFC protocol to connect to an on-premise system.
Remote tables (and model import for SAP S/4HANA connections) are not supported with OAuth 2.0 authentication. When changing an existing connection from basic authentication to OAuth 2.0 authentication, remote tables will be disabled.
See :
- [SAP ABAP Connections](a75c1aacf951449ba3b740c7e46da3a9.html)
- [SAP S/4HANA On-Premise Connections](a49a1e3cc50f4af89711d8306bdd8f26.html)
590833722.title: Use OAuth 2.0 Authentication for Secure Access to SAP ABAP and SAP S/4HANA connections

590833723.text:
You can cancel a transformation flow run on file with or without rollback:
- Cancel with rollback allows the data to be restored to the version it had when the run started.
- Cancelling without rollback stops the run where it is and what has already been processed will be kept.
See [Cancel a Transformation Flow Run](ab885f05210f4a52aebe8306c8cad083.html).
590833723.title: Cancelling Options for Transformation Flow Runs on File

590833724.text:
As part of a simulated run, you can now use the Explain Plan to understand how the selected transformation flow run will be executed and get details about its performance. It is a quick way to obtain an overview of your run without saving any changes to your run.
See [Explore Transformation Flows](7588192bf4cd4e3db43704239ba4d366.html).
590833724.title: Generate an Explain Plan for a Transformation Flow Run

590833725.text: You can now schedule tasks in your preferred region/location time zone. Schedules will automatically adjust to reflect daylight saving time. This ensures accurate timing for task execution to syncronize with all shared global operations.See [Schedule a Data Integration Task (Simple Schedule)](7c11059ed3314e1fb753736b7867512c.html) and [Schedule a Data Integration Task (with Cron Expression)](169ba34e19744362be25a4325de8d10c.html).
590833725.title: Schedule Tasks to Run in Preferred Region/Location Time Zone with Daylight Saving Adjustments

590833726.text: From the Local Tables (File) monitor you can now optimize and merge your data using a direct task run or via a schedule. You can also update the settings to run these tasks using the necessary workload that applies to your case.See [Monitoring Local Tables (File)](6b2d0073a8684ee6a59d6f47d00ec895.html) and [Merge or Optimize Your Local Tables (File)](e533b154ed3e49ce9a03e4421a5296e7.html).
590833726.title: Optimize and Merge Your Local Tables (Files) Data

590833727.text: The View Analyzer identifies local tables (file) consumed directly or inderectly by views. Local tables (file) are evaluated when calculating data persistence candidate scores for views. See [Data Persistence Guidance](85f7be45761f4ae5b7e49819ce4b4d2e.html).
590833727.title: View Analyzer Interprets Local Tables (File).

590833728.text: When creating a new replication flow to load data from an ABAP-based source system, you can choose between Template Type or Native Type. The content type can be modify later on if needed but with some restrictions to consider.See [Creating a Replication Flow](25e2bd7a70d44ac5b05e844f9e913471.html) and [Modify Replication Flow Object Schemas and Settings](a24c71f3ba7548909534d4cb52cefbfc.html).
590833728.title: New Content Type to Load Data From an ABAP-Based Source System

590833729.text:
You can now use connection type SAP Signavio and replication flows to load data from SAP source systems, such as SAP S/4HANA, into SAP Signavio as target system. This allows for efficient and scalable data replication to SAP Signavio.See:
- [SAP Signavio Targets for Replication Flows](b8f5e28d34b44d71a52f6265e4fc245f.html)
- [SAP Signavio Connections](4c367de075a44ad7b7a6db576a4a9c82.html)
590833729.title: Use SAP Signavio as Target for Your Replication Flows

590833730.text:
You can now use the ABAP SQL Service for SQL-level remote access to data from published, ABAP-managed CDS view entities in SAP S/4HANA. Instead of accessing ABAP-managed database objects like tables or CDS views via the SQL layer of the SAP S/4HANA database, you can use the SQL service exposure to access SAP S/4HANA directly, taking advantage of ABAP-level security concepts and full ABAP SQL semantics. Using the SQL service, you can expose CDS view entities to SAP Datasphere by creating a service definition and binding and a corresponding role for privileged access. To facilitate this new way of accessing SAP S/4HANA data, we've added a new section called Remote Tables in the connection properties of the SAP S/4HANA connection type. In this section, you can choose between different data provisioning options, including the existing Data Provisioning Agent selection which moved from the Features section to the Remote Tables section. To use the ABAP SQL Service for federated access to CDS view entities, you select data provisioning option Cloud Connector.
See:
- [Using ABAP SQL Services for Accessing Data from SAP S/4HANA](4d7474595a5b41bb986616262ff44a3a.html)
- [SAP S/4HANA On-Premise Connections](a49a1e3cc50f4af89711d8306bdd8f26.html)
590833730.title: Use the ABAP SQL Service in SAP S/4HANA for Data Federation With Remote Tables

590833731.text: Task chains may now be canceled after a run has started, by selecting the Cancel Run link from the Run Details display for a specific task chain. If you click this link, SAP Datasphere will initiate the cancel operation and immediately remove all child tasks not already run. For any child task that has already started, the effect of the cancel operation depends on the individual object. For example, replication flows and Open SQL procedures cannot effectively be canceled, so successful completion of the task chain cancelation will wait until those child tasks are completed.See [Monitoring Task Chains](4142201ec1aa49faad89a688a2f1852c.html).
590833731.title: Task Chain Cancelation

590833732.text: If you are using an existing table as the target for your replication flow, this table may contain columns that don't exist in the corresponding source object. Previously, you'd have to remove each of these columns manually in the table editor before you could start you replication flow. Now you can choose to ignore these columns during the replication.See [Add the Target for a Replication Flow](ab490fb4d083442197e2ba3b92079734.html).
590833732.title: Skip target columns that don't exist in the source

590833733.text:
As a data modeler or data integrator, you have the option to generate an Explain Plan in the view analyzer to analyze the performance of a view and get a quick and efficient overview of your model.
See [Getting Started with View Analyzer](e0aeddba00b14be29b5e49b47001d43b.html) .
590833733.title: Generate Explain Plan in View Analyzer

590833734.text:
You can now enable RFC fast serialization for SAP S/4HANA on-premise connections when replicating data using replication flows. This can help improve replication flow performance, particularly in cases of large data volumes.For new SAP S/4HANA connections, the default of the Fast Serialization property is On. For existing connections, the default is Off.
See:
- [Prepare Connectivity to SAP S/4HANA On-Premise](8de01dd25c1e443e8e2de7d2fbe1364d.html)
- [SAP S/4HANA On-Premise Connections](a49a1e3cc50f4af89711d8306bdd8f26.html)
590833734.title: Improved RFC Performance for Replication Flows (SAP S/4HANA Connections)

590833735.text:
You can now list, validate, and delete connections and read connection details, and you can create and edit SAP SuccssFactors connections via the command line or via the REST API. See:
- [Managing Connections via the Command Line](8eb811898d1049fbb426339e44a2eb70.html)
- [SAP SuccessFactors (Connection Definition File Format)](d75cee60bda04dadb7b2e96ad090ea14.html)
590833735.title: Manage Connections via the Command Line or via REST API

590833736.text:
Monitoring information for replication flows is now available at partition level (not just for the replication flow run as a whole). Information at partition level is not available for replication flow runs that were started before version 2024.21 and are in status Completed or Failed. If you run the respective replication flow again, partitioning information is displayed for this latest run.
For more information about monitoring, see [Monitoring Flows](b661ea0766a24c7d839df950330a89fd.html).
590833736.title: Improved monitoring information for replication flows

590833737.text: You can now validate the status for connections to Apache Kafka and Confluent in the Connections app.See [Validate a Connection](99bd2294c3724d478c41555e186ce0ef.html).
590833737.title: Validation for Apache Kafka and Confluent Connections

590833738.text: Models consuming entities shared from other spaces can now be analyzed fully in the View Analyzer.See [Exploring Views with View Analyzer](8921e5acf2ad4c8a98073edae4c214c7.html).
590833738.title: Cross-Space Analysis in View Analyzer

590833739.text:
From the Local Tables monitor, you can clean up your table records:
- Delete all records contained in the table.
- Delete records using filter conditions.
- Delete records marked as deleted in your local table where delta capture is enabled.
See [Controlling Deletion of Local Table Records](2a59b7142e1b4d478b0bf4063084261e.html).
590833739.title: Delete Local Tables Records On-Demand, Using Filter Conditions or Using a Schedule.

590833740.text: The total used premium outbound volume (for all replication flows in the tenant) for the last 90 days is now displayed directly in the Flows monitor. See [Working With Existing Replication Flow Runs](da62e1ee746448e8bc043e1be4377cbe.html).
590833740.title: Premium outbound volume for replication flows displayed in Flows monitor

590833741.text:
You can now use the following cloud storage providers and the corresponding connection types to add sources to replication flows:
- Data lake Files from SAP HANA Cloud, data lake
- Amazon Simple Storage Service
- Google Cloud Storage
- Microsoft Azure Data Lake Gen2
See
- [Cloud Storage Provider Sources for Replication Flows](4d481a2c620f4b52ba65b360299d7719.html)
- [Integrating Data via Connections](eb85e157ab654152bd68a8714036e463.html)
590833741.title: Cloud storage providers as sources for replication flows

590833742.text: You can now use CDS views and ODP artifacts that do not have a primary key as the source for a replication flow (load type Initial Only). See [SAP S/4HANA and Other ABAP Sources for Replication Flows](3f70579c92434f4f88471bba2bd70893.html).
590833742.title: Objects without primary key as sources for replication flows

590833743.text:
You can now use the ABAP SQL Service for SQL-level remote access to data from published, ABAP-managed CDS view entities in SAP S/4HANA Cloud. Instead of accessing ABAP-managed database objects like tables or CDS views via the SQL layer of the SAP S/4HANA Cloud database, you can use the SQL service exposure to access SAP S/4HANA Cloud directly, taking advantage of ABAP-level security concepts and full ABAP SQL semantics.
Using the SQL service, you can expose CDS view entities to SAP HANA by creating a service definition and binding and a corresponding communication arrangement. To facilitate this new way of accessing SAP S/4HANA Cloud data, we've added a new section called Remote Tables in the connection properties of the SAP S/4HANA Cloud connection type. In this section, you can choose between different data provisioning options, including the existing Data Provisioning Agent selection which moved from the Features section to the Remote Tables section. To use the ABAP SQL Service for federated access to CDS view entities, you select data provisioning option Direct.
See:
- [Why SQL Services?](https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_S4HANA_CLOUD/6aa39f1ac05441e5a23f484f31e477e7/4082fe1b66164eeb8aa41192166526af.html) in the SAP S/4HANA Cloud documentation
- [Using ABAP SQL Services for Accessing Data from SAP S/4HANA Cloud or SAP BTP ABAP Environment](ef2b2238154f4cd78a08df360447c1d5.html)
- [SAP S/4HANA Cloud Connections](a98e5ffdf47c44d9a845dca01a18bd82.html)
590833743.title: Use the ABAP SQL Service in SAP S/4HANA Cloud for Data Federation With Remote Tables

590833744.text: Previously, data flows were able to consume data from Oracle databases available on the public internet. This restriction is removed. Using Cloud Connector with your Oracle connection, data flows now can also consume data from Oracle on-premise databases.See [Oracle Connections](c73ae0601d364f47830d339b6e86b7e8.html).
590833744.title: Access Oracle On-Premise Databases With Oracle Connection Type

590833745.text: Local tables that are enabled for delta capturing and have load type Initial and Delta can now be used as source objects in a replication flow. See [Add the Source for a Replication Flow](749638060e8746e48b0f9bf0e50c6d0c.html) and [Capturing Delta Changes in Your Local Table](154bdffb35814d5481d1f6de143a6b9e.html).
590833745.title: Local tables with load type Initial and Delta as sources for replication flows

590833746.text: Data persistence can be run for a view that contains one single input parameter, and if this input parameter has a default value maintained. The technical name of the parameter used to persist the view is displayed in the metrics tab in the Views monitor detail screen. See[Persisting and Monitoring Views](9af04c990f294fd28c00f46763dd8b0d.html) and [Understanding the Data Persistence Metrics](d65994c3611946c19c2634e1a6c0a7ad.html).
590833746.title: Persisted Views and Input Parameters

590833747.text: You can now integrate SAP Datasphere with SAP Cloud Transport Management service to transport content packages across different landscapes. See [Transporting Content Through SAP Cloud Transport Management](05383980f0704c71ab9872360ce45622.html).
590833747.title: Transport Your Content Through SAP Cloud Transport Management

590833748.text: The details screen in the Views monitor displays the name of the elastic compute node used to persist the view.See [Understanding the Data Persistence Metrics](d65994c3611946c19c2634e1a6c0a7ad.html).
590833748.title: Elastic Compute Node Name Metric

590833749.text: You can now include Open SQL procedures within task chains. See [Run Open SQL Procedures in a Task Chain](59b9c773035a48c5beb54ce9bb29f1d8.html). For procedures to be available to be included in a task chain, an administrator must grant EXECUTE privileges for objects in the Open SQL schema space. See [Allow the Space to Access the Open SQL Schema](7eaa370fe4624dea9f182ee9c9ab645f.html).
590833749.title: Include Open SQL Schema Procedures in Task Chains

590833750.text: You can persist a view when one or multiple "Operator and Value" or "Hierarchy" DACs are assigned to the view.See[Persisting and Monitoring Views](9af04c990f294fd28c00f46763dd8b0d.html) .
590833750.title: Persist Views Protected with Data Access "Operator and Value" and "Hierarchy"

590833751.text: The details screen in the Views monitor now indicates if your view data is protected by a data access control.See [Understanding the Data Persistence Metrics](d65994c3611946c19c2634e1a6c0a7ad.html).
590833751.title: Data Access Control Metrics

590833752.text: You can now add an open SQL schema object as a source in a transformation flow. See [Creating a Transformation Flow](f7161e6c20204672ac4a6d90c81762e4.html).
590833752.title: Open SQL Schema Objects in Transformation Flows

590833753.title: Local Tables Monitor Available in the Data Integration Monitors

590833754.text: The status descriptions in replication flow monitoring have been rephrased so that they are more self-explanatory. In particular, they now differentiate more clearly between the situation at flow level and at object level. See also [Working With Existing Replication Flow Runs](da62e1ee746448e8bc043e1be4377cbe.html).
590833754.title: Improved status texts in replication flow monitoring

590833755.text: You can now use TLS encryption for the Schema Registry in Confluent connections.See [Confluent Connections](d83c08ad4eaf49dba9602b1d51c07a52.html#loiod83c08ad4eaf49dba9602b1d51c07a52).
590833755.title: Transport layer security for Schema Registry in Confluent Connections

590833756.text: Upload of data in a table can now be monitored in a details log that is accessible by clicking on the task in the notification area or navigating to the logs tab of the System Monitor.See [Load or Delete Local Table Data](870401f211f94132909bd9f2fafd91b2.html).
590833756.title: Enhancement of Monitoring While Uploading data in Table Editor

590833757.text:
For local tables as the source of a replication flow, you can now also use local tables that are enabled for delta capturing. However this is still only possible for load type Initial Only ( not Initial and Delta).
See [Add the Source for a Replication Flow](749638060e8746e48b0f9bf0e50c6d0c.html).
590833757.title: Delta-Enabled Local Tables As Source for Replication Flows

590833758.text: To ensure better resilience, the SQL procedure to persist view data is always executed asynchronously.
590833758.title: Processing Mode to Persist View Data is Asynchronous Only

590833759.text: If email notification is set up for a task chain, you'll now receive email notifications if an error occurs during initialization or preparation to run the task chain, before the task chain run actually starts.See [Creating a Task Chain](d1afbc2b9ee84d44a00b0b777ac243e1.html).
590833759.title: Task Chain Email Notification

590833760.text:
Replication flows can now be scheduled and included in task chains if all their objects have load type Initial Only.See:
- [Schedule a Data Integration Task (Simple Schedule)](7c11059ed3314e1fb753736b7867512c.html)
- [Creating a Task Chain](d1afbc2b9ee84d44a00b0b777ac243e1.html)
590833760.title: Scheduling and Task Chains for Replication Flows (Initial Only)

590833761.text:
In Views monitor, you can now see all views that have been created in the Data Builder without additional actions from your side. Views are displayed into 3 tabs to allow a better navigation:
- All Views: It displays all the deployed views that have been created in the Data Builder for the current space.
- Scheduled (default): It displays the views for which a schedule is defined to persist the data.
- Persisted: It displays the views already persisted.
See [Persisting and Monitoring Views](9af04c990f294fd28c00f46763dd8b0d.html).
590833761.title: Views Monitor Displays all Deployed Views Into 3 Tabs

590833762.text: You can now use X.509 client certificates or certificate chains for authentication when creating connections to SAP HANA in a more secure way. For new connections, X.509 Client Certificate becomes the default authentication type.See [SAP HANA Connections](e6b63f176d3640609adcf06297fb37e9.html#loioe6b63f176d3640609adcf06297fb37e9).
590833762.title: X.509 Client Certificate Support for SAP HANA Connections

590833763.text: You now have a better overview of all connections with warning messages. When there is one or more messages for your connections, a button is displayed in the toolbar of the Connections app specifying the number of warning messages for your connections. Clicking the button opens the list of messages providing guidance on how to solve the issues. In the connections list, connections with warning messages are highlighted in yellow. See [Integrating Data via Connections](eb85e157ab654152bd68a8714036e463.html).
590833763.title: Improved Display of Warning Messages in Connections App

590833764.text: When you persist view data that is coming from different spaces, you can display the information of the data provenance by spaces clicking in the View Details in the log. From this View Details, you can navigate to the Remote Queries monitor and check the statement details.
590833764.title: Enhancement of Data Persistence Run Logs with Spaces Information

590833765.text:
When replicating data to Parquet files in a cloud storage provider, you can now have the time data type columns converted into int64 (microseconds after midnight) so that they can be consumed by Apache Spark.
See [Using a Cloud Storage Provider As the Target](https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_DATASPHERE/c8a54ee704e94e15926551293243fd1d/43d93a27150a4a218e3df14e3abdf456.html).
590833765.title: Enable Apache Spark Compatibility

590833766.text:
When replicating data to a cloud storage provider, you now have the option to suppress duplicate records in the target.
See [Using a Cloud Storage Provider As the Target](https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_DATASPHERE/c8a54ee704e94e15926551293243fd1d/43d93a27150a4a218e3df14e3abdf456.html).
590833766.title: Suppress Duplicate Records

590833767.text:
When you run a transformation flow that loads delta changes to a target table, the system uses a watermark (a timestamp) to track the data that has been transferred. You can now view the watermark for a source table. You can also reset the watermark if required.
If you reset a watermark, the system will transfer all data to the target table the next time the transformation flow runs (using the load type Initial and Delta).
See [Watermarks](890897f00a4944c7a6f90d3816a8d4c6.html).
590833767.title: Watermarks for Transformation Flows

590833768.text:
You can now define the length of the delta interval for replication flows with load type Initial and Delta.
See[Configure the Run Settings of a Replication Flow](3f5ba0c5ae3944c1b7279bb989a2a5b5.html) .
590833768.title: Delta Interval for Replication Flow Can Be Changed

590833769.text: In addition to the data persistence simulation, the View Analyzer now offers the possibility to generate an SQL analyzer plan file that you can download for further analysis.See[Exploring Views with View Analyzer](8921e5acf2ad4c8a98073edae4c214c7.html).
590833769.title: Generate SQL Analyzer Plan File

590833770.text:
You can now use Apache Kafka and the corresponding connection type to add targets to replication flows.See:
- [Apache Kafka Targets for Replication Flows](6df55db4028842c1b1866e709ffef456.html)
- [Integrating Data via Connections](eb85e157ab654152bd68a8714036e463.html)
590833770.title: Apache Kafka as Target for Replication Flows

590833771.text: When scheduling a new task in the Data Integration Monitor, or elsewhere in SAP Datasphere, users can now specify a frequency for scheduled runs in minutes, in addition to hourly, daily, weekly, or monthly intervals.See [Schedule a Data Integration Task (Simple Schedule)](7c11059ed3314e1fb753736b7867512c.html).
590833771.title: Scheduled Task Run Frequency Settings

590833772.text: You can now use local tables from SAP Datasphere as source objects for a replication flow (with load type Initial). See [Add the Source for a Replication Flow](749638060e8746e48b0f9bf0e50c6d0c.html).
590833772.title: Local Tables as Source for Replication Flows

590833773.text:
You can now use Google BigQuery and the corresponding connection type to add targets to replication flows.See:
- [Google BigQuery Targets for Replication Flows](56d4472a0e1f44d58e07ca26ab666328.html)
- [Google BigQuery Connections](30ed77de13864368bdc596099b37ed70.html)
- [Integrating Data via Connections](eb85e157ab654152bd68a8714036e463.html)
590833773.title: Google BigQuery As Target For Replication Flows

590833774.text: The new Semantic Onboarding app provides a central entry point to import semantically-rich objects from your SAP systems and the Content Network, as well as the Public Data Marketplace and other marketplace contexts.See [Semantic Onboarding](4c9e45e19ff14271a65f883e30023736.html).
590833774.title: Semantic Onboarding

590833775.text:
Microsoft Azure Data Lake Storage Gen1 will be retired on February 29, 2024. After this date, it might not be possible to access data with Gen1 connections.The corresponding SAP Datasphere connection type Microsoft Azure Data Lake Storage Gen1 is deprecated and may be removed in future releases.
Action: After your Microsoft Azure Data Lake Storage Gen1 has been migrated to Microsoft Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2, recreate existing Gen1 connections with the Gen2 connection type and adapt your models and processes to the new connections.
590833775.title: Deprecation of Connection Type Microsoft Azure Data Lake Storage Gen1

590833776.text: To ensure a consistent user experience in the Data Integration Monitor, terminology and user interface have been harmonized in all monitors. See [Managing and Monitoring Data Integration](4cbf7c7fc64645bfa364332827557267.html).
590833776.title: Consistent User Experience in Data Integration Monitor

590833777.text: To ensure a better resilience while persisting a view, the default job execution is now set to asynchronous mode. See [Change Persisted View Settings](d04f5dd6bbda44448407d54d2a7979be.html).
590833777.title: Default Job Execution to Persist a View changed to Asynchronous Mode

590833778.text:
You can now create transformation flows to to load data from one or more source tables, apply transformations (such as a join), and output the result in a target table. You can load a full set of data from one or more source tables to a target table. You can also load delta changes (including deleted records) from one source table to a target table.
See [Creating a Transformation Flow](f7161e6c20204672ac4a6d90c81762e4.html).
590833778.title: Transformation Flows

590833779.text: While defining partitions when persisting your views, switch on the option Rate Column Suitability to get information on column suitability for partitioning: The columns are ranked so that you can quickly identify the most suitable columns and additional information is provided about important factors that influence the suitability for each column to help you with your choice.See [Creating Partitions for Your Persisted Views](9b1b595054c34da5b67ac07595093f82.html).
590833779.title: Use Rate Column Suitability to Identify the Most Suitable Columns to Partion Your Views

590833780.text:
You can now use authentication type OAuth 2.0 with Microsoft Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 Connections supporting authentication with client ID and client secret, client ID and X.509 certificate, and username and password.
See [Microsoft Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 Connections](cd06b3c5ab5147c0905e3fa8abd13eb1.html).
590833780.title: Use OAuth 2.0 Authentication for Microsoft Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 Connections

590833781.text:
In data flows, you can now use input parameters in the expression for calculating a column.
See [Create an Input Parameter in a Data Flow](a6fb3e70da0a42b2aa4a7ac7b73f5ae1.html).
590833781.title: Use Input Parameters for Calculated Columns in Data Flows

590833782.text: In the Data Integration Monitor, you can select multiple objects to perform the same action, whenever it’s applicable. You can also pause, resume, delete and take the ownership of multiple schedules.
590833782.title: Perform Actions on Multiple Objects

590833783.text: If you change the partition definition, you can lock the unchanged partitions to avoid unnecessary data loads and ensure that only the new defined partitions are updated.See [Creating Partitions for Your Persisted Views](9b1b595054c34da5b67ac07595093f82.html).
590833783.title: Locked Partitions and Changes in the Partition Definition

590833784.text:
The configuration of Generic OData connections has been enhanced:
- You can now specify custom HTTP headers to add them to the OData request.
- You can now specify the content type of the OAuth2 token request. It can be either URL Encoded or JSON.
See [Generic OData Connections](5d36f1aae68a4e59989c424a66d948c9.html).
590833784.title: Generic OData Connection Type Supports Custom HTTP Headers and Selection of OAuth2 Token Request Content Type

590833785.text:
You can define input parameters in data flows and use them as a filter condition in projection operators.
At runtime, the user is prompted to enter a value. You can keep the default value for all parameters or define new values as filter criteria.
See [Create an Input Parameter in a Data Flow](a6fb3e70da0a42b2aa4a7ac7b73f5ae1.html).
590833785.title: Create Input Parameters for Data Flows

590833786.text:
You can now see the active primary key column with a new key icon shown in the properties panel and how it is propagated from source to target table.
A notification informs you if the source table has been modified and shows which columns have been set or removed.
See [Columns](8f0f40df2ed34035b8b5837897205ee6.html).
To apply new features to existing data flows, sync or open to update new primary key columns. For remote sources refresh the metadata.
590833786.title: Show Primary Key Column Field Propagation in Data Flow

590833787.text: In addition to linear task chains in which one task is executed after another, you can also create task chains in which individual tasks are run in parallel and continuation of the entire task chain run depends on whether ANY or ALL parallel tasks are completed successfully.See [Creating a Task Chain](d1afbc2b9ee84d44a00b0b777ac243e1.html).
590833787.title: Create Parallel Task Branches in Task Chains

590833788.text: You can now select multiple objects to import simultaneously via the Import Entities wizard.See [Importing Entities with Semantics from SAP S/4HANA](845fedbd28574aa8b84239df848936f6.html) and[Importing Entities with Semantics from SAP BW∕4HANA or SAP BW Bridge](7bcd3218b4064b898ca367b47ff246e2.html) .
590833788.title: Multi-Select Objects in the Import Entities Wizard
