Each user can only see the records that fulfill the operator-value pairs she is authorized for in the permissions entity, including support for complex AND and OR combinations. See [Create an "Operator and Values" Data Access Control](501594bf2afb4e49ab5ce254e35e3504.html).
590833986.title: Operator and Values Data Access Control

590833987.text: The SAP Datasphere Security Recommendations guide is now available. It provides a list with our recommendations for the configuration of SAP Datasphere to help you meet your compliance goals and secure your business.See [SAP Datasphere Security Recommendations](4b14c62a62eb4c83bb74e33f5a646aa5.html).
590833987.title: New Guide SAP Datasphere Security Recommendations

590833988.text:
By default, SAP Data Warehouse Cloud keeps track of objects you’ve accessed, so you can quickly locate those objects again. It also saves previous searches you executed, so you may repeat them. You can now opt out of this object tracking and saving of previous search queries with Privacy settings you can specify in your user profile.
See [Changing SAP Datasphere Settings](1084796d09464e78870f32cab8584dfc.html).
590833988.title: GDPR Data Privacy Compliance

590833989.text:
Data entity is renamed to permissions entity and output is renamed to criteria.
See [Create a "Single Values" Data Access Control](5246328ec59045cb9c2aa693daee2557.html).
590833989.title: Terminology Changes in Data Access Control

590833990.text:
It is now possible to apply one or more data access controls to a view that contains input parameters.
See [Create an Input Parameter in a Graphical View](53fa99ad58c04a1ba3bb87288756dabc.html) and [Apply a Data Access Control to a Graphical or SQL View](8f79fc80d6134a89a03837a205d340cd.html).
590833990.title: Apply Data Access Controls to Views with Input Parameters

590833991.text:
You can now modify tables and views that are used by data access controls and modify data access controls that are attached to views.
See [Modifying Objects That Have Dependent Objects](f315863264db489593c7f54f1f7fd83e.html) and [Process Source Changes in the Data Access Control Editor](3c470e82554145658a5029d7a1dca4a0.html).
590833991.title: Modify Permission Entities and Data Access Controls

590833992.text:
You can now import analysis authorizations defined in SAP BW∕4HANA v2.0 and higher systems into SAP Data Warehouse Cloud from SAP BW∕4HANA Model Transfer Connections, either directly in the wizard when importing a query or in the Data Access Controls app.
See [Importing SAP BW∕4HANA Models](a3d4a2f91bea4810ba8839ff73577dac.html) and [Import SAP BW and SAP BW∕4HANA Analysis Authorizations](f56e4271dc4943aa9f21223ce5c93873.html).
590833992.title: Import SAP BW Analysis Authorizations from SAP BW∕4HANA Model Transfer Connections

590833993.text:
You can now import analysis authorizations defined in SAP BW 7.5 SP16 and higher systems into SAP Data Warehouse Cloud.
See [Import SAP BW and SAP BW∕4HANA Analysis Authorizations](f56e4271dc4943aa9f21223ce5c93873.html).
590833993.title: Import SAP BW Analysis Authorizations

590833994.text:
You can now delete audit logs. Audit logs can consume a large quantity of GB of disk. Deleting them will free up space in your tenant database.
See [Audit Logging](c78a7c2a3cec4b0897db294d74e00d9b.html).
590833994.title: Delete Audit Logs

590833995.text: SAP Datasphere now supports Montenegrin, Macedonian, Kazakh, and Serbian Cyrillic in its menus, buttons, messages, and other elements of the user interface.See [System Requirements and Technical Prerequisites](70ffed417b054b4692458edbd56c90f5.html).
590833995.title: Language Support

590833996.text:
SAP Datasphere has adopted the SAP standard Horizon theme, which offers a modern and fresh look with a new vibrant color palette.
Icons and user interface elements may have changed to adopt this modern design but functionalities remain the same.
590833996.title: New Look and Feel : Horizon Theme

590833997.text:
SAP Business Data Cloud is a fully managed SaaS solution that unifies and governs all SAP data and seamlessly connects with third-party data—giving line-of-business leaders context to make even more impactful decisions.
If your SAP Datasphere tenant is included in an SAP Business Data Cloud formation:
- Other formation tenants are automatically connected to the SAP Datasphere catalog.
- Users with an SAP Business Data Cloud administrator role working in the SAP Business Data Cloud Cockpit can:
- Install pre-packaged intelligent applications to the SAP Datasphere and SAP Analytics Cloud tenants in the formation.
- Activate data packages that make SAP Business Data Cloud data products available to install from the SAP Datasphere catalog.
- Users with an SAP Datasphere catalog administrator role can share SAP Business Data Cloud data products to connected systems.
- Users with an SAP Datasphere modeler role can install SAP Business Data Cloud data products to their spaces.
See [Working with SAP Datasphere in SAP Business Data Cloud](8f9c3725cfe84e08b3e951e7af06ce57.html).
590833997.title: SAP Business Data Cloud

590833998.text:
A change of certificates is going to be rolled out with an upcoming release of SAP Datasphere. Once this change has been implemented, if you’re using an older version of Java VM with SAP Cloud Connector, connections involving SAP Cloud Connector will fail because the new certificates are not trusted. We recommend that you update your Java VM to the latest version as soon as possible to avoid issues with the new certificates.
For more information, see SAP Notes [3369433](https://me.sap.com/notes/3369433) and [3508452](https://me.sap.com/notes/3508452).
590833998.title: Upcoming change of certificates – relevant if you use SAP Cloud Connector

590833999.text:
The new SAP Datasphere homepage gives you access to recent objects, quick actions, and blog posts. You can choose to show, hide, and reorder cards to suit your needs.
See [The SAP Datasphere Homepage](2d85c8b63c454df585099fc93e4f8baf.html).
590833999.title: New Customizable Homepage

590834000.text:
- The list of available options per command has been cleaned up: only command specific options are listed now.
- A new config command regroups previously available commands like host, cache etc…
- You can now log in to multiple tenants in parallel.
For more information, see [Accessing SAP Datasphere via the Command Line](3f9a42ccde6b4b6aba121e2aab79c36d.html).
590834000.title: SAP Datasphere Command Line Interface: Client Module Improvements

590834001.text: The contents of the guide Using SAP Datasphere, SAP BW Bridge in SAP Datasphere are now included in the guide Getting Started With SAP Datasphere, SAP BW Bridge and the topic Importing Entities with Semantics from SAP BW Bridge.
590834001.title: Guide has been removed

590834002.text: SAP Datasphere page titles now give you clear information about the object and application you are working in. You can easily distinguish between open browser tabs, quickly navigate your browser history, and have more meaningful bookmarks.
590834002.title: Informative Web Page Titles

590834003.text: The SAP Datasphere command line interface module has been renamed from dwc to datasphere. The command dwc will be decommissioned at the end of 2023: please use the new datasphere command instead. For more information, see [Accessing SAP Datasphere via the Command Line](3f9a42ccde6b4b6aba121e2aab79c36d.html).
590834003.title: New Name for the SAP Datasphere Command Line Interface

590834004.text:
The documentation process becomes more collaborative, by inviting you to provide feedbacks and contributions to our content through GitHub. The collaboration process is available for the following documentation sets:
- [Acquiring, Preparing, and Modeling Data with SAP Datasphere](b4a5d02cefdf45478e7376860c985202.html)
- [Administering SAP Datasphere](70ee87c19d3b47459ac7f2c8d4fea48a.html)
- [Integrating Data and Managing Spaces in SAP Datasphere](8f98d3c917f94452bafe288055b60b35.html)
For more information, see this [Blog](https://blogs.sap.com/2023/03/28/open-documentation-initiative-for-sap-datasphere-provide-feedback-and-help-us-improve-the-documentation/)
590834004.title: Provide Feedback on Documentation Using the New Collaboration Process

590834005.text:
SAP Datasphere enables a business data fabric architecture that uniquely harmonizes mission-critical data across the organization, unleashing business experts to make the most impactful decisions. It combines previously discrete capabilities into a unified service for data integration, cataloging, semantic modeling, data warehousing, and virtualizing workloads across SAP and non-SAP data.
SAP Datasphere includes the following major new features:
- Replication Flows - Load data with both batch and delta functionality from your source systems with a single flow.
- Catalog - Enable self-service discovery of data and analytic assets, glossaries and terms, and key performance indicators.
- Analytic Models - Combine, filter, and enrich your analytical datasets and dimensions to produce business-ready models optimized for consumption in SAP Analytics Cloud.
For details, see the relevant new feature items in this release.
Our SAP Help documentation is now at [https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_DATASPHERE](https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_DATASPHERE). Your existing bookmarks will be redirected.
590834005.title: SAP Data Warehouse Cloud Is Now SAP Datasphere

590834006.text: You can now use the new  (Feedback) button in the shell bar to share your experience when working with SAP Data Warehouse Cloud and to provide feedback to help us improve your experience. The new button opens a separate browser tab. It is replacing the Send Feedback button that was available on the Home page.
590834006.title: Providing Feedback

590834007.text:
SAP Datasphere now supports Latvian and Estonian in its menus, buttons, messages, and other elements of the user interface.
See [System Requirements and Technical Prerequisites](70ffed417b054b4692458edbd56c90f5.html).
590834007.title: Language Support (Latvian and Estonian)

590834008.text:
The Content Network allows you to deploy many imported objects in your Space. You can now chose to deploy newly imported objects or all imported objects in your Space via the Transport application available in the side navigation area.
See [Importing Content from Another Tenant](b607a12931d74c4a93506ea64c55ab4e.html).
590834008.title: Deploy a wide selection of imported objects

590834009.text:
SAP Data Warehouse Cloud now supports Lithuanian in its menus, buttons, messages, and other elements of the user interface.
See [System Requirements and Technical Prerequisites](70ffed417b054b4692458edbd56c90f5.html).
590834009.title: Language Support (Lithuanian)

590834010.text:
You can now work with SAP Data Warehouse Cloud in the latest version of the Microsoft Edge browser based on Chromium.
See [System Requirements and Technical Prerequisites](70ffed417b054b4692458edbd56c90f5.html) .
590834010.title: Support of Microsoft Edge Browsers Based on Chromium

590834011.text:
Rules and restrictions for technical names in SAP Data Warehouse Cloud have been revised. Certain prefixes are reserved.
See [Rules for Technical Names](982f9a30d4ab49c8b019cfaf3dc08391.html).
590834011.title: Naming Rules and Reserved Prefixes for Technical Names

590834012.text: The former Welcome Guide for SAP Data Warehouse Cloud, SAP BW Bridge is renamed to [Getting Started With SAP Datasphere, SAP BW Bridge](32b4861ce7d94ebd9f5abd854691582f.html)
590834012.title: Guide renamed

590834013.text:
To provide more role-focused information, the former Administration Guide has been split into two guides:
- [Administering SAP Datasphere](70ee87c19d3b47459ac7f2c8d4fea48a.html) - Providing documentation for Administrators.
- [Integrating Data and Managing Spaces in SAP Datasphere](8f98d3c917f94452bafe288055b60b35.html) - Providing documentation for Space Administrators and Data Integrators.
590834013.title: New <cite class="cite">Integrating Data and Managing Spaces</cite> Guide

590834014.text:
The former Modeling Guide is renamed to [Acquiring, Preparing, and Modeling Data with SAP Datasphere](b4a5d02cefdf45478e7376860c985202.html).
The former Welcome Guide is renamed to [Getting Started with SAP Datasphere](2377bb6efedb42d9a6796f0d7d68f1a4.html).
590834014.title: Guides renamed

590834015.text: You can now create, update, and delete space database users via the command line. See [Managing Database Users via the Command Line](cd3b314dd33f407f9ba507dd870ba1f1.html).
590834015.title: Manage Space Database Users via the Command Line

590834016.text: You can now set space priorities and statement limits by group, such as data integration, data modeling, or data consumption, which will ensure a consistent workload distribution for these processes across all spaces and reduce administrative effort. See [Set Priorities and Statement Limits for Spaces or Groups](d66ac1efb5054068a104c4559b72d272.html).
590834016.title: Manage Workload by Group

590834017.text:
To prevent spaces from being deleted unintentionally, deleting a space now moves the space in the new Recycle Bin area, from which you can either restore the space or permanently delete the space from the database.Note
Be aware that deleting spaces via the command line interface continues to work as before, which means that the spaces are permanently deleted right away from the database.
See [Delete Your Space](3eb19b96e6ba41dfbffd759c5c8370bb.html) and [Manage Deleted Spaces in the Recycle Bin](c4e26c09325a45d3ab7011a600c8fc6c.html).
590834017.title: Deleting a Space Moves it in the Recycle Bin

590834018.text:
In consistency with the interface changes, we’ve made changes to the command line interface.The following parameters in the .json file containing the space definition are deprecated and will be removed in future releases:
- priority
- workloadClass.totalStatementMemoryLimit.value
- workloadClass.totalStatementMemoryLimit.unit
- workloadClass.totalStatementThreadLimit.value
- workloadClass.totalStatementThreadLimit.unit
Starting with this version, we recommend that you use these new commands:
- The new datasphere workload list command allows you to list space priorities and statement limits for all spaces and to change them.
- The new datasphere workload update command allows you to change the space priorities and statement limits for one or more spaces.
See [Managing Priorities and Statement Limits for Spaces or Groups via the Command Line](9e3537b72e6c445d9f34201df650735b.html).
590834018.title: Command Line Interface Changes for Setting Space Priorities and Statement Limits for Spaces

590834019.text:
You can now set space priorities and statement limits for all the spaces in the new Workload Management page (in System  Configuration).
In the space details pages, you can view the values set for the space priority and statement limits but you can no longer edit them.
See [Set Priorities and Statement Limits for Spaces or Groups](d66ac1efb5054068a104c4559b72d272.html).
590834019.title: Set Space Priorities and Statement Limits for Spaces in New Workload Management Area

590834020.text: The Space Management now includes the area where administrators can create and manage elastic compute nodes. See [Add Scalable Processing Capacity via Elastic Compute Nodes](1f7c1811d264462fb0cd03e37da07ad7.html).
590834020.title: Now Including Elastic Compute Nodes Area

590834021.text: The total storage available and the amount assigned to and used by spaces are no longer displayed in the bars at the top of the Space Management page but instead in the System Monitor Dashboard tab. See [Monitoring SAP Datasphere](d39b8652994846f9ab80b32fc5b4d671.html).
590834021.title: Space Storage Values Removed From Space Management Tool

590834022.text:
You can now enter descriptive information about your space in a new dedicated field.
See [Create a Space](bbd41b82ad4d4d9ba91341545f0b37e7.html).
590834022.title: Enter a Description for Your Space

590834023.text:
To prevent a space from consuming too many tenant threads, we’ve reduced the range of allowed values for custom configuration statement limits in the Workload Configuration area. You can now enter a percentage between 1% and 70% (or the equivalent number) of the total number of threads available in your tenant. Also, the default value for custom configuration is now 70% instead of 80%.Note
For spaces created before version 2023.04: If you’ve set a thread limit percentage (or number) that is no longer allowed, it is changed to the new default percentage 70% (or the number corresponding to 70% of the total number of threads).
See [Set Priorities and Statement Limits for Spaces or Groups](d66ac1efb5054068a104c4559b72d272.html).
590834023.title: Prevent a Space from Consuming Too Many Threads with Statement Limits

590834024.text:
To prevent statements from consuming too many threads available in your tenant, the value of the parameter ADMISSION CONTROL QUEUE CPU THRESHOLD has been lowered from 90% to 80% for both default and custom configurations of the Workload Configuration area.
Note
This parameter cannot be changed and its threshold value applies to all spaces – including spaces created before this version.
See [Set Priorities and Statement Limits for Spaces or Groups](d66ac1efb5054068a104c4559b72d272.html).
You can now monitor the statements that are queued by viewing the cards dedicated to admission control events in the Dashboard tab of the System Monitor.
See [Monitoring SAP Datasphere](d39b8652994846f9ab80b32fc5b4d671.html).
590834024.title: Prevent Statements from Consuming Too Many Threads with Admission Control Parameters

590834025.text:
A new command dwc dbusers password reset lets administrators and space administrators reset the password of a database user.
See [Manage Spaces and Space Access via the Command Line](5eac5b71e2d34c32b63f3d8d47a0b1d0.html).
590834025.title: Command Line Interface Enhancements: Reset Database User Password

590834026.text:
A new command dwc spaces list lets any user obtain a list of the spaces to which they have access on the tenant.
See [Manage Spaces and Space Access via the Command Line](5eac5b71e2d34c32b63f3d8d47a0b1d0.html).
590834026.title: Command Line Interface Enhancements: List Spaces

590834027.text:
Up to now, a space was automatically locked when it exceeded its allocations of in-memory or disk storage. In addition, certain spaces are now automatically locked when audit logs consume a high amount of GB of the tenant disk.
Also, if you have a Space Administrator role, you can now manually lock a space.
See [Unlock a Locked Space](c05b6a6d06db427dbdd3041d61fd5840.html).
590834027.title: Locking Spaces to Avoid Audit Logs from Consuming Too Much Disk Storage

590834028.text:
You can now log into an OAuth client with the dwc command line interface and run multiple commands without needing to provide passcodes.
In addition the following syntax changes affect existing options and commands:
- -s (--space) is now capitalized to -S
- -sd (--definitions) is now capitalized to -D
- cache-init is changed to cache init and the other cache-* commands also have their hyphens replaced by spaces.
See [Manage Spaces and Space Access via the Command Line](5eac5b71e2d34c32b63f3d8d47a0b1d0.html).
590834028.title: Command Line Interface Enhancements: OAuth Client Login and Syntax Changes

590834029.text:
It is now possible to create, read, update, and delete data access controls using the SAP Data Warehouse Cloud command line interface.
See [The Space Definition File Format](3fcbf619f2774b849fa7df58163b3609.html).
590834029.title: Create, Read, Update, and Delete Data Access Controls using the SAP Data Warehouse Cloud Command Line Interface

590834030.text:
The Space Management page has been refreshed and now loads more quickly and provides more pertinent information, which includes:
- Redesign of the space tiles - You now click Edit on a tile to open a space and you can select several spaces using a checkbox to delete them in one click.
- Used Disk bar - Provides a breakdown of the different types of data consuming disk storage.
- The space status Hot has been renamed to Critical, Green to Healthy, and the status Hibernated has been removed.
See [Creating Spaces and Allocating Resources](2ace657356d54199b0b87d2327b1a70b.html).
590834030.title: Space Management Redesign

590834031.text:
You can now read entity (table and view) definitions (in the standard CSN syntax) from a space with the dwc command line interface, using the -d option. If you include entity definitions in your space definition file when creating or updating a space, then the entities are added to the space.
See [Manage Spaces and Space Access via the Command Line](5eac5b71e2d34c32b63f3d8d47a0b1d0.html).
590834031.title: Read and Write Entities in Spaces from the Command Line

590834032.text:
On rare occasions when the run-time database is not available, an information message is displayed and certain features that depend on the run-time are disabled.
See [Save and Deploy Your Space](95973c709373415ebf42f6446a909924.html).
590834032.title: Information Message and Disabled Features when Run-Time Database is Not Available

590834033.text:
Metric names and values in transformation flow monitoring Run Details now display in simplified format instead of technical wording. For example, EXECUTION_MODE: 0 now shows as Execution Mode: Sequential. You can immediately understand run results without referencing internal documentation.
See [Metrics for Transformation Flows](b42fa5b6f4e04a9491efa9bf7dab0929.html).
590834033.title: Simplified Metric Names for Transformation Flow Monitoring

590834034.text:
Object Store Requests are now metered and consumed in three separate categories: Control Plane, Read, and Write. Each category has its own price per 1,000 requests. Previously, all request types were charged at a single blended rate.
You can view your consumption per category in the Capacity Monitor and in the consumption cards on the Tenant Configuration screen.
See [Configure the Size of Your SAP Datasphere Tenant](33f8ef4ec359409fb75925a68c23ebc3.html)
590834034.title: Object Store Requests Consumed by Category

590834035.text:
More users can now monitor task logs. Access is no longer restricted to global roles. Users with scoped roles may can also monitor task logs when granted access to a space with the required scoped privileges: Data Warehouse General (-R------); Data Warehouse Data Integration (-R------) to view data integration task logs in the Task Logs app; Data Warehouse Data Integration (--U-----) to cancel a task run. The DW Integrator role template, for example, grants these privileges.
See [Reviewing Task Logs](399e52f2b3824026a2c427a346fa792d.html).
590834035.title: Extended Access to Monitoring Task Logs

590834036.text:
X.509 certificate-based authentication is now available for database analysis users. This enhancement strengthens security for technical users by reducing reliance on passwords, while maintaining password-based authentication as the default method.
See [Create a Database Analysis User to Debug Database Issues](c28145bcb76c4415a1ec6265dd2a4c11.html).
590834036.title: Certificate-Based Authentication for Database Analysis Users

590834037.text:
The System Information Bar and Favicon settings have been relocated to the System  Administration  Default Appearance tab.
See [Display Your System Information](6bdd79878afa4ec5bcd9d3502158a06e.html).
590834037.title: Display Your System Information

590834038.text:
In Configuration  Task, you can monitor the size of logs generated by Apache Spark tasks, and configure a deletion task to free up space in your tenant.
See [Delete Task Logs to Reduce Storage Consumption](c6902024ecd74956b4ba2d1c67ccb073.html)
590834038.title: Delete Logs Associated With Apache Spark Tasks

590834039.text:
A new billable metric is available to track Apache Spark resource consumption. Apache Spark compute block-hours measures the allocated memory capacity provisioned for Apache Spark tasks, expressed in compute block-hours.
See [Reviewing Task Logs](399e52f2b3824026a2c427a346fa792d.html).
590834039.title: Apache Spark Metrics Tracking for Resource Consumption

590834040.text:
To enable X.509 client certificate-based authentication for Open SQL database users, you can now upload the required X.509 root certificate (root CA) to SAP Datasphere.
We have introduced the option to select a Purpose when uploading certificates to the SAP Datasphere trust store (under  (System)     (Configuration)   Security  Certificates). For using certificate-based authentication when creating a database user, select X.509 Client (Open SQL). To secure connections, select TLS Server.
See:
- [Manage Certificates](46f5467adc5242deb1f6b68083e72994.html)
- [Create a Database User](798e3fd6707940c3bd2219b2d1ebaac2.html)
590834040.title: Different Purposes Introduced for Certificate Upload

590834041.text: Joule is now integrated with SAP Datasphere, allowing you to use natural language to access system information, manage users and spaces, and navigate data assets and administration tools. This capability simplifies everyday administrative and discovery tasks while respecting existing authorizations, security, and governance settings.
590834041.title: Joule Natural Language Capabilities in SAP Datasphere

590834042.text:
You can now view your SAP Datasphere tenant disk storage capacity and its current utilization in the SAP HANA database via the new Disk Storage Usage card of the System Monitor. This will allow you to protect your tenant by identifying in advance risks of storage-related outages.
See [Monitoring SAP Datasphere](d39b8652994846f9ab80b32fc5b4d671.html).
590834042.title: Monitor Your Tenant Disk Storage Usage

590834043.text:
The configurations of Apache Spark applications that are used by default to run certain tasks in file spaces have changed. For more information, see SAP Note
[3726059](https://launchpad.support.sap.com/#/notes/3726059).See [Create a File Space to Load Data in the Object Store](947444683e524cfd9169d7671b72ba0c.html).
590834043.title: Changed Default Task Assignment for File Spaces

590834044.text:
Limits to the amount of compute resources that Apache Spark applications can consume when running tasks are set with configurations. In addition to using the provided configurations, which are applied by default to new file spaces, you can now change the default configuration for a task activity in each file space, and create your own configurations.
Note
As newly provided default configurations for task activities may allocate fewer resources than those used in previous versions (see [3726059](https://launchpad.support.sap.com/#/notes/3726059)), tasks might run more slowly even though they consume less compute. If these defaults don’t meet your needs, you can change the default configuration for a task activity in each file space.
See [Set Limits to Compute Resources for File Spaces](0cf1015768e44324b4088da4c5ebd8ca.html).
590834044.title: Change Default Configurations for Tasks in File Spaces and Create your Own Configurations

590834045.text:
If your SAP Datasphere tenant is enabled for job & automation monitoring in SAP Cloud ALM, you can now monitor the child tasks of the task chains that are run in SAP Datasphere, from the Job & Automation Monitoring app in SAP Cloud ALM.
See [Job & Automation Monitoring](https://help.sap.com/docs/cloud-alm/applicationhelp/job-automation-monitoring) in the SAP Cloud ALM - Application Help.
590834045.title: Monitor Child Tasks of Task Chains in SAP Cloud ALM

590834046.text:
There is no longer any limit to the number of spaces you can assign a user to via scoped roles.
See [Create a Scoped Role to Assign Privileges to Users in Spaces](b5c4e0b6c462414783ebbfc053815521.html).
590834046.title: Assign More Than 100 Spaces to Users

590834047.text: The Business Builder is deprecated and will not receive further updates. We recommend that you migrate your consumption models to analytic models, which are now the preferred way to expose data to SAP Analytics Cloud and other clients, tools and apps.
590834047.title: Deprecation of the Business Builder

590834048.text:
The runtime of the data preview in the Business Builder has been changed to align with the data preview of the analytic model.
This gives you all the options that you have in the data preview of the analytic model.
The preview is available for consumption models, but not for perspectives anymore. Also, the preview of business entities and authorization scenarios is no longer available. You also can't save your data preview anymore.
590834048.title: Data Preview in Business Builder

590834049.text:
You can now choose on measure level if null values shall be treated as NULL or zero in the data preview and story consumption.
See [Define Measures](903acb8d378d4984af8ad4f694d56529.html).
590834049.title: Display of NULL Values

590834050.text:
You can now add one or more external parent-child hierarchies which have been defined in the source view in the Data Builder.
See [Add an External Hierarchy](1ec95b0f18824586bc330b8c445278a8.html).
590834050.title: External Hierarchy

590834051.text:
Users can review release state information for SAP Datasphere views. The release states help catalog users understand the view's lifecycle stage. They can also filter to find views at different release states in their lifecycle.
See [Catalog Asset Details](afccc581146542c485a52563167e23cc.html).
590834051.title: Release State Metadata for SAP Datasphere Views

590834052.text:
Data products sometimes have schema changes that aren't updated in the installed versions. As a result, installed data products can have inconsistencies when compared to the corresponding catalog version.
You can check for schema inconsistencies on the Data Product Access page. Once you identify the affected data products, you can resolve the inconsistencies by updating their installations.
See [Resolving Schema Inconsistencies](f4d469b644af4c30b8cd071d07a2babc.html).
590834052.title: Manual Check for Data Product Schema Changes

590834053.text:
The workflow for accessing data products has been streamlined across SAP Business Data Cloud. You'll now be able to send access requests for data products, track their statuses, and receive timely notifications when a request is approved or rejected.
See [Obtaining Access to Data Products](998fb5f447d04021baf497375261c9d1.html)
590834053.title: Data Product Access Request Management

590834054.text:
You can now connect SAP Datasphere to external applications that offer a REST API by creating custom connection types.
A custom connection type is a reusable blueprint that maps external API resources to structured entities, allowing you to load compatible JSON-based data from third-party systems or customer-built REST APIs into the SAP Datasphere object store using replication flows.
Custom connection types extend standard SAP Datasphere-managed connectivity when predefined connection types do not exist. They are available in spaces with storage type SAP HANA Data Lake Files (file spaces). Connections created from a custom connection type are independent of the connection type, meaning that later changes to the connection type do not affect existing connections.
See:
- [Creating a Custom Connection Type](9c582ca295164a538cb61b7e7beb6719.html)
- [Create a Connection from a Custom Connection Type](d0653d37167a49679d0a3e909547a674.html)
- [Rest API Custom Connection Sources for Replication Flows](cc0fad818e9b4d409c43969195d3fd82.html)
590834054.title: Connect to External REST APIs via Custom Connections

590834055.text:
The new task chain monitor graphical view feature provides a visual view of a task chain that is representative of the data builder editor.
This helps identify the flow of task chains and provides color coded object level status of tasks in the task chain.
See [Monitoring Task Chains](4142201ec1aa49faad89a688a2f1852c.html).
590834055.title: Monitor Task Chain Status with a Graphical Display

590834056.text:
The BD Administrator can now define system mappings to help your transported content automatically connect to the correct data products. When you import a content package installed from an SAP Business Data Cloud data product into an SAP Datasphere tenant, SAP Datasphere will automatically connect to the correct data-product provider system instance.
For more information, see [System Mapping for Content Transport Between SAP Datasphere Tenants](https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_BUSINESS_DATA_CLOUD/f7acf8c9dad54e99b5ce5ebc633ed8e1/4a4024c409ef427ebe285b8e60a9e58a.html) in SAP Business Data Cloud documentation.
590834056.title: Automatic Data-Product Provider Connection During Content Transport

590834057.text:
You can now restart replication flow objects via API.
See [Controlling Replication Flows via API](5e60730b5b4c45f49e261af6fdaad72b.html).
590834057.title: Restart Replication Flow Objects via API

590834058.text:
You can now start, stop, pause, and resume replication flows (and pause and resume individual replication flow objects) via API.
See [Controlling Replication Flows via API](5e60730b5b4c45f49e261af6fdaad72b.html).
590834058.title: New Replication Flow Monitoring APIs

590834059.text:
When issues occur in analytical models or exposed views, related SAP Analytics Cloud stories can be displayed in the impact summary and pipeline graph. This enables you to identify affected analytics content, navigate directly to impacted objects, and gain visibility into downstream business impact from a single location.
See [Viewing SAP Analytics Cloud Objects in the Data Pipeline Analyzer](55d92f3d718d4246bca5782325b078b2.html).
590834059.title: Data Pipeline Analyzer Displays Impact on related SAP Analytics Cloud Stories

590834060.text:
We've standardized size displays across all monitors using a dynamic decimal format for improved readability and consistency.
With dynamic scaling, values are automatically adjusted so they remain between 1 and 1,000. Instead of displaying very large or very small numbers, the unit changes automatically:
- KB for sizes greater than 1,000 bytes
- MB for sizes greater than 1,000,000 bytes
- GB for sizes greater than 1,000,000,000 bytes
- TB for sizes greater than 1,000,000,000,000 bytes, etc...
This makes size values easier to read and compare across SAP Datasphere.
590834060.title: Consistent Size Display Across All Monitors

590834061.text:
When using a local table (file) as the source in a replication flow, you can now use the Initial and Delta and Delta Only load types in addition to the already supported Initial Only load type. To use delta load types, delta capture must be enabled on the source table.
See [SAP Datasphere Local Table (File) Sources for Replication Flows](bdff6b91cf4b44f895429c23566b3ea0.html).
590834061.title: Initial and Delta and Delta Only Load Types Now Supported for Local Table (File) as Source

590834062.text:
You can now define and use input and output parameters in API tasks. This provides more flexibility and allows for better reuse when working with API tasks. In this context, we've also added the GET and DELETE methods for API tasks in synchronous mode and the use of an ID output parameter for status retrieval for API tasks in asynchronous mode.
See:
- [Run API Tasks in a Task Chain](9a8489ed7443436197fbd8b8ffba61ab.html)
- [Using Parameters in API Tasks](6b6d6004c2c94a71a8a732718fed100c.html)
590834062.title: Use Input and Output Parameters in API Tasks

590834063.text:
You can now detect and apply compatible source schema changes for replication flows that use SAP ABAP (SLT) sources targets without reinitializing the replication flow. Supported changes include adding nullable non-key columns. When schema changes are detected, review and selectively apply them in the replication flow editor before resuming replication. See:
- [Configure the Run Settings of a Replication Flow](3f5ba0c5ae3944c1b7279bb989a2a5b5.html)
- [Modify Replication Flow Object Schemas and Settings](a24c71f3ba7548909534d4cb52cefbfc.html)
590834063.title: Apply Compatible Source Schema Changes Without Reinitializing Replication Flows

590834064.text:
Replication flows now support compatible "add column" schema changes from ABAP SLT sources to Local Table (file) targets. You can apply new nullable non-key columns to the target without reinitializing the replication flow.
See [Modify Replication Flow Object Schemas and Settings](a24c71f3ba7548909534d4cb52cefbfc.html).
590834064.title: Support for Schema Changes from ABAP SLT Sources to Local Table File Targets

590834065.text:
You can now select which runtime settings are included when a replication flow is exported using the Transport app. The following settings can be marked for transport: Delta Load Run, Delta Load Frequency, Thread Limit for Initial Load, Email Notification Configuration, and Capture Source Schema Changes.
See [Working With Existing Replication Flow Runs](da62e1ee746448e8bc043e1be4377cbe.html).
590834065.title: Transporting Runtime Settings for Replication Flows

590834066.text:
You can now use MySQL and the corresponding connection type to add sources to replication flows.
See:
- [MySQL Sources for Replication Flows](4fe921866ee44d6e8bb13d92f378d3a2.html)
- [MySQL Connections](520a2601fd7a45f084e5ed1d30c6ebfa.html)
590834066.title: MySQL Sources for Replication Flows

590834067.text:
You can now use the Workload Identity Federation authentication type to let replication flows securely access Google BigQuery with short-lived access tokens.
See:
- [Google BigQuery Connections](30ed77de13864368bdc596099b37ed70.html)
- [Configuring Workload Identity Federation for Google BigQuery Connections](7962a49923d84644910b1c6001df0145.html)
590834067.title: Use Short-Lived Access Tokens for Google BigQuery Connections

590834068.text:
You can now use authentication type OAuth 2.0 with the Client Credentials with X.509 Client Certificate grant type for SAP ABAP (on-premise), SAP S/4HANA On-Premise, SAP ECC, and SAP BW connections. This certificate-based grant type is the most secure option for the connection types and is selected by default when you choose OAuth 2.0 as the authentication type.
This authentication type is available for connections that use Cloud Connector. For SAP ABAP (on-premise) and SAP S/4HANA On-Premise, the OAuth 2.0 authentication type with client credentials was introduced in an earlier version of SAP Datasphere. For SAP BW and SAP ECC connections, OAuth 2.0 authentication is new and supports both grant types: client credentials and client credentials with X.509 client certificate.
Note the following for all connection types:
- Remote tables are not supported with the OAuth 2.0 authentication type. This also applies to model import for SAP S/4HANA connections.
- For SAP BW and SAP ECC connections, only replication flows are supported.
- For SAP ABAP and SAP S/4HANA On-Premise connections, replication flows and data flows are supported.
- When you change an existing connection from basic authentication to authentication type OAuth 2.0, remote tables are disabled. For SAP BW and SAP ECC connections, data flows are also disabled.
See:
- [SAP ABAP Connections](a75c1aacf951449ba3b740c7e46da3a9.html)
- [SAP BW Connections](e589041e80264f43b6c209c407336376.html)
- [SAP ECC Connections](e546ccd61af54bf49a0f531a43fe0961.html)
- [SAP S/4HANA On-Premise Connections](a49a1e3cc50f4af89711d8306bdd8f26.html)
590834068.title: Use OAuth 2.0 Authentication with X.509 Client Certificate for ABAP-based Connections

590834069.text: To improve overall performance of task chain runs, we have reduced the idle times between task runs.
590834069.title: Performance Improvement for Task Chains

590834070.text:
You can now use the Initial Only load type when replicating data to a local table (file) target with delta capturing switched off. This applies to object store sources (Amazon Simple Storage Service, Google Cloud Storage, Microsoft Azure Data Lake Gen2, SAP HANA Cloud Data Lake Files), HANA views, and all other sources that support initial-only load.
See [SAP Datasphere Targets for Replication Flows](12c45eb2659f4069b29ef4d69bdd9070.html).
590834070.title: Initial Only Load Type for Local Table (File) Targets

590834071.text:
You can now centrally per tenant create and manage reusable mail lists for email notifications across task chains, notification tasks, and replication flows. This feature streamlines notification management and enhances data protection by preventing exposure of personal email addresses to unauthorized users.
Existing lists of recipient email addresses in your tenant have been migrated to corresponding reusable mail lists. These lists are assigned to the task chains or replication flows for which they were originally created. The names of the new mailing lists are generated as follows:
- For task chains and notification tasks: <space_technical_name>:<task_chain_technical_name>
- For replication flows: <space_technical_name>:<replication_flow_technical_name>
See:
- [Configure Email Notification for Task Chains and Notification Tasks](7ff6a4e584a345a88d002c18c1fc321e.html)
- [Configure Email Notification for Replication Flow Failure at Object Level](5dc4db23d3894b10aca6ade3c666554d.html)
590834071.title: Centralized Reusable Mail Lists for Task Chain and Replication Flow Notifications

590834072.text:
If your filter is defined on a column where values are of data type "Date" or "Datetime", you can add a time zone using the selector. A suffix with the time zone in brackets is then added to the column name in the deletion filter.
See:
- [Controlling Deletion of Local Table Records](2a59b7142e1b4d478b0bf4063084261e.html)
- [Delete Data From Your Local Tables (File)](872ad509995a451890bf8b80b73ec0e6.html)
590834072.title: Define a Time Zone When Deleting Records With Filters on Date or Datetime Columns

590834073.text: You can now apply and clear column filters on Data Integration Monitor overview pages. Active filter conditions are displayed directly in the user interface for improved visibility.
590834073.title: Add or Clear Filters on Columns in Data Integration Monitor

590834074.text:
You can now use the Initial and Delta and Delta Only load types for Oracle sources. Previously, Oracle sources supported only the Initial Only load type.
See [Select Source and Target Connections for Replication Flows](10891192186c4920b08939a7b46adc79.html).
590834074.title: Oracle Sources Now Support Delta Load Types

590834075.text:
You can now trace personal and sensitive personal data in your objects. Objects containing personal data are automatically tagged in the task chain editors, and are displayed in a new column "Tags" in the Local Tables, Views and Remote Tables monitors.
See [Creating a Task Chain](d1afbc2b9ee84d44a00b0b777ac243e1.html), [Monitoring Remote Tables](4dd95d7bff1f48b399c8b55dbdd34b9e.html), [Monitoring Local Tables](374046156e5b47599fc9b96c8c3a4dce.html), [Persisting and Monitoring Views](9af04c990f294fd28c00f46763dd8b0d.html).
590834075.title: Data Privacy and Protection－Personal Data and Sensitive Personal Data Tagging in Monitors and Task Chain Editor

590834076.text:
When using the OAuth 2.0 authentication type with SAP SuccessFactors connections, you can now use automated, dynamic generation and rotation of SAML assertions to avoid manual efforts that have been required before.
For dynamically generating SAML assertions, SAP Cloud Identity Services (IAS) is used as Identity Provider.
See:
- [SAP SuccessFactors Connections](39df02030d4b411487bacecf9afea4e8.html)
- [Configuring Dynamic Generation of SAML Assertions for SAP SuccessFactors Connections](63c8260a7f574e6e8e3c386656c93b00.html)
Note
Access to APIs based on HTTP Basic Authentication will be deleted on November 12, 2027. We strongly recommend to adopt the OAuth 2.0 authentication type for your connections.
For more information, see:
- [Deprecation of Basic Authentication for APIs](https://help.sap.com/doc/62fddbd651204629b46bbccbabf886ba/cloud/en-US/fcc05a902b4140e585d968c2fe4a96bc.html) in SAP SuccessFactors What's New Viewer
- SAP Note [3774454](https://me.sap.com/notes/3774454)
590834076.title: Dynamically Generate SAML Assertions for SAP SuccessFactors Connections

590834077.text:
You can now use Local Table (Files) as source objects in replication flows. This allows you to replicate data from a Local Table (File) to supported SAP and non-SAP target systems without re-extracting the data from the original source.
See [SAP Datasphere Local Table (File) Sources for Replication Flows](bdff6b91cf4b44f895429c23566b3ea0.html).
590834077.title: Local Table (Files) as Replication Flow Sources

590834078.text:
SAP HANA Cloud migrates its server certificates to DigiCert TLS RSA4096 Root G5 by end of November 2026 and will switch exclusively to a G5 certificate chain in all productive landscapes following a dedicated migration schedule.
Action: If you have connections pointing to SAP HANA Cloud, you must ensure that the new DigiCert TLS RSA4096 Root G5 (DigiCertTLSRSA4096RootG5.crt.pem) is uploaded to the SAP Datasphere trust store (under  (System)     (Configuration)   Security  Certificates).
See:
- SAP Note [3399573](https://me.sap.com/notes/3399573)
- Prerequisites for SAP HANA Cloud in [SAP HANA Connections](e6b63f176d3640609adcf06297fb37e9.html#loioe6b63f176d3640609adcf06297fb37e9)
590834078.title: SAP HANA Cloud Connections: DigiCert TLS RSA4096 Root G5 Certificate Required

590834079.text:
You can now use all supported load types when replicating data from SAP BW/ECC sources. In addition to Initial Only, SAP BW/ECC sources now support Initial and Delta and Delta Only load types.
See [Select Source and Target Connections for Replication Flows](10891192186c4920b08939a7b46adc79.html).
590834079.title: SAP BW/ECC Sources Now Support Delta Load Types

590834080.text:
From the Local table monitor, you can display the partitioning details of your local tables.
See [Monitoring Your Partitions](3c9de9eb77e649a98450f4fd67a5f7ba.html).
590834080.title: Monitor Your Partition Details

590834081.text:
You can now pause and resume replication flows and individual replication objects as well as other actions already available via the command line.
See: [Running and Managing Tasks via the Command Line](2b26a31f197444dea314495bc0008eae.html).
590834081.title: Additional Replication Flow Actions on the Command Line

590834082.text:
Leverage AI to gain deeper insights into your data pipeline. You can generate a Business Summary to quickly understand how your pipeline is structured, or create an Errors and Impacts Summary to identify issues and pinpoint any blocked data movements.
See [Generate Summaries of the Data Pipeline Analyzer With AI](1e72ea2b540f412c8bcd5d4751560ebc.html).
590834082.title: Generate a Business Summary and an Errors and Impacts Summary With AI

590834083.text: Transformation flows load data without intermediate data copying when accessing delta share tables from BDC Foundation Services or Databricks. You benefit from improved performance and reduced storage overhead by reading data directly from delta sharing sources through the native client instead of copying to a file space.
590834083.title: Direct Delta Sharing Client Integration for Transformation Flows

590834084.text:
You can now use Cloud Connector for object store connections and Microsoft Azure SQL Database.
Cloud Connector acts as a reverse invoke proxy and routes traffic through a TLS tunnel, allowing you to use replication flows to replicate data from or, if applicable, write data to cloud object stores and Microsoft Azure SQL Database without having to expose public endpoints.
See:
- [Amazon Simple Storage Service Connections](a7b660a0a4ef4a4fbee57b44f5b2147d.html)
- [Google Cloud Storage Connections](aec242c29188408c9ebe1a3ab63ce28b.html)
- [Microsoft Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 Connections](cd06b3c5ab5147c0905e3fa8abd13eb1.html)
- [Microsoft Azure SQL Database Connections](46343fc1c4544fa9a075d97f84d39826.html)
- [Microsoft OneLake Connections](057fa4b51c734e679dd70eec9514839d.html)
590834084.title: Cloud Connector Support for Cloud Object Store and Microsoft Azure SQL Database Connections

590834085.text:
You can now view a summary of your replication flow performance, including data volume and transfer speed, to better monitor and understand the performance of your replication flow.
See [Understanding Replication Flow Metrics](39c116da4e5a41629040f38a907091ce.html).
590834085.title: View Performance Summary for Replication Flows

590834086.text: You can cancel transformation flows with Apache Spark runtime while exporting a local table used as a source. Users can now immediately stop running flows without waiting for export completion, improving control over long-running data operations and reducing unnecessary resource consumption.
590834086.title: Cancel Transformation Flows During Table Export

590834087.text:
You can now create connections to Snowflake and use them as source for replication flows.
You can configure Cloud Connector for Snowflake with Cloud Connector acting as a reverse invoke proxy routing traffic through a TLS tunnel. This allows you to replicate data from Snowflake databases that don't necessarily have public endpoints.
See [Snowflake Connections](d9ead8bb44ac456d99a141b4e3f5e973.html).
590834087.title: Connection Type Snowflake

590834088.text:
You can now schedule replication flows with delta-enabled objects or use them in task chains by setting Delta Load Run to At Scheduled Time. With this setting, replication flows process available delta records and complete after each run.
See [Configure the Run Settings of a Replication Flow](3f5ba0c5ae3944c1b7279bb989a2a5b5.html).
590834088.title: Run Replication Flows with Delta Load Objects at Scheduled Times

590834089.text:
Use the  Download Spark Driver Logs button for transformation flows on file and local tables (file) to get the Spark driver logs as a .txt file. This is useful to better understand your runs and for debugging purposes. To download this file, you must have the DWC_RUNTIME privilege added to your DW Administrator role or custom role.
See :
- [Monitoring Flows](b661ea0766a24c7d839df950330a89fd.html)
- [Monitoring Local Tables (File)](6b2d0073a8684ee6a59d6f47d00ec895.html)
590834089.title: Download Spark Driver Logs

590834090.text:
You can now use SAP ECC and SAP BW systems as sources for replication flows and replicate data from these systems using the Operational Data Provisioning framework.
See:
- [SAP ECC and SAP BW Sources for Replication Flows](c7accb3184274e1eb25c582bf3235789.html)
- [SAP BW Connections](e589041e80264f43b6c209c407336376.html)
- [SAP ECC Connections](e546ccd61af54bf49a0f531a43fe0961.html)
590834090.title: SAP ECC and SAP BW Supported as Source Connections for Replication Flows

590834091.text:
You can now use the following properties when your Cloud Data Integration connection is enabled for remote tables:
- Subscription Mode: For high-volume data sources, using the Stateless mode can avoid errors related to a filled persistence data store in SAP HANA Cloud that can occur with the default Stateful mode.
- Page Size: To increase stability and performance when reading the data, you can increase the maximum size of each page returned for the CDI remote source (default is 10000).
When you have selected a Data Provisioning Agent to enable remote tables, the properties are available in the Configure Advanced Properties step (when creating connections) or in the Show Advanced Properties section (when editing connection).
See [Cloud Data Integration Connections](cd33107246f446628f9baff56faf5a1b.html).
590834091.title: Advanced Properties for Cloud Data Integration Connections Using Data Provisioning Agent

590834092.text:
The API endpoint /dsc/providers/:providerIdentifier/assignUsers is available to assign and activate data provider memberships.
For more information, see the API documentation on the [SAP Business Accelerator Hub](https://api.sap.com/api/DataSharingCockpit/overview).
You can also use the command datasphere marketplace providers assign-users in the SAP Datasphere command line interface.
See [Managing Data Marketplace Data Providers via the Command Line](ca9f910607da4a9e8a2385f655edab95.html).
590834092.title: New API Endpoint and New Command for Data Providers

590834093.text:
You can now install the same data product into multiple target spaces using different scoped licenses, each with its own activation key.
See [Changing License Scope](7890c5b332504a4b954c981b5f871e49.html).
590834093.title: Multiple Scoped License Installations

590834094.text:
You can use hana.SMALLINT and hana.TINYINT data types in your custom data products for SAP Business Data Cloud.
See :
- [Creating Data Products for SAP Business Data Cloud](b07e95d07a1e4569b87d9bb57b732bcf.html)
- [Data Types Supported By Local Tables (File)](2f39104e5bd847919b8daee1580c4f68.html)
590834094.title: New Supported Data Types for Custom Data Products

590834095.text:
Create Catena-X data products with external delivery to bring data from the Catena-X network within SAP Datasphere.
See [Creating Data Products for Catena-X](806c56d8a32b48d5a834107543351c20.html).
590834095.title: Catena-X Data Products with External Delivery

590834096.text:
With the new Expression Evaluator task you can evaluate expressions using input and output parameters within task chains. Use it to transform data, perform calculations, and create conditional values that can be reused as input parameters in subsequent tasks.
See [Run Expression Evaluator Tasks in a Task Chain](5064ede215654f2eb6e18b86a29dfab5.html).
590834096.title: Expression Evaluator Task for Dynamic Task Chain Calculation

590834097.text:
Information-sensitive data is now visually highlighted in the analytic model with the tags Sensitive Personal Data and Personal Data.
This improves data security awareness and compliance.
590834097.title: Tags for Sensitive Data in Analytic Models

590834098.text:
In the data preview of an analytic model, you can export the data as an Excel or CSV file. This enables you to share the intermediate results with colleagues, and to validate the calculations and measures.
See: [Preview Data in an Analytic Model](9f1fa73a33424cbe9bac3064702c0dbd.html)
590834098.title: Export Data of Data Preview

590834099.text:
You can now generate SQL code in transformation flows on file by prompting the built-in SAP Business AI. You can create a view from scratch by specifying your sources and what you want to output or modify existing SQL code. CTEs (Common Table Expressions) WITH clauses are supported.
See :
- [Generate SQL Code with AI in a File Space](15452a78b52749b59b0f133c981f17ab.html)
- [Create a SQL View in a Transformation Flow on File](06c4e72bcbee46568be499c77a3a0d00.html)
590834099.title: AI SQL Code Generation in Transformation Flows on File

590834100.text:
If your SAP Datasphere is part of an SAP Business Data Cloud formation, you can now install multiple major versions of intelligent content on the same source system. Use this to safely test and migrate workflows to new major versions without disrupting existing processes.
All major versions use the source system's ingestion and preparation spaces, but each version creates its own model space to contain its data products. The spaces are identified by version numbers.
See [Installing Intelligent Content](344999cbd4ff4d8188fb67b4ca6ea33f.html).
590834100.title: Side-by-side Major Version Installation of Intelligent Content

590834101.text:
Trace personal and sensitive personal data installed from an SAP BDC data product as it is processed in transformation flows. Flow operators display the personal data tags on relevant columns and these tags are inherited by target tables to which personal data is written.
See :
- [Creating a Transformation Flow](f7161e6c20204672ac4a6d90c81762e4.html)
- [Creating a Transformation Flow in a File Space](b917baf0431343bea8381fa37e12eeb8.html)
- [Modeling with Personal Data](fd0d4e63b73c4b8bb2efbd2399a9f9b9.html)
590834101.title: Data Protection: Tracking of Personal and Sensitive Data in Transformation Flows in SAP HANA Runtime or Apache Spark Runtime

590834102.text: You can now change the protect data export configuration for analytic models that are part of Intelligent applications.
590834102.title: Protect Data Export for Analytic Models

590834103.text:
Simplify complex star-schema data models with the new Flatten operator in Apache Spark transformation flows. The operator automatically joins tables to create flattened views, streamlining data preparation for machine learning, AI, and analytics use cases.
See [Creating a Flatten Operator](34f48faf744a429f9db581e5b43b920a.html).
590834103.title: Flatten Operator for Transformation Flows on File

590834104.text:
When creating a text association, you can now specify a text column from your fact or dimension to provide Fallback Text in the event that no translation is available for the selected record/language in the text entity.
See [Create an Association to Define a Semantic Relationship Between Entities](66c6998af9974dac8f54a46515777560.html)
590834104.title: Fallback Text for Attribute Translation

590834105.text:
You can now clearly differentiate in the different areas of SAP Datasphere if your object is a local table (stored in a standard space) or a local table (file) stored in a file space.
See :
- [Creating a Local Table](2509fe4d86aa472b9858164b55b38077.html)
- [Creating a Local Table (File)](d21881b121bc4703861be6ead4aea2ab.html)
590834105.title: Improved User Experience Through Clear Differentiation Between Local Tables and Local Tables (File)

590834106.text:
If your SAP Datasphere is part of an SAP Business Data Cloud formation, you can now install intelligent content that combines data products from multiple systems. Each source system creates (or re-uses) its own ingestion and preparation spaces to contain its data products, and an additional cross-source space is created that combines data from all the source systems. The source-specific and cross-source spaces are identified by aliases.
See [Reviewing Installed Intelligent Content](644648756d334daaaf35d4fc9a0feeda.html).
590834106.title: Intelligent Content that Combines Data Products from Multiple Systems

590834107.text:
Automatically flag and correct erroneous records without interrupting your transformation flow. When Support Data Validation is enabled on a Python operator, flagged records are captured in a dedicated Data Remediation table. Review issues in the Data Integration monitor, correct values individually or in bulk, and reprocess corrected records in the next run. The system tracks record status and automatically merges corrections back into your target table.
See [Resolving Erroneous Records Using the Data Remediation Table](0cbcc49d36f345208ffd97d3695a141e.html).
590834107.title: Resolve Erroneous Records with the Data Remediation Table

590834108.text:
New validation rules can help optimize and ensure the completeness of your translations.
See [Validating View Data](ed4063dc7f53436d806ea48f2fd3949a.html).
590834108.title: Data Validation: Text Entities

590834109.text:
You can now list, create, read, update, delete, and export packages via the datasphere command line interface.
See [Managing Packages via the Command Line](9dfeea1833ce4b61a3304e0dbb4468b8.html).
590834109.title: Manage Packages via the Command Line

590834110.text:
In the table editor, you can enable deletion vectors to optimize how delete and update operations are handled in local tables (file).
See [Creating a Local Table (File)](d21881b121bc4703861be6ead4aea2ab.html)
590834110.title: Enable Delta Vector for Your Local Table (File)

590834111.text:
To improve scalability and reduce operational overhead, you can now select a new partition type: Dynamic Range. This option monitors incoming data in the “OTHERS” partition and automatically creates new partitions as needed. It ensures efficient data distribution, maintains optimal query performance, and seamlessly adapts to increasing data volumes.
See [Partitioning Local Tables](03191f36e9144b2aaa47b8c9eea039c1.html)
590834111.title: New Partition Type Available For Your Local Tables: Dynamic Range

590834112.text:
Track and resolve errors automatically in transformation flows on file by enabling Support Data Validation on the Python operator to generate an error tracking table during deployment. The system captures failed records with error status and detailed error messages, enabling iterative data quality improvement and seamless reprocessing of erroneous records without manual intervention.
See [Creating a Python Operator](a747acf9d96b450da4b802b80e05a896.html).
590834112.title: Automated Error Tracking for Transformation Flows on File

590834113.text:
- Insert records from delta-enabled source tables to non-delta targets.
- For initial-only loads, automatically clear the target table data before each run by enabling Delete All Before Loading.
Transformation flows on file support two new features. You can now: See [Creating a Transformation Flow in a File Space](b917baf0431343bea8381fa37e12eeb8.html).
590834113.title: Delta Capture Flag Handling for Transformation Flows on File

590834114.text:
If your SAP Datasphere is part of an SAP Business Data Cloud formation, you can now install intelligent content that combines data products from multiple systems. Each source system creates (or re-uses) its own ingestion and preparation spaces to contain its data products, and an additional cross-source preparation space is created that combines data from all source systems. The source-specific and cross-source spaces are identified by aliases.
See [Reviewing Installed Intelligent Content](644648756d334daaaf35d4fc9a0feeda.html).
590834114.title: Install Intelligent Content that Combines Data Products from Multiple Source Systems

590834115.text:
New filter options now allow you to filter your text data based on partial matches:
- startswith(<field>,'<value>') - String value starts with
- endswith(<field>,'<value>') - String value ends with
- contains(<field>,'<value>') - String value contains
See [Consuming Data via the OData API](7a453609c8694b029493e7d87e0de60a.html).
590834115.title: OData Consumption API: Partial String Filtering

590834116.text:
The Runtime Metrics tool now allows you to analyze the performance of a view including the underlying source objects in the lineage graph. This allows you to refine your metrics for more precises analysis.
See [Analyzing View Performance](6e9ba26e11dc4062801c1dfcbf9a1072.html).
590834116.title: Analyze the Lineage Graph of a View with Runtime Metrics

590834117.text:
When you use an analytic model as a source for another analytic model, you can now customize its variables and
- renamed them
- change their default value
- use them in the new analytic model, including restricted measures and calculations.
590834117.title: Variables in Analytic Models

590834118.text:
The Runtime Metrics tool now allows you the flexibility to set the metrics for the entire main view or review the metrics of just the remote tables in the view. This allows you to refine your metrics for more precises analysis.
See [Analyzing View Performance](6e9ba26e11dc4062801c1dfcbf9a1072.html).
590834118.title: Analyze Views with Extended Runtime Metrics

590834119.text: In the analytic model, you can now control whether currency conversion applies a shift of the decimal points.
590834119.title: Shift for Currency Conversion

590834120.text:
If you have defined multiple primary keys, you can change the index type in the Local Table editor to optimize the performance in very large volume scenarios.
See [Columns](8f0f40df2ed34035b8b5837897205ee6.html)
590834120.title: Change the Primary Key Index Type in Local Tables

590834121.text: For calculated and restricted measures,and for calculated and restricted structures, the functions YTD, QTD, MTD and %GrandTotal are now supported.
590834121.title: More Functions for Calculated and Restricted Measures

590834122.text:
Local tables (file) can be shared between file spaces (also known as SAP HANA Data Lake Files).
See [Creating a Transformation Flow in a File Space](b917baf0431343bea8381fa37e12eeb8.html).
590834122.title: Sharing Local Tables (File) Between File Spaces

590834123.text:
You can now generate SQL code by prompting the built-in SAP Business AI. You can create a view from scratch by specifying your sources and what you want to output or modify existing SQL code.
See [Generate SQL Code with AI](d1530656d42f44f68b6265666ec35531.html).
590834123.title: AI SQL Code Generation

590834124.text:
You can now trace personal and sensitive personal data installed from an SAP BDC data product across the entities that consume it.
Columns containing personal data are automatically tagged in the Catalog, and these tags are visible in the table and view editors. As subsequent entities consume this data, they inherit these tags, which are also visible in the Data Viewer and in the impact and lineage analysis diagram.
See: [Modeling with Personal Data](fd0d4e63b73c4b8bb2efbd2399a9f9b9.html).
590834124.title: Personal Data and Sensitive Personal Data Tagging

590834125.text:
You can now see data access controls applied to the sources of your view in a subsection Applied via Sources under the list of Data Access Controls in the side panel.
See [Apply a Data Access Control to a Graphical or SQL View](8f79fc80d6134a89a03837a205d340cd.html).
590834125.title: Visibility of Data Access Controls Applied to Sources

590834126.text:
You can now export and import intelligent lookups either manually as JSON files or via the Transport app.
See:
- [Importing and Exporting Objects in CSN/JSON Files](f8ff0628c9fc49229740ffcd4d20e9aa.html)
- [Transporting Content Between Tenants](df12666cf98e41248ef2251c564b0166.html)
590834126.title: Export and Import Intelligent Lookups as JSON Files or via the Transport App

590834127.text:
The navigation in SAP Datasphere has been redesigned, with applications now reorganized based on their functions. Additionally, the About dialog has now moved under the user profile:
See :
- [Navigating in SAP Datasphere](bd79b74face14b17a4cfa844a2fd36c7.html)
- [Changing SAP Datasphere Settings](1084796d09464e78870f32cab8584dfc.html)
590834127.title: Side Bar Navigation Reorganized

590834128.text:
You can now view detailed storage usage for each file space (spaces with a storage type of SAP HANA Data Lake Files) directly from the space page.
See [Monitor Your Space Storage Consumption](94fe6c13f6a340288cd50ee355566591.html).
590834128.title: Monitor File Space Storage Usage

590834129.text:
You can now create up to 20 file spaces (spaces with a storage type of SAP HANA Data Lake Files), compared to the previous limit of 5.
See [Create a File Space to Load Data in the Object Store](947444683e524cfd9169d7671b72ba0c.html).
590834129.title: Create up to 20 File Spaces

590834130.text:
When copying a space, you can now select some or all of its source spaces (which share data to it), and some or all of its consumer spaces (to which it shares data), in order to create a new stack of spaces sharing data between them, independently of the original spaces.
See [Copy Spaces and their Contents](73068ac8e1934615b419d8c6c4095a9a.html).
This feature is available for all spaces, but can be particularly useful for copying the preparation and model spaces installed as intelligent content, in order to extend them to incorporate custom fields.
See [Extending Intelligent Content](3c158685865d4b408938a148e828e21f.html).
590834130.title: Copy Spaces and their Contents

590834131.text:
X.509 certificate-based authentication is now available as the default method for database users. This enhancement provides stronger security for technical users by reducing reliance on passwords, while still allowing password-based authentication as an alternative. See [Create a Database User](798e3fd6707940c3bd2219b2d1ebaac2.html).
This authentication method is also available via the Command Line. See [Managing Database Users via the Command Line](cd3b314dd33f407f9ba507dd870ba1f1.html).
590834131.title: Certificate-Based Authentication for Database Users

590834132.text:
When you create, edit, or delete a database user for a space, it is now immediately deployed without needing to deploy the space.
See [Create a Database User](798e3fd6707940c3bd2219b2d1ebaac2.html).
590834132.title: Database Users Immediately Deployed

590834133.text: You can now customize your system to generate CDS views when generate DataStore objects. These CDS views provide a data model for the DataStore object and can be used for custom development.
590834133.title: Access to Data of DataStore Objects Via CDS Views

590834134.text:
You now have the option of obtaining information about the metadata of SAP BW bridge objects using specific interfaces, and thus accessing these objects in your custom applications.The following interfaces provide you with access to the metadata:
- IF_RS_BW_INFOPROVIDER (metadata for InfoProviders), i.e. DataStore objects
- IF_RS_BW_DATASTORE (metadata for DataStore objects)
- IF_RS_BW_INFOOBJECT (metadata for InfoObjects)
590834134.title: Metadata API Layer for ABAP Customer Code

590834135.text: You can import variables in the global filter of the query definition as well as in restricted key figures to SAP Datasphere and use them there in the analytic model. The default values set in SAP BW bridge are displayed in the preview. You can also define your own values.
590834135.title: Variable Import

590834136.text: As an SAP BW bridge administrator, you want to control external process chains, that is process chains from a third-party tool or from SAP BW / SAP BW∕4HANA. You can do this by using the following communication scenarios in SAP BW bridge:[Integration of Process Chain API (Communication Scenario SAP_COM_0941)](https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_BW_BRIDGE/107a6e8a38b74ede94c833ca3b7b6f51/f01aefe0cc5442d0808d847c365b5630.html) and [Integration of Process Type Remote Process Chain (Communication Scenario SAP_COM_0A16)](https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_BW_BRIDGE/107a6e8a38b74ede94c833ca3b7b6f51/895a1b2b9cc54662becc13c65c6adde3.html)
590834136.title: External Access to Process Chains

590834137.text: Data Tiering allows you to assign data to various storage areas and storage media. The critera for this decision are data type, operational considerations, performance requirements, frequency of access, and security requirements. Data Tiering Optimization (DTO) helps you to classify the data in your DataStore object as warm or cold, depending on how frequently it is accessed. See [Data Tiering Optimization (DTO)](https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_BW_BRIDGE/107a6e8a38b74ede94c833ca3b7b6f51/9d76dae79ab047099ee81b50208d5945.html) in the SAP BW bridge documentation.
590834137.title: Data Tiering Optimization

590834138.text: Using the role SAP_BR_DEVELOPER_DWC, you can now extract metadata from SAP BW bridge using the catalog in SAP Datasphere. See [Business Role Templates and Business Catalogs](https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_BW_BRIDGE/107a6e8a38b74ede94c833ca3b7b6f51/75d2fa4c36a548ca86d0b8527123beb6.html) in the SAP BW bridge documentation.
590834138.title: Metadata Extraction as Part of Role SAP_BR_DEVELOPER_DWC

590834139.text: Process chains are executed in the Queued Task Manager framework (i.e. in ODQ_TQ_JOB jobs) rather than in a separate background job per process.
590834139.title: QTM (Queued Task Manager) Runtime for Process Chains

590834140.text:
As an administrator, you can now use four new key figures and a statistics record to find out how much usage there is in ABAP and the SAP HANA database when you execute a BW process.
See:
- [Monitoring CPU and Memory Usage](https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_BW_BRIDGE/107a6e8a38b74ede94c833ca3b7b6f51/eba48b07e2764047b42916eca979cae1.html?version=latest)
- [Average CPU Usage (ABAP)](https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_BW_BRIDGE/107a6e8a38b74ede94c833ca3b7b6f51/822d528e19544c2293157a0fb6b99e8a.html?version=latest)
- [Average Peak Memory (ABAP)](https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_BW_BRIDGE/107a6e8a38b74ede94c833ca3b7b6f51/6639e270bb4d444ab3700a3c094e3d6b.html?version=latest)
- [Average CPU Usage (Database)](https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_BW_BRIDGE/107a6e8a38b74ede94c833ca3b7b6f51/7bb87d939e8e499e860a8bca09fe4eb2.html?version=latest)
- [Average Peak Memory Usage (Database)](https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_BW_BRIDGE/107a6e8a38b74ede94c833ca3b7b6f51/00ea7cabf2b24d2d995c2d6fa141e93a.html?version=latest)
in the SAP BW bridge documentation.
590834140.title: Monitoring CPU and Memory Usage

590834141.text:
You can now enhance or change technical content InfoObjects by assigning them to one of your transportable packages.
See [Changing Technical Content InfoObjects](https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_BW_BRIDGE/107a6e8a38b74ede94c833ca3b7b6f51/f116ce7d83a940e7a66f6550409ba22c.html?locale=en-US&version=latest) in the SAP BW bridge documentation.
590834141.title: Changing Technical Content InfoObjects

590834142.text:
The DTP Monitor app offers you new functions. You can now get more information on red packages.
See [Monitoring Data Transfer Process](https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_BW_BRIDGE/107a6e8a38b74ede94c833ca3b7b6f51/11965da3103249338f519d139ac3a993.html?locale=en-US&version=latest).
590834142.title: DTP Monitor

590834143.text: You can now simulate the data update of a DTP request to help you to analyze an incorrect DTP request. You can also simulate a transformation prior to the actual data transfer.
590834143.title: Simulating DTPs

590834144.text:
To ease the transition from SAP BW to the SAP Data Warehouse Cloud, you can now transfer data models from SAP BW or SAP BW∕4HANA to SAP BW bridge via shell conversion. This is supported for SAP BW 7.3x, 7.40, and 7.50 and for SAP BW∕4HANA 2021. Shell conversion can be used to transfer metadata such as DataStore objects, InfoObjects, transformations, and Data Transfer Processes. It does not include the transfer of existing data sets. After the transfer, you can load data from the original source systems, the SAP BW system, or the SAP BW∕4HANA system.
See [3141688](https://me.sap.com/notes/3141688 ).
590834144.title: Shell Conversion

590834145.text:
For replicating source systems, you can now replicate the DataSources in the BW Modeling Tools.
See [Executing Replication](https://help.sap.com/viewer/107a6e8a38b74ede94c833ca3b7b6f51/latest/en-US/78bbe157705f4c27aa5c25e341f3e1cf.html).
590834145.title: Replicating DataSources

590834146.text: You can view the amount of capacity units consumed in a month using the new Capacities Dashboard. Access the dashboard from System Monitor   Capacities. See [Monitoring Capacity Unit Consumption](ba3d05baac854171914c09d64bed7202.html).
590834146.title: Monitor Consumption Unit Capacity

590834147.text: Joule can provide information and automate certain business processes through a chat. This functionality is available for customers who sign up for a restricted release. To learn more about signing up, see [Become an Early Adopter for Joule in SAP Datasphere](https://community.sap.com/t5/technology-blog-posts-by-sap/become-an-early-adopter-for-joule-in-sap-datasphere/ba-p/14096474).
590834147.title: Joule Available for Conversational Interactions

590834148.text: You can choose from more SAP BW bridge storage sizes. See [Configure the Size of Your SAP Datasphere Tenant](33f8ef4ec359409fb75925a68c23ebc3.html).
590834148.title: Additional SAP BW Bridge Storage Sizes

590834149.text:
Access to task and statement logs is made easier with the creation of Task Logs and Statement Logs tabs.Find task and statement logs faster with the new quick filtering options added to the existing advanced filtering option.
See [Monitoring SAP Datasphere](d39b8652994846f9ab80b32fc5b4d671.html).
590834149.title: New Navigation and Filtering Options in the System Monitor

590834150.text: The Capacity Units section in the Tenant Configuration tab has additional information including purchased unites, estimate, and available capacity units as well as the amount of capacity units used this month. See [Configure the Size of Your SAP Datasphere Tenant](33f8ef4ec359409fb75925a68c23ebc3.html).
590834150.title: More Capacity Units Details

590834151.text: You can now activate or deactivate a user via the SCIM 2.0 API by using the active attribute. See [Managing Users via the SCIM 2.0 API](1ca8c4a9467f43df9ae6d4ed3734f05a.html).
590834151.title: Activate or Deactivate a User via the SCIM 2.0 API

590834152.text:
When you enable SAP HANA multi-dimensional services (MDS) information tracing to analyze individual MDS queries in the System Monitor, the view M_MULTIDIMENSIONAL_STATEMENTS is now also made accessible in addition to the view M_MULTIDIMENSIONAL_STATEMENT_STATISTICS and provides extensive information about MDS queries.Also, you can now specify the maximum number of records that are stored for MDS requests in the monitoring tables.
See [Configure Monitoring](9cd0691c44a74f2aa47b52f615f74433.html).
590834152.title: More Information Available on MDS Queries

590834153.text:
If certain views and SAP HANA multi-dimensional services (MDS) requests regularly require more resources than are available on your SAP Datasphere tenant, you can now purchase additional on-demand compute and processing memory. You can then create elastic compute nodes, allocate the additional resources to them and schedule them to spin up to handle read peak loads.You can identify peak loads and monitor elastic compute nodes in dedicated dashboards in the System Monitor. Note
Users of SAP Analytics Cloud and Microsoft Excel (with the SAP add-in) will then automatically benefit from the improved performance of the elastic compute nodes when consuming data exposed by SAP Datasphere.
- To purchase compute and processing memory for elastic compute nodes in the Tenant Configuration page, see [Configure the Size of Your SAP Datasphere Tenant](33f8ef4ec359409fb75925a68c23ebc3.html).
- To create and run elastic compute nodes in the Space Management, see [Add Scalable Processing Capacity via Elastic Compute Nodes](1f7c1811d264462fb0cd03e37da07ad7.html).
- To monitor elastic compute nodes in the System Monitor, see [Monitoring SAP Datasphere](d39b8652994846f9ab80b32fc5b4d671.html).
In Tenant Configuration, you can also modify your elastic compute node consumption settings. See [Configure the Size of Your SAP Datasphere Tenant](33f8ef4ec359409fb75925a68c23ebc3.html).
590834153.title: Add Scalable Processing Capacity via Elastic Compute Nodes

If you accidentally deleted your SAP Datasphere service instance in SAP BTP, you can now restore it within seven days.
See [Delete Your Service Instance in SAP BTP](2665ce1e83314dd396cea0b88ed5af40.html).

When enabled, a colored information bar is visible to all users of the tenant, and the browser favicon is updated with the matching color.See [Display Your System Information](6bdd79878afa4ec5bcd9d3502158a06e.html).

You can now set tenant memory by size instead of by the number of compute blocks. Performance classes have been added to allow you to choose the vCPU allocation to your tenant.See [Configure the Size of Your SAP Datasphere Tenant](33f8ef4ec359409fb75925a68c23ebc3.html).
