590834157.title: New Privilege Data Warehouse Runtime

590834158.text: You can now access the _SYS_BI schema views from the monitoring spaces. See [Configure Monitoring](9cd0691c44a74f2aa47b52f615f74433.html).
590834158.title: Additional Views Available in the Monitoring Spaces

590834159.text: In Tenant Configuration, you may now allocate blocks for premium outbound integration. See [Configure the Size of Your SAP Datasphere Tenant](33f8ef4ec359409fb75925a68c23ebc3.html).
590834159.title: Allocate storage to premium outbound integration

590834160.text: In Tenant Configuration, you may now modify the storage blocks allocated to the catalog and catalog crawling. See [Configure the Size of Your SAP Datasphere Tenant](33f8ef4ec359409fb75925a68c23ebc3.html).
590834160.title: Change the storage blocks allocated to the catalog and catalog crawling

590834161.text: Users with the DW Administrator role (or equivalent privileges) can now create spaces by importing packages via the Content Network or Transport apps.See [Importing Content from Another Tenant](b607a12931d74c4a93506ea64c55ab4e.html) and [Importing SAP and Partner Business Content from the Content Network](400078d689bf4454b3fc977a4e201c2f.html).
590834161.title: DW Administrators Can Create Spaces via Content Network Packages

590834162.text: Additional driver versions are supported for Amazon Redshift, Oracle, and Google BigQuery connections. We recommend to use the newest supported versions. See [Upload Third-Party ODBC Drivers (Required for Data Flows)](b9b5579054df48c39381d5b17286bf21.html).
590834162.title: New ODBC Driver Versions Supported for Connections

590834163.text:
Now, each user can have different privileges in each of the spaces she is assigned to. For example, a user can be a viewer in space A, a modeler in space B and a space administrator in space C:
Note
Scoped roles and all related features will be rolled out to all tenants over the course of a number of versions. For more details, see SAP Note [3380409](https://launchpad.support.sap.com/#/notes/3380409).
SAP Datasphere Roles Up to Version 2023.21: Each user was assigned one or more roles and could use all the privileges granted by these roles in all the spaces of which she was a member.
SAP Datasphere Scoped Roles from Version 2023.21: Each assignment of a user to a space is performed via a scoped role which grants the privileges of a particular role to the user in the context of one or more spaces. By assigning the user to other spaces via other scoped roles, the administrator can provide the user exactly the privileges that she needs in each space. For example, Julia can be a modeler in space Sales Germany and Sales France and a viewer in space Europe Sales.
- For SAP Datasphere tenants that were created before version 2023.21, the roles and user assignment to spaces have been converted so that users can continue to perform the same actions as before in their spaces. See [Automated Conversion to Scoped Roles](6f7c6dfa3cb249debb749c729025bae0.html).
- Assigning users to spaces:
- A DW Administrator can assign a role to multiple users in multiple spaces, in a single scoped role. See [Create a Scoped Role to Assign Privileges to Users in Spaces](b5c4e0b6c462414783ebbfc053815521.html).
- A DW Space Administrator can assign and unassign users to their spaces and the changes are reflected in the scoped roles. See [Control User Access to Your Space](9d59fe511ae644d98384897443054c16.html).
- New scoped roles vs global roles:
- Each standard or custom role is now either a global role or a template for scoped roles.
- A scoped role inherits a set of scoped privileges from a standard or custom role and grants these privileges to users for use in the assigned spaces.
- A global role enables users assigned to it to perform actions that are tenant-wide (and not space-related), typically a role that enables to administrate the tenant. A global role includes global privileges. The DW Administrator, Catalog Administrator and Catalog User standard roles delivered with SAP Datasphere are global roles.
- Privileges and permissions are now either global or scoped. See [Privileges and Permissions](d7350c6823a14733a7a5727bad8371aa.html).Note
When you create a custom role: if you’re creating it to enable users to perform global actions, you should include only global privileges; if you’re creating it to enable users to perform space-related actions, you should include only scoped privileges. See [Create a Custom Role](862b88eed50244049d41361ba3290456.html).
See [Managing Roles and Privileges](3740dacbc2794f33bb5d8d42216cc3bc.html) and [Standard Roles Delivered with SAP Datasphere](a50a51d80d5746c9b805a2aacbb7e4ee.html).
- Standard roles become templates - The following standard roles that are delivered with SAP Datasphere become templates for creating customs roles, because they are space-related and can be used as templates for creating scoped roles: DW Space Administrator, DW Integrator, DW Modeler, DW Viewer, DW Consumer. Predefined scoped roles that are based on the roles mentioned above are also delivered with SAP Datasphere and inherit the privileges and permissions of the standard roles they are derived from. See [Standard Roles Delivered with SAP Datasphere](a50a51d80d5746c9b805a2aacbb7e4ee.html).
- Main privileges and permissions changes in standard roles:
- The DW Administrator role no longer has access to modeling apps (such as Data Builder).
- The DW Space Administrator role can manage the users in their space now by using the new privilege Scoped User Role Assignment.
- No more membership of users in spaces - Users are now assigned to spaces via scoped roles, they are no more members of spaces. The Members area in a space page has been renamed to Users. See [Create a Space](bbd41b82ad4d4d9ba91341545f0b37e7.html) and [Control User Access to Your Space](9d59fe511ae644d98384897443054c16.html).
- Assigning users to a role via SAML attributes - You can now assign users to a role via SAML attributes. If a user is assigned to a scoped role, the user is automatically assigned to all the spaces included in the scoped roles. See [Assign Users to a Role Using SAML Attributes](33157115bac34f9b8e96dc0797969387.html).
590834163.title: New Flexible Space and Role Assignment for Users - Scoped Roles

590834164.text: In Tenant Configuration, you can now delete your data lake storage in order to reduce or remove the storage used by your tenant.
590834164.title: Reduce or delete the data lake storage used by your tenant

590834165.text: In Tenant Configuration, you may now modify the capacity units allocated to Data Integration applications. See [Configure the Size of Your SAP Datasphere Tenant](33f8ef4ec359409fb75925a68c23ebc3.html).
590834165.title: Change the capacity units allocated to Data Integration applications

590834166.text: To further analyze SAP HANA multi-dimensional services (MDS) queries in the System Monitor, you can now enable the tracing of MDS information.See [Configure Monitoring](9cd0691c44a74f2aa47b52f615f74433.html) and [Monitoring SAP Datasphere](d39b8652994846f9ab80b32fc5b4d671.html).
590834166.title: Display Additional Information on MDS queries

590834167.text:
A database analysis user can now stop a statement by running a database procedure in SAP HANA Database Explorer (for example when a long-running statement causes performance issues).
See [Stop a Running Statement With a Database Analysis User](0cf11ede362b4f4186c459097464943d.html).
590834167.title: Stop Running Statements

590834168.text:
You can now allow SAP Product Support to generate support users based on SAP support incidents.
With the new setting, you don't need to create a support user for each incident separately. To improve security, the user is a personalized user which is enabled for multi-factor authentication and will be deleted after the incident has been solved.
See [Request Help from SAP Technical Support](831a97714dfe4301918afece5a3b380b.html).
590834168.title: Allow Support User Creation

590834169.text:
You can now monitor the statements that are queued by viewing the cards dedicated to admission control events in the Dashboard tab of the System Monitor.
See [Monitoring SAP Datasphere](d39b8652994846f9ab80b32fc5b4d671.html).
590834169.title: Monitor Admission Control Events (Queued Statements)

590834170.text:
Up to now, the maximum number of records for expensive statements that were stored in the monitoring tables was 30 000. An administrator can now change this number, which will impact the views dedicated to monitoring and information related to statements in the System Monitor. For example, you may want to increase the number of records in order to trace more data in the System Monitor.
See [Configure Monitoring](9cd0691c44a74f2aa47b52f615f74433.html).
590834170.title: Changing the Maximum Number of Records for Expensive Statements

590834171.text:
When you’re using a consumption-based tenant with a free plan, the number of remaining days before the 90-day expiration is now displayed in the top panel of SAP Data Warehouse Cloud. This enables you to know how many days remain before you can update your free-plan tenant to a standard plan.
See [Creating and Configuring Your SAP Datasphere Tenant](2f80b57359254b5cbb4faac794ade90c.html) and [Update Your Free Plan to Standard Plan in SAP BTP](f173be27e9cb4c758c0f1fa133d9edda.html).
590834171.title: Displayed Number of Remaining Days Before Expiration of Free-Plan Tenant

590834172.text:
The privilege Data Warehouse General allows users to log onto SAP Data Warehouse Cloud and is included in all roles except for DW Consumer.
Note
If you have created custom roles in an earlier version, we recommend that you adjust them and include the Data Warehouse General privilege. However, if you do not do this, note that users with custom roles including at least one the following privileges are still able to connect onto SAP Data Warehouse Cloud: Data Warehouse Data Builder, Data Warehouse Business Builder, Spaces, Data Warehouse Cloud Data Access Control, Data Warehouse Remote Connection, or Data Warehouse Cloud Data Integration.
See [Privileges and Permissions](d7350c6823a14733a7a5727bad8371aa.html).
590834172.title: New Privilege Allowing Login

590834173.text:
You can now monitor data integration tasks using pre-configured views provided as business content by SAP via the Content Network.
As a pre-requisite, you'll create the new dedicated monitoring space (with the space ID <SAP_ADMIN> and the space name <Administration (SAP)>) and then import the <Technical Content: Task Monitoring> package from the Content Network.
See [Configure Monitoring](9cd0691c44a74f2aa47b52f615f74433.html) and [Working with SAP HANA Monitoring Views](4ab45090c5684ebf8765757a1dfc4e5d.html).
590834173.title: Monitor Data Integration Tasks With Views From the Content Network in New Dedicated Space

590834174.text:
Users with the appropriate privilege can share data products to SAP Databricks, where users can query and enrich the data products using machine learning and generative AI tools. Also, the share status for data products are updated so users can easily see which data products have been shared.
See [Requesting Access to Data Products](ea7cb802cbea47b39a441888873c3a49.html) and [Sharing Data Products to Target Systems](https://help.sap.com/docs/business-data-cloud/governing-and-publishing-data-in-catalog/sharing-data-products-to-sap-databricks).
590834174.title: Share Data Products to SAP Databricks

590834175.text:
When a data product is no longer needed in an SAP Datasphere space, users can uninstall it from that space.
See [Requesting Access to Data Products](ea7cb802cbea47b39a441888873c3a49.html) and [Data Product Details](71f4d1599dba4aa59e6682a314650cf7.html).
590834175.title: Remove Data Product from an SAP Datasphere Space

590834176.text:
When catalog assets have lineage to a data product, that data product and its exposed entities appears in the Impact and Lineage Analysis diagram.
See [Accessing Catalog Assets](dc061a23484241b1b791f5540b1f38e3.html).
590834176.title: Data Products Visible in the Impact and Lineage Diagram

590834177.text:
When viewing the information for an asset, a new Details tab is available. This tab shows detailed metadata about the asset, which can include columns, attributes, measures, dimensions, and properties specific to each data object.
See [Accessing Catalog Assets](dc061a23484241b1b791f5540b1f38e3.html).
Note
For existing connections to source systems with assets that have already been extracted to the catalog, you must manually resynchronize the systems to be able to see metadata in the Details tab.
- In the side navigation area, choose  (Catalog & Marketplace)   (Metadata Extractions).
- For each existing source system in the Systems Connection table, click  (Synchronize).
After the resynchronization finishes, you can select an asset to see if metadata in the Details tab is available.
See [Connecting Source Systems](0b5de87f256f466f95b46d4bcaa52640.html).
590834177.title: Add Details Tab for the Asset Details Page

590834178.text:
Predictive scenarios and data actions can now be extracted from SAP Analytics Cloud tenants and added to the catalog. Note
You can take advantage of this enhancement with the release of SAP Analytics Cloud Q3 2023.
See [Connecting to SAP Analytics Cloud Systems](27a4f9620761458dbc60cf9cf853989d.html).
590834178.title: Metadata Extraction of Predictive Scenarios and Data Actions from SAP Analytics Cloud

590834179.text: From the Local Tables (File) monitor, you can now cancel a merge task that is running with a new Cancel button.See [Merge or Optimize Your Local Tables (File)](e533b154ed3e49ce9a03e4421a5296e7.html).
590834179.title: Cancel a Running Merge Task

590834180.text: With the new connection type, you can connect to external systems and add tasks that are exposed by REST-based APIs to task chains. For this purpose, we have introduced the new API Tasks connection feature, which is supported only for Generic HTTP connections.See [Generic HTTP Connections](b79b865e64794c7abcd12a54f2f73c8c.html).
590834180.title: Connection Type Generic HTTP

590834181.text: SAP Datasphere now allows users to set up additional email notification within a task chain, in addition to the notification specified for completion of the entire task chain. Users drag the new Notification Task object to any point in the sequence of tasks run in a task chain and then specify the subject and message for this new email notification. (These new notifications use the same recipient list as the email notification maintained at the task chain level.)See [Configure Email Notification for Task Chains and Notification Tasks](7ff6a4e584a345a88d002c18c1fc321e.html).
590834181.title: New Notification Task Object in Task Chains

590834182.text: SAP Datasphere now provides the ability to run tasks in a task chain that use a REST-based API to access external systems.See [Run API Tasks in a Task Chain](9a8489ed7443436197fbd8b8ffba61ab.html).
590834182.title: Running API Tasks in a Task Chain

590834183.text: If you are filtering on a column that has values of data type Date or Datetime, you can refine your filter with additional options.See [Controlling Deletion of Local Table Records](2a59b7142e1b4d478b0bf4063084261e.html).
590834183.title: Additional Filter Options to Delete Records for Data Type Date or Datetime

590834184.text:
Microsoft Azure Data Lake Storage Gen1 was retired on February 29, 2024. The corresponding connection type was deprecated with SAP Datasphere version 2023.24. We have now removed the option to create or edit connections for connection type Microsoft Azure Data Lake Storage Gen1 from the Connections app:
- The connection type tile has been removed from the connection creation wizard.
- Existing connections are still visible in the connections list but cannot be edited anymore.
Action: Recreate your existing Gen1 connections with the Microsoft Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 connection type, adapt your models and processes to the new connection, and delete your Gen1 connections.
590834184.title: Connection Type Microsoft Azure Data Lake Storage Gen1 Removed from Connections App

590834185.text: In the event of an out-of-memory error, a link to Help Portal documentation will be provided in the task log messages. The enhanced documentation provides additional information about out-of-memory events.See [Persisted Views and Memory Consumption](e3d04951a4a344c28b25b2b1b13bf3d8.html) .
590834185.title: View Persistence Link to Out of Memory Documentation

590834186.text: The new scheduling feature allows tasks to be set at 5-minute intervals, offering greater flexibility and precision in task management.See [Schedule a Data Integration Task (Simple Schedule)](7c11059ed3314e1fb753736b7867512c.html) .
590834186.title: Enhanced Task Scheduling with 5-minute Increments

590834187.text: In the Local Tables (File) monitor, you can now display additional information to monitor your local tables (file): Number of Active Records, Active Records File Storage (MiB), Total Table File Storage (MiB) and Previous Versions File Storage (MiB) See [Monitoring Local Tables (File)](6b2d0073a8684ee6a59d6f47d00ec895.html).
590834187.title: Additional Monitoring Information for Local Tables (file)

590834188.text: From the replication flow editor, you can change the schema properties of an individual object that has Confluent Kafka as source.See [Confluent Kafka Sources for Replication Flows](4f2d0a8f23384efdab6891b29093786a.html).
590834188.title: Confluent Kafka as Source: Expand Array or Map, Configure Opcode and Change Primary Key

590834189.text: For task chains that include nested task chains, the behavior for retrying failed tasks within a nested chain has been improved. When a task chain reports a failure, and the failure occurred running one of the tasks inside a nested task chain, retry of the parent task chain no longer requires rerunning all the tasks in the nested task chain, but only needs to rerun tasks from the point where an individual task reported a failure.See [Monitoring Task Chains](4142201ec1aa49faad89a688a2f1852c.html).
590834189.title: Retry of Nested Task Chains within a Parent Task Chain

590834190.text: You can now load large quantities of data via replication flows and store them inexpensively in file spaces in the object store. You can prepare the data using transformation flows and then share data to a standard space to be used as a source of flows, views, and analytic models.See [Acquiring and Preparing Data in the Object Store](2a6bc3f6d79b4c39a01b6d58d043fbaf.html) and [Create a File Space to Load Data in the Object Store](947444683e524cfd9169d7671b72ba0c.html).
590834190.title: Acquire and Prepare Data in the Object Store

590834191.text:
You can now use connection type Microsoft SQL Server to replicate data from Microsoft SQL Server databases using replication flows.See:
- [Creating a Replication Flow](25e2bd7a70d44ac5b05e844f9e913471.html)
- [Microsoft SQL Server Connections](a13c8abb328f45be891599c9cc76fb91.html)
590834191.title: Microsoft SQL Server as Source for Your Replication Flow

590834192.text:
You can update the required amount of compute resources that the file space can consume when running a specific translation flow.
See [Override the Default Settings to Run Your Transformation Flow (in a File Space)](e5c4ac8ab3bf4573b86cd4f4f3118c16.html) .
590834192.title: Change the Settings used to Run a Transformation Flow in a File Space

590834193.text: Refinements have been made in the view partitioning and View Analyzer run details and task logs for improved usability. See [Analyze Results](9ad9b8b42c82414c9cd166c55752c9a8.html) .
590834193.title: Data Persistence - View Monitoring Improvements

590834194.text: You can now include and run SAP BW bridge process chains in a task chain. To create and run SAP BW bridge process chains in a task chain, you must first have created the SAP BW bridge space and configured the SAP BW Bridge Cockpit. You use the cockpit to create and update process chains.See [Run SAP BW Bridge Process Chains in a Task Chain](7d7d02a81bfe401ab85ce4d6c527a536.html).
590834194.title: SAP BW Bridge Process Chains in a Task Chain

590834195.text:
Two new options are available in the transformation flow monitor via the Data Integration Monitor:
- Simulate a run that doesn't save changes in the target table by clicking Simulate Run. Simulating allows you to test a transformation flow and see if you get the desired outcome. Based on the result, you can decide to deploy the flow, resolve errors, or to optimize the flow to improve performances.
- Download a PLV file of a visual map of the operators and their relationships and hierarchies by clicking Generate a SQL Analyzer Plan File. The plan file contains detailed information about your data model that you can download for further analysis. Analyzing this file allows you to resolve errors and enhance the transformation flow performances.
See [Explore Transformation Flows](7588192bf4cd4e3db43704239ba4d366.html)
590834195.title: New Flow Analysis Possibilities for Transformation Flows

590834196.text: For views with one input parameter with default value, you can execute View Analyzer with memory consumption. For views with one or more parameters with default value, you can generate Explain Plan or SQL analyzer plan file.See [Getting Started with View Analyzer](e0aeddba00b14be29b5e49b47001d43b.html) .
590834196.title: Run View Analyzer for Views with Input Parameters

590834197.text:
You can now change the delta load interval for a replication flow in status Active without stopping the replication flow first.
See [Modify Replication Flow Object Schemas and Settings](a24c71f3ba7548909534d4cb52cefbfc.html) and [Working With Existing Replication Flow Runs](da62e1ee746448e8bc043e1be4377cbe.html).
590834197.title: Change delta interval without impacting running replication flow

590834198.text:
The View Analyzer provides data persistence guidance. This feature provides concrete recommendations for views persist to improve performance, run-time, and memory consumption. The goal is to provide readily available recommendations to optimize performance and minimize evaluation time for the business user.
See [Data Persistence Guidance](85f7be45761f4ae5b7e49819ce4b4d2e.html).
590834198.title: Data Persistence Guidance in View Analyzer

590834199.text:
You can now share task chains to other spaces where they can be nested in other task chains. This allows you to run tasks in multiple spaces from a single chain. In addition, you can export a task chain from its editor to a CSN/JSON file, which can then be imported into another space or tenant.See:
- [Creating a Task Chain](d1afbc2b9ee84d44a00b0b777ac243e1.html)
- [Sharing Entities and Task Chains to Other Spaces](64b318f8afd74bb78467cf56eb44294f.html)
- [Importing and Exporting Objects in CSN/JSON Files](f8ff0628c9fc49229740ffcd4d20e9aa.html)
590834199.title: Sharing and Exporting Task Chains

590834200.text:
You can now use Confluent Kafka and the corresponding connection type to add sources to replication flows.
See
- [Confluent Kafka Sources for Replication Flows](4f2d0a8f23384efdab6891b29093786a.html)
- [Integrating Data via Connections](eb85e157ab654152bd68a8714036e463.html)
590834200.title: Confluent Kafka as source for replication flows

590834201.text: You can now change the source language of a Space enabled for Translation. For more information, see Translating Metadata for SAP Analytics Cloud. See [Translating Metadata for SAP Analytics Cloud](fe829debe389450394cf7a15860e2caa.html).
590834201.title: Changing a space source language for metadata translation

590834202.text:
When creating a task chain, the task chain editor now lets you choose to remove the replicated or persisted data for remote tables and views.
See [Creating a Task Chain](d1afbc2b9ee84d44a00b0b777ac243e1.html).
590834202.title: Removing replicated and persisted data from tables and views in task chains

590834203.text: You can now use a BAdI implementation to add your own projection logic for replication of CDS view data. Note that you can only use this feature if the corresponding BAdI is available for your source system release. See [Define Custom Projection Logic in a Replication Flow](970636e38ce44a10ab0a8734a284c7c9.html).
590834203.title: Add customer-specific projection logic to replication flows

590834204.text: For replication flows having the local repository (SAP Datasphere) as the target, new target objects would previously only be created when you deployed the flow. Now they are already created when you save the flow. This helps to ensure that dependencies are displayed correctly in Impact and Lineage Analysis as well as within packages, and it makes the deployment process faster. However it also means that certain changes to the replication flows are no longer possible (or have to be done in a different way) after you save the flow for the first time. See [Modify Replication Flow Object Schemas and Settings](a24c71f3ba7548909534d4cb52cefbfc.html).
590834204.title: New target objects for replication flow created at saving

590834205.text: You can now add a view as a source in a transformation flow. See [Creating a Transformation Flow](f7161e6c20204672ac4a6d90c81762e4.html).
590834205.title: Views in Transformation Flows

590834206.text: As a Data Integrator you want to monitor all local tables whichYou can now add objects to a replication flow in status Active without having to stop the run first. See [Working With Existing Replication Flow Runs](da62e1ee746448e8bc043e1be4377cbe.html).
590834206.title: Add new replication objects without impacting running replication flow

590834207.text:
For CDS views and, SLT tables that have load type Initial and Delta, you can now specify a thread count greater than 1 for delta load and thus enable parallel processing.
See [Configure the Run Settings of a Replication Flow](3f5ba0c5ae3944c1b7279bb989a2a5b5.html).
590834207.title: Replication flows: parallel processing during delta load

590834208.text:
Once a data persistence task is completed, metrics information relating to the persisted view are displayed
See [Understanding the Data Persistence Metrics](d65994c3611946c19c2634e1a6c0a7ad.html).
590834208.title: Data Persistence Metrics

590834209.text:
For the connection types SAP ABAP, SAP BW, SAP ECC, and SAP S/4HANA On-Premise, we've added RFC Serialization to the advanced connection properties. The property is available with Data Provisioning Agent version 2.3.7.2 or higher. You can use it to specify whether to use fast column-based serialization or row-based serialization when transferring data. The default is column-based serialization. See:
- [SAP ABAP Connections](a75c1aacf951449ba3b740c7e46da3a9.html)
- [SAP BW Connections](e589041e80264f43b6c209c407336376.html)
- [SAP ECC Connections](e546ccd61af54bf49a0f531a43fe0961.html)
- [SAP S/4HANA On-Premise Connections](a49a1e3cc50f4af89711d8306bdd8f26.html)
590834209.title: RFC Serialization for ABAP-Based Connection Types

590834210.text:
You can now use Confluent Kafka and the corresponding connection type to add targets to replication flows.See:
- [Confluent Kafka Targets for Replication Flows](74b3c95464f246aa8c3fd510661daa6d.html)
- [Integrating Data via Connections](eb85e157ab654152bd68a8714036e463.html)
- [Confluent Connections](d83c08ad4eaf49dba9602b1d51c07a52.html#loiod83c08ad4eaf49dba9602b1d51c07a52)
590834210.title: Confluent Kafka as Target for Replication Flows

590834211.text: When the source system is not available, you can disable real-time data replication from the Remote Tables monitor or from the table editor of the Data Builder. The data access of your remote table is switched from Replicated (Real-time) to Replicated (Snapshot), and the replicated data are kept to allow further consumption or actions on the object such as deleting or changing the properties of the connection. See [Disabling Real-Time Data Replication](82380e6f01c84fac898a285ac40a1e50.html).
590834211.title: Disable Real-Time Data Replication When the Source System is not Available

590834212.text: You can add remote tables located in SAP BW bridge spaces to a transformation flow. See [Creating a Transformation Flow](f7161e6c20204672ac4a6d90c81762e4.html).
590834212.title: Add Source Tables from SAP BW Bridge Spaces to Transformation Flows

590834213.text: In Views monitor, the findings provided with the option Rate Column Suitability while creating partitions to persist your views, have been refined with more precise information.See [Creating Partitions for Your Persisted Views](9b1b595054c34da5b67ac07595093f82.html).
590834213.title: View Partitioning Advisor Provides More Precise Findings

590834214.text: You can change the run mode for a transformation flow and choose between performance and memory consumption. See [Change Transformation Flow Settings](f7da0290f5084e3db17c65b3d7c3140a.html).
590834214.title: Change the Run Mode for a Transformation Flow

590834215.text:
You can now add connections to packages either via the  (Transport) app or when creating or editing connections. Furthermore, you can export and import connections via the  (Transport) app. If your imported content included one or more connections that didn't exist in your space before the import, you must:.
- Edit the connections to complete their configuration and provide the credentials to connect to the remote systems
- Manually deploy imported objects that depend on the imported connections (and which could not, therefore, be automatically deployed)
See:
- [Transporting Content Between Tenants](df12666cf98e41248ef2251c564b0166.html)
- [Create a Connection](c2165842082c43fc85bad9f0c97572bb.html)
- [Edit a Connection](ba20892f25744b86a62ae571e3ea6ead.html)
590834215.title: Add Connections to Packages and Transport Connections

590834216.text: The Remote Queries monitor have been enhanced with additional columns, which provide additional information regarding used sources and runtimes. See [Monitoring Remote Queries](806d7f0c45a14f1fb07db0a226b2b822.html).
590834216.title: Additional Columns in Remote Queries Monitor

590834217.text: For transformation flows, you can now create an SQL view transform to combine and transform data in a powerful SQL editor.See [Create an SQL View in a Transformation Flow](775e0ab758e54c58af5a240294d234f2.html).
590834217.title: Create an SQL View Transform For a Transformation Flow

590834218.text: From the Views monitor, in the details screen of a data persistence view run, you can change the run mode to choose between performance and memory consumption depending on your needs.See [Change Persisted View Settings](d04f5dd6bbda44448407d54d2a7979be.html).
590834218.title: Change the Data Persistence Run Mode

590834219.text: You can now create Microsoft SQL Server connections with the version Microsoft SQL Server 2022 to connect to databases with this version.See [Microsoft SQL Server Connections](a13c8abb328f45be891599c9cc76fb91.html).
590834219.title: Connection Type Microsoft SQL Server Supports Version 2022

590834220.text: You can now modify the throughput by changing the number of replication threads for the source or target, respectively.See [Add the Source for a Replication Flow](749638060e8746e48b0f9bf0e50c6d0c.html) and [Add the Target for a Replication Flow](ab490fb4d083442197e2ba3b92079734.html).
590834220.title: Change Number of Replication Threads

590834221.text:
In addition to data lake Files from SAP HANA Cloud, data lake, you can now also use the following cloud storage providers and corresponding connection types to add targets to replication flows:
- [Amazon Simple Storage Service Connections](a7b660a0a4ef4a4fbee57b44f5b2147d.html)
- [Google Cloud Storage Connections](aec242c29188408c9ebe1a3ab63ce28b.html)
- [Microsoft Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 Connections](cd06b3c5ab5147c0905e3fa8abd13eb1.html)
See also:
- [Cloud Storage Provider Targets for Replication Flows](43d93a27150a4a218e3df14e3abdf456.html)
- [Integrating Data via Connections](eb85e157ab654152bd68a8714036e463.html)
590834221.title: Additional Cloud Storage Providers As Targets For Replication Flows

590834222.text: You can now grant access to Application Function Library functions to your database users working in HDI containers on your SAP Datasphere tenant.See [Consume Space Objects in Your HDI Container](656eebc2ced14ec09afa455224fa9a98.html).
590834222.title: Access the Application Function Library in HDI containers

590834223.text: In the View Persistency Monitor – Details screen, execution logs have been enhanced with statistics information related to remote queries. You can use this information and navigate directly to the Remote Query Monitor to analyze what’s happened with the remote statements.See [Persisting and Monitoring Views](9af04c990f294fd28c00f46763dd8b0d.html).
590834223.title: Statistics Information on Remote Queries Involved While Persisting Views

590834224.text:
We've enhanced the Google BigQuery connection type:
- You can now use the connection type to add source objects to data flows. To use the connection for data flows, it is required to upload an ODBC driver. To enable an existing connection for data flows, you need to edit the connection and re-enter your credentials.
- You can now enter an additional region to access BigQuery datasets, for example EU, us-west1, or asia-east1.
See [Google BigQuery Connections](30ed77de13864368bdc596099b37ed70.html).
590834224.title: Connection Type Google BigQuery Supports Data Flows and Regions

590834225.text:
The previous method to use the /oauth/idp API to generate and provide SAML assertions has been deprecated as it is considered unsafe. You now directly enter the SAML assertion when creating or editing a connection.
For new connections, in the OAuth 2.0 section of the connection configuration, the properties related to the previous method (OAuth API Endpoint and OAuth User ID) have been removed. In the Credentials section, the Client Secret property has been replaced by the new property SAML Assertion where you can add a valid SAML assertion.
For existing connections, you can set the Provide SAML Assertion property in the OAuth 2.0 section to true to switch to the new method and then enter the SAML assertion in the Credentials section.
See:
- [Deprecation of OAuth IdP API /oauth/idp](https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_SUCCESSFACTORS_RELEASE_INFORMATION/8e0d540f96474717bbf18df51e54e522/db7ccbbbc7a54e929a305ff92d12241c.html) in the SAP SuccessFactors Release Information documentation
- [SAP SuccessFactors Connections](39df02030d4b411487bacecf9afea4e8.html)
590834225.title: Changed SAML Authentication for SAP SuccessFactors Connection Type

590834226.text:
To improve security when connecting to your Amazon S3 buckets, the connection configuration has been enhanced:
- You can now enable server side encryption to use encrypted objects in data flows, optionally using an AWS Key Management Service key for encryption.
- You can now assume a role to use temporary security credentials and restrict access to your Amazon S3 buckets based on an Identity and Access Management role (IAM role).
See [Amazon Simple Storage Service Connections](a7b660a0a4ef4a4fbee57b44f5b2147d.html).
590834226.title: Amazon Simple Storage Service Connection (S3) Supports Server Side Encryption and Restricted Access by Assuming a Role

590834227.text:
The following connection types now support adding source objects to replication flows:
- [SAP S/4HANA Cloud Connections](a98e5ffdf47c44d9a845dca01a18bd82.html)
- [SAP S/4HANA On-Premise Connections](a49a1e3cc50f4af89711d8306bdd8f26.html)
- [SAP ABAP Connections](a75c1aacf951449ba3b740c7e46da3a9.html)
- [Microsoft Azure SQL Database Connections](46343fc1c4544fa9a075d97f84d39826.html)
The following connection type now supports adding target objects to replication flows:
- [SAP HANA Cloud, Data Lake Files Connections](356e41e880e54255891b702d2afefeb3.html)
The following connection type now supports adding source and target objects to replication flows:
- [SAP HANA Connections](e6b63f176d3640609adcf06297fb37e9.html#loioe6b63f176d3640609adcf06297fb37e9)
See [Integrating Data via Connections](eb85e157ab654152bd68a8714036e463.html).
590834227.title: Connection Types Supporting Replication Flows

590834228.text:
You can now create a replication flow to load multiple data assets from one source into one target in a fast and easy way.
Possible data sources are, for example, SAP HANA, SAP HANA Cloud, or SAP S/4HANA. Possible targets are the local repository (SAP Datasphere); SAP HANA Cloud; SAP HANA; or SAP HANA Cloud, data lake.
For more information about available connection types, see [Integrating Data via Connections](eb85e157ab654152bd68a8714036e463.html).
You can either copy all relevant data once (initial load) or choose initial and delta, where the system does an initial load, then checks for source data changes once every 60 minutes and replicates the changes to the target.
You can define filters and mapping to delimit the scope of the replication flow.
See [Creating a Replication Flow](25e2bd7a70d44ac5b05e844f9e913471.html).
590834228.title: Replication Flows

590834229.text:
The Data Integration Monitor now allows you to retry execution of a failed task chain run. When the last task chain run fails, you can choose the Retry Run option to retry execution of the failed task chain, including child or subtasks (if any are defined), starting at the point at which the task chain run failed.
See [Monitoring Task Chains](4142201ec1aa49faad89a688a2f1852c.html).
590834229.title: Retry of Failed Task Chain Runs

590834230.text:
You can now create connections to access data from the Files component of standalone SAP HANA, data lake and use these connections in data flows.
See [SAP HANA Cloud, Data Lake Files Connections](356e41e880e54255891b702d2afefeb3.html).
590834230.title: Connection Type for SAP HANA, Data Lake Files

590834231.text: For remote tables with a replication error (real-time or snapshot), you can now open error messages by clicking on the error status in the Remote Table Monitor, on the monitor details page, or in the table editor. The messages provide contextual information including where and at which date and time the error occurred. If appropriate, they let you open applications that help solving the error, for example the monitor details page or the Connections or Configuration application to be able to fix issues with the connection or the Data Provisioning agent. If applicable, they offer the Retry action to resume real-time replication.
590834231.title: Replication Error Messages in Remote Table Monitor and Table Editor

590834232.text:
The Data Integration Monitor ( ) now provides a simpler method of resizing column or panel layouts in remote table replication, view persistency, data flow, and task chain run monitors. In addition, each of the monitors now provides the ability to sort and filter column displays as well as search log messages for individual task runs.
See [Managing and Monitoring Data Integration](4cbf7c7fc64645bfa364332827557267.html).
590834232.title: New Flexible Column Layout, Search, Sort, and Filter Controls

590834233.text:
From the View Persistency Monitor, you can now cancel a running execution of a view persistency using the Cancel Run button. This will turn the status of the task into failed.
See [Persisting and Monitoring Views](9af04c990f294fd28c00f46763dd8b0d.html).
590834233.title: Cancel a Running Execution of a View Persistency

590834234.text:
Task logs for persisted views have been enhanced in the View Persistency Monitor as memory consumption while persisting views can be checked using monitoring views.
See [Persisting and Monitoring Views](9af04c990f294fd28c00f46763dd8b0d.html).
590834234.title: Monitor Memory Consumption While Persisting Views

590834235.text:
To improve usability and provide instant access to creating and managing connections, they have been moved from Space Management into a separate Connections app that you can open from the side navigation area with the  (Connections) button. You can still open the app from the Connections section in Space Management.
See [Create a Connection](c2165842082c43fc85bad9f0c97572bb.html).
590834235.title: Connections App

590834236.text:
With the new connection type, you can connect to SFTP-based file shares in your local network to consume CSV, JSON, and other files in data flows.
See [Generic SFTP Connections](b645de78a8374c24871ab6169be40d35.html).
590834236.title: Connection Type Generic SFTP

590834237.text:
With the new connection type, you can connect to Microsoft Azure Blob Storage and use the connection in data flows.
See [Microsoft Azure Blob Storage Connections](df5a7c56ac21472c973f6fab341f3991.html).
590834237.title: Connection Type Microsoft Azure Blob Storage

590834238.text:
You can create a private offering of data products for the Catena-X network.
See [Creating Data Products for Catena-X](806c56d8a32b48d5a834107543351c20.html).
590834238.title: Catena-X Data Products

590834239.text:
You can define the scope of a license by enabling scope changes, and specifying which data product content users can access.
See [Changing License Scope](7890c5b332504a4b954c981b5f871e49.html).
590834239.title: Changing License Scope

590834240.text:
Use the Catena-X Access Policy context to create a private offering within the Catena-X network.
See [The Context Management App](2f3dbb9da8ae4b7a992c6358ab4fc2be.html).
590834240.title: Catena-X Access Policy

590834241.text: To create a new data provider profile, or edit an existing one, you must have the Space > Update privilege assigned to your role.
590834241.title: Required Privilege to Maintain Data Provider Profiles

590834242.text:
Use the Live Access mode to deliver data within the same tenant without replication. Indeed, the data view is shared live with the customer version of the tenant. In this way, the data is always up-to-date and doesn’t require any update.
See [Creating Marketplace Data Products](bbcbf42b0cb541529e63628d95f394c8.html).
590834242.title: Data Products: New Live Access Delivery Mode

590834243.text:
With the new lifecycle functions Deactivate and Delete the following product lifecycle states are introduced as well: Deactivated and Deleted.
SAP has the option to block products from the Data Marketplace in cases of non-compliance or pending disputes. Products that are affected by this action are indicated with the status Blocked.
See [Managing your Data Product's Lifecycle](c400001264094f8c89da104db72514ad.html).
590834243.title: New Product Lifecycle States

590834244.text:
With this version you as the Data Provider can add a URL to your external website where consumers can purchase a license key for your data products. Consumers will find the button Get License on the details page of the data product which will lead them to this website. You find the new parameter URL for License Key Purchase in the Create Data Product function.
See [Creating Marketplace Data Products](bbcbf42b0cb541529e63628d95f394c8.html).
590834244.title: Enabling External License Key Purchase

590834245.text:
The landing page for Data Marketplace targeted at consumers, enables you to find and acquire the right data products:
- You can search and browse for data products and data providers.
- You can use filter criteria to limit the search results.
- After you evaluated the data products, by downloading and testing free sample data for example you can acquire a product using different ways. A data product can be free of charge, be available on request, or require a license key.
See [Installing Marketplace Data Products](92c35efd6a4945a1a78250539aee9a51.html).
590834245.title: Find and Acquire Data Products

590834246.text: You can export the definition of the data preview of an analytic model as a local file. This enables technical support to recreate a data preview using this exported file for analysis purposes.
590834246.title: Export the Definition of the Data Preview

590834247.text: The aggregation types MIN, MAX, COUNT*, and AVG have been added to the already existing types LAST, SUM, and COUNT. See Creating a Transformation Flow in a File Space. See [Creating a Transformation Flow in a File Space](b917baf0431343bea8381fa37e12eeb8.html).
590834247.title: New Incremental Aggregation Types for Transformation Flows in a File Space

590834248.text: When creating a local table (file) from the table editor or as a target of your transformation flow, you can disable the delta capture settings. See [Creating a Local Table (File)](d21881b121bc4703861be6ead4aea2ab.html) and [Creating a Transformation Flow in a File Space](b917baf0431343bea8381fa37e12eeb8.html).
590834248.title: Disable Delta Capture for Local Tables (File)

590834249.text: In order to create restrictions and calculations across all measures of an analytic model, you can create structures. Structures help you to save time and ensure consistency in your calculations, as you don’t need to create a formula/calculation for each measure. See [Create a Structure for an Analytic Model](de1ed4742dec44088236131e239df8b9.html).
590834249.title: Structures for Analytic Models

590834250.text:
The OData consumption API URLs are modified to:GET https://<tenant_url>/api/v1/datasphere/consumption/<request>
The existing URLs are deprecated and will be removed in a future version.See [Consuming Data via the OData API](7a453609c8694b029493e7d87e0de60a.html).
590834250.title: New OData Consumption API URLs

590834251.text: When creating a data flow or modifying an existing one, you can now choose the new Python Version 3.11. Note that Python 3.9 will be deprecated soon.See [Create a Script in a Data Flow](f3e2570966ac4036b552ebd998274af1.html).
590834251.title: Python Version 3.11 Available for Your Data Flow Script Operators

590834252.text: Execute two database queries on a view directly in the Data Builder to get important runtime indicators to analyze performance. Additionally, you can now generate and download an Explain Plan for a select statement on the view.
590834252.title: Analyze the Performance of a View with the New Runtime Metrics Tool

590834253.text:
Working with large data files can require many resources and can lead to performance issues. To save resources and prevent performance issues, some changes have been made on table editor for local tables (file) data management:
- Previewing data: Data preview is possible, and is now read using Apache Spark resources.
- Find and replace: You can't add a filter on your Find and Replace activity : Replacement will happen in the whole dataset.
- Default sorting and filtering is no longer available and is disabled.
590834253.title: Data Preview and Data Management for Local Tables (File) Updates

590834254.text: You can create a new analytic model using another analytic model as fact source and re-use the modelled definitions for measures, exposed attributes, dimensions, and variables.See [Add a Fact to an Analytic Model](27075eeeba634f55be0b52e92cf88159.html).
590834254.title: Analytic Model as Fact Source

590834255.text: While creating a task chain, you can update the required amount of compute resources that the file space can consume when running a specific object.See [Creating a Task Chain](d1afbc2b9ee84d44a00b0b777ac243e1.html)
590834255.title: Change the Setting Used to Run a Task Chain in a File Space

590834256.text: Support for restoring past versions of objects is now extended to include data access controls.See [Reviewing and Restoring Object Versions](4f717cc0d90e4453a072b37f6b043593.html).
590834256.title: Restore Past Versions of Data Access Controls

590834257.text: You can replace the fact source of an existing analytic model by dragging the new fact source onto the fact source of the analytic model on the canvas. See: [Replace the Fact Source of an Analytic Model](ccf070353186428eb940ee6715c87a6a.html)
590834257.title: Replace The Fact Source of an Analytic Model

590834258.text: View the data in objects used in deployed SQL view transforms with the Data Preview panel. See [Create an SQL View in a Transformation Flow](775e0ab758e54c58af5a240294d234f2.html).
590834258.title: View data in a SQL View Transform

590834259.text: You can insert a Python operator to transform incoming data with a Python script and output structured data to the next operator with the new Python operator. See [.](a747acf9d96b450da4b802b80e05a896.html)
590834259.title: Python script for Transformation Flow in a File Space

590834260.text: You can now consume analytic models containing multi-value variables via the OData consumption API.See [Consuming Data via the OData API](7a453609c8694b029493e7d87e0de60a.html).
590834260.title: Consume Analytic Models with Multi-Value Variables via OData API

590834261.text: new validation rule lets you verify that your view columns have appropriate data types.See [Validating View Data](ed4063dc7f53436d806ea48f2fd3949a.html).
590834261.title: Data Type Validation Rule

590834262.text:
We have improved the user experience of the editor of the analytic model:
- You can now change the orientation of the layout of the diagram of the analytic model.
- When you edit an analytic model, you can now undo or redo your changes.
590834262.title: UX Improvements for Analytic Model

590834263.text:
There are several changes for variables in analytic models:
- You can now use standard variables in calculated measures.
- We have renamed source variables to standard variables.
- The data type of variables is now checked. You may need to select a data type in your variables now.
590834263.title: Variables in the Analytic Model

590834264.text: You can now choose to use replication flows when importing entities from SAP S/4HANA on-premise connections.See [Importing Entities with Semantics from SAP S/4HANA](845fedbd28574aa8b84239df848936f6.html).
590834264.title: SAP S/4HANA On-Premise Import Enhancements

590834265.text:
You can now create and update modeling objects of any type from the command line using the following commands:
- datasphere objects <object-type> create --space <id> --file-path <file>.json
- datasphere objects <object-type> update --space <id> --technical-name <name> --file-path <file>.json
See [Manage Modeling Objects and Tasks via the Command Line](6f5c65f209004751aa48f9682ee2ec45.html).
590834265.title: Create and Update Modeling Objects via the Command Line

590834266.text: You can now persist your SAP Analytics Cloud models directly in the SAP Datasphere repository and choose to expose them for use as sources of SAP Datasphere views and flows.See [Consume SAP Datasphere Data in SAP Analytics Cloud via an OData Service](9de2c660fd3b4db2b89ad25e584e8857.html)
590834266.title: Replication-Free Consumption of SAP Analytics Cloud Models

590834267.text: When you import SAP HANA SQL views via Open SQL schemas, you can now obtain input parameters and Not Null and Default Value metadata for columns.See [Review and Edit Imported Table Properties](75cea7b1cbeb4c9dba0ac13605c527b3.html).
590834267.title: Additional Open SQL Schema Table Metadata

590834268.text: You can now consume analytic models containing variables that require single values via the OData consumption API.See [Consuming Data via the OData API](7a453609c8694b029493e7d87e0de60a.html).
590834268.title: Consume Analytic Models with Single-Value Variables via OData API

590834269.text:
You can now preview data for ABAP CDS views and SAP Landscape Transformation Replication Server objects if your system meets the requirements:
- For CDS views, the source connection is SAP S/4HANA Cloud 2302, SAP S/4HANA on-premise 1909 or higher.
- For SAP Landscape Transformation Replication Server objects, ABAP Add-on DMIS 2018 SP08 / DMIS 2020 SP04 is installed.
See [Creating a Data Flow](e30fd1417e954577baae3246ea470c3f.html)
590834269.title: Data Preview for ABAP CDS Views and SAP Landscape Transformation Replication Server Objects in Data Flow Editor

590834270.text: For currency conversion measures in the analytic model, you can now define variables for the target currency, the reference date, and the exchange rate type. For more information, see [Create a Conversion Measure for Currencies](ec00efb338f3421a87dab4006d7ce6c8.html).
590834270.title: Variables for Currency Conversion Measures

590834271.text: You can now use the Data Editor to find and replace data in a local table. For more information, see [Maintain Local Table Data](4bd5e641be48409c8c79336df0c4a3c7.html).
590834271.title: Find and Replace Local Table Data

590834272.text: You can now search for objects in the Data Builder start page by filtering on existing objects. For more information, see the section "Create Objects and Act On Existing Objects" in [Preparing Data](f2e359c899fa4351b5f514d1d86ed9e2.html).
590834272.title: Find Objects with Filters in the Data Builder Start Page

590834273.text: The analytic model is now exposed for analytic access and the catalog service to the OData API.See [Consuming Data via the OData API](7a453609c8694b029493e7d87e0de60a.html).
590834273.title: Consume Analytic Models via OData API

590834274.text:
You can now use folders to organize the objects in your space. You can create a folder in the Repository Explorer, Business Builder, or Data Builder and it is immediately available across each of these apps. Once a folder is created, you can move objects to it or create objects in it.
You can create as many levels of folder as necessary.Note
The requirement that each object in a space must have a unique technical name, remains unchanged.
See [Organizing Objects in Folders](bbedad63821443518fcd8fe56f7d26f7.html).
590834274.title: Repository Folders

590834275.text: You can now export information from the runtime CSN of an analytic model for support to analyze it.
590834275.title: Export Support Information

590834276.text: You can now consume views with input parameters via both the relational and analytical OData APIs. You must set a value for each parameter that does not have a default value. If a parameter has a default value, you can accept or override it.See [Consuming Data via the OData API](7a453609c8694b029493e7d87e0de60a.html).
590834276.title: Consume Views with Input Parameters via OData API

590834277.text: You can now easily set or change a default value for input parameters with the assistance of the Value Help dialog. This dialog follows you along your workflow and allows you to change an input parameter default value while defining the parameter, previewing or consuming an object using the parameter, and also while modeling and previewing an analytic model. See [Create an Input Parameter in a Graphical View](53fa99ad58c04a1ba3bb87288756dabc.html), [Preview Data in an Analytic Model](9f1fa73a33424cbe9bac3064702c0dbd.html), [Creating a Graphical View](27efb479c4814252964d3fbc6ca2dfc3.html), and [Add a Fact to an Analytic Model](27075eeeba634f55be0b52e92cf88159.html).
590834277.title: Setting Default Values for Input Parameters and Propagating Them

590834278.text: In the Data Builder, when creating a local table, you can enable the new setting Delta Capture to track later changes in your local table. Local tables can be reused as source or target objects in many SAP Datasphere objects. See [Capturing Delta Changes in Your Local Table](154bdffb35814d5481d1f6de143a6b9e.html)
590834278.title: Capturing Delta Changes in Your local table

590834279.text:
For restricted measures in the analytic model, you can now enable constant selection.
See [Create a Restricted Measure](bfb43ddc98bc4162bc4196faf3e5d8c6.html).
590834279.title: Constant Selection

590834280.text:
The data preview that is integrated in the editor of the analytic model has been improved:
- There are now more filter options
- The filter options are now available under Settings
- Values are formatted according to the data type of the columns.
590834280.title: Data Preview of Analytic Model

590834281.text: You can now include intelligent lookups in task chains, in addition to previously allowed remote table replication, view persistency, and data flow objects. Like other objects, intelligent lookups can be included anywhere within the order of tasks defined in a task chain.See [Creating a Task Chain](d1afbc2b9ee84d44a00b0b777ac243e1.html).
590834281.title: Support for Intelligent Lookups in Task Chains

590834282.text: You can now use SAP HANA Cloud window functions such as RANK and WEIGHTED_AVG, which allow you to perform analytic operations over a set of input rows, in the SQL and graphical view editors.See [SQL Functions Reference](6d624a1956234d818d0bfdc77cbd0e09.html).
590834282.title: Support for Window Functions

590834283.text: In the editor of the analytic model, associations containing compounded keys are now available. When you add an associated dimension that uses a compounded key, the key attributes are added automatically.
590834283.title: Analytic Model: Compounded Keys

590834284.text:
In the Data Builder, a new object is available: the analytic model. Analytic models are now the preferred objects for making data ready for consumption in SAP Analytics Cloud. They allow you to create and define multi-dimensional models to provide data for analytical purposes to answer different business questions. Pre-defined measures, hierarchies, filters, variables, and associations provide flexible and simple navigation through the underlying data.
See [Creating an Analytic Model](e5fbe9e2cb93484dab8b1963145e565f.html).
590834284.title: Analytic Model

590834285.text:
- Define OData parameters to control how the data is returned from the service with the OData Parameters section. You can define custom parameters or select suggested parameters in a dropdown list.
- Browse entities related to the table source up to the second level when navigating properties by setting the depth of OData objects with the OData Properties section.
See [Add a Source to a Data Flow](7b50e8e304244ced9ff1e62e2f2fe919.html).
590834285.title: Data Flow: New Features for Table Sources from OData Remote Connections.

590834286.text:
After running a data flow, source and target table metrics are displayed in the Data Flow Monitor for longer and can be used for further analysis.
See [Creating a Data Flow](e30fd1417e954577baae3246ea470c3f.html).
590834286.title: Data Flow Monitor: Running Metrics

590834287.text:
You can now share the TCUR* currency conversion tables to other spaces using the already existing dialog box that allows to create currency conversion objects. Once the tables have been shared to other spaces, these spaces will see your space as an alternative source to create the currency conversion views.
See [Enabling Currency Conversion with TCUR* Tables and Views](b462239ffb644d9baab4442a10a72edf.html).
590834287.title: Sharing TCUR* Tables To Other Spaces

590834288.text:
You can now choose to insert missing string values as either Empty value or Null when loading and maintaining local table data. Also, you can filter on Empty value and Null in a data preview.
See [Load or Delete Local Table Data](870401f211f94132909bd9f2fafd91b2.html), [Maintain Local Table Data](4bd5e641be48409c8c79336df0c4a3c7.html), and [Viewing Object Data](b338e4aa7e7e494eb68c383720ebfd3a.html).
590834288.title: New Null and Empty Value Handling Options

590834289.text: You can now use the Data Viewer and all its options to view and filter on data stored in a local table using an Open SQL Schema as a source.
590834289.title: Viewing Data in Local Tables Using Open SQL Schema As Source

590834290.text:
To provide a more consistent experience and reduce loads on remote systems, the Data Builder data preview now times out if it is unable to return data within three minutes. When previewing a remote table or view, guidance is given to the user to improve response times by enabling replication or persistence, removing unnecessary columns, and enabling filters.
See [Viewing Object Data](b338e4aa7e7e494eb68c383720ebfd3a.html).
590834290.title: Data Preview Timeout

590834291.text:
By refreshing your remote table structure from the Data Builder, if new columns exist in the data source, you can select those that need to be added to your remote tables.
See [Process Source Changes in the Table Editor](622328b59afa40fd810b44ac84d6afd3.html).
590834291.title: Refresh Remote Tables Structure

590834292.text:
Compound keys are now supported and can be set in the Data Builder editors such as the Table Editor, the Graphical View editor, the E/R Model editor, and the SQL View editor. Compound keys are also supported in parent/child hierarchies.
See [Set Key Columns to Uniquely Identify Records](d9ef2c91f6d647e584bad51999e441cd.html) and [Create an External Hierarchy for Drill-Down](dbac7a862b3744d8a71d268644aac389.html).
590834292.title: Setting Compound Keys

590834293.text:
You can now choose to fail a data flow run if string truncation is detected while fetching the source columns.
See [Add a Source to a Data Flow](7b50e8e304244ced9ff1e62e2f2fe919.html).
590834293.title: Fail on String Truncation in Data Flow

590834294.text:
A view’s persisted data will now be removed if any changes are made and deployed to data access controls applied to any of its sources. This change ensures that the row-level security provided by your data access controls is kept up-to-date at each level in the stack whenever changes are made.
See [Persisted Views and Data Access Control](7a4a983611cc4efb9415e6f3db310eaa.html).
590834294.title: Enforcing Row-Level Security Following View Source Changes

590834295.text:
The Impact and Lineage Analysis has been completely rebuilt to provide a new look and feel and the following enhancements:
- Now access the analysis from the Data Builder start page (as well as the Repository Explorer and the data access control editor).
- See each object in the context of its space.
- Explore and tailor the diagram to your needs by showing or hiding individual branches of lineage or impacts.
- See the deployment status of objects, whether they contain persisted/replicated data, and whether they are exposed for consumption directly on their diagram symbols.
- See a preview of any object’s properties and open it in its editor.
See [Impact and Lineage Analysis](9da4892cb0e4427ab80ad8d89e6676b8.html).
590834295.title: New Impact and Lineage Diagram

590834296.text:
You can restrict data loads on remote tables that use an SDI ABAP or SDI CDI Adapter.
See [Restrict Remote Table Data Loads](bd1ece5c9f78444c87708ef11eed0a31.html).
590834296.title: Restrict Data Loads on Remote table

590834297.text:
Maintaining an object's data is facilitated with an URL link access. You can:
- share the URL link to other users with the proper editing rights
- bookmark the URL link in your browser for frequent use
The URL link brings you directly in the object's data editor and allows you to quickly maintain data contained in the object.See [Maintain Local Table Data](4bd5e641be48409c8c79336df0c4a3c7.html).
590834297.title: Quickly Maintain Data with a URL Access

590834298.text:
You can now configure join optimization for Join operator in a data flow to be either automatic or manual.
See [Create a Join in a Data Flow](e57633deb333431c8787f2f57b1cb08a.html).
590834298.title: Join Optimization in Data Flows

590834299.text:
You can now create associations in a SQLScript view. You can also, now, use shared objects as sources in a SQLScript view. When a shared object is added to the code, it's added in the form "spaceName"."objectName" and can directly be accessed, avoiding the need to duplicate the object in your space.
See [Creating an SQL View](81920e4d583f45fd8761c662d3c8abab.html)
590834299.title: Support for Associations and Shared Objects as Sources in SQLScript Views

590834300.text:
You can now reduce the volume of data loaded from your source systems and improve performance by removing unnecessary columns from the definition of a remote table.
See [Restrict Remote Table Data Loads](bd1ece5c9f78444c87708ef11eed0a31.html).
590834300.title: Remove Unnecessary Remote Table Columns to Reduce Data Loads

590834301.text:
Audit logs can consume a large quantity of GB of disk in your tenant. To avoid over-usage of your disk space, we’ve changed the audit log deletion behavior.
Behavior before this version: When doing the actions listed below, all related audit log entries were kept, even when the retention period specified for the audit logs had expired. An administrator could decide to delete the audit logs entries using the dedicated area System  Configuration  Audit.
- Deleting a space
- Deleting a database user (open SQL schema)
- Disabling an audit policy for a space
- Disabling an audit policy for a database user (open SQL schema)
- Unassigning an HDI container from a space
New behavior starting with this version:
- For spaces that have been deleted before this version: All related audit logs have been kept and an administrator can decide to delete them using the dedicated area System  Configuration  Audit.
- For spaces that are deleted from this version onward: audit log entries are deleted once the number of retention days has been reached (given that the space or database user that generates the logs is not deleted). Also, when doing the actions listed above, all related audit log entries are now deleted, and you’re informed about this directly on the interface.
See [Logging Read and Change Actions for Audit](266553976e1c4db9aaa28a75e2308b77.html).
Before performing any of these actions, which will delete the audit log entries, you may want to export them.
590834301.title: Changed Behavior for Audit Log Deletion

590834302.text:
A SAP Data Warehouse Cloud user must be a member of a space to access the data in that space. You can now restrict data access based on user roles with the Data Warehouse Consumption privilege (-RU-E---), which defines three levels of permission:
- R (Read) - Access only data that is exposed for consumption.
- U (Update) - Upload data from CSV files to local tables and delete data from local tables.
- E (Execute) - Access all data and edit data in local tables.
The standard application roles have been updated to include appropriate levels of DW Consumption permission: Role DW Consumption Permissions Can Access DW Administrator -RU-E--- All data DW Space Administrator -RU-E--- All data in space DW Integrator -------- No data DW Modeler -RU-E--- All data in space DW Viewer -R------ Only data exposed for consumption DW Consumer -RU----- Only data exposed for consumption
The main effect of these changes is for users with the DW Viewer role, who will continue to be able to access SAP Data Warehouse Cloud and open any object in their space but will no longer be able to preview data, except the output nodes of views that are exposed for consumption.Note
If you have created custom roles, you will need to add the DW Consumption privilege with the appropriate level of permission to allow them to continue accessing data. You should set the minimum level of permission necessary and, if appropriate, you may be able to move users from a modeler or viewer-like role to a consumer-like role.
See [Privileges and Permissions](d7350c6823a14733a7a5727bad8371aa.html) and [Privileges by App, Tool, Object, and Task](2d8b7d04dcae402f911d119437ce0a74.html).
590834302.title: More Granular Control of Data Access

590834303.text: This version contains no new generally available features.
590834303.title: No New Features

590834304.text: To further improve your product experience, we're now offering an extended, 5-minute user experience survey. We assign each user to one of four survey phases per year, during which we provide a 21-day period to take the survey. You will receive a notification when the survey becomes available to you. During its availability, you can access the survey by clicking Give Feedback in the shell bar. Besides, the shorter feedback survey remains available at all times.See [Navigating in SAP Datasphere](bd79b74face14b17a4cfa844a2fd36c7.html).
590834304.title: Extended User Experience Survey Available

590834305.text:
A few months ago, we have enabled 3 of our guides to be commented using the Open Documentation Initiative. See [blog](https://community.sap.com/t5/technology-blogs-by-sap/open-documentation-initiative-for-sap-datasphere-provide-feedback-and-help/ba-p/13562111)
As from wave 2024.08 all SAP Datasphere guides can be commented directly from the Help Portal: the Feedback button becomes visible in the action bar once you are logged in
590834305.title: New Feedback Button to Comment all Guides

590834306.text:
The new guide includes all information on accessing SAP Data Warehouse Cloud via the command line.
You will find information on how to install and update the dwc command line interface and how to log in via an OAuth client. It lists all commands to perform various operations on the following entity types:
- Spaces
- Data providers (Data Marketplace entity)
- Data products (Data Marketplace entity)
The new guide includes also the definition file formats for the named entity types.
See [Accessing SAP Datasphere via the Command Line](3f9a42ccde6b4b6aba121e2aab79c36d.html).
590834306.title: New Guide for Command Line Interface

590834307.text:
As of the current release, when displaying context-sensitive help in the application, a question mark () replaces the information icon () to highlight screen elements with context-sensitive help on the user interface.
To open context-sensitive help, select  (Help) in the shell bar of the application.
590834307.title: Question Mark Highlights Screen Elements with Context-Sensitive Help

590834308.text:
In the Repository Explorer, objects that are shared to a space you are a member of are now listed, even if you are not a member of the space that shared them.
See [Repository Explorer](f8ce0b4a24fe473a962176c8aa3cad42.html).
590834308.title: View Objects Shared to Your Spaces in the Repository Explorer

590834309.text:
The display name chosen in your profile settings - business or technical name – now also applies to the objects of the Data Integration Monitor.
See [Changing SAP Datasphere Settings](1084796d09464e78870f32cab8584dfc.html).
590834309.title: Display Name Applied to Data Integration Monitor Objects

590834310.text: In file space pages (for spaces with a storage type SAP HANA Data Lake Files), the Workload Management area has been renamed to Apache Spark and has been reorganized. The area now displays additional tasks and the applications that are used to run them.See [Create a File Space to Load Data in the Object Store](947444683e524cfd9169d7671b72ba0c.html).
590834310.title: Enhanced Apache Spark Area for File Spaces

590834311.text: The value of the default configuration for the total amount of threads that each space can consume has been changed to 70%.See [Set Priorities and Statement Limits for Spaces or Groups](d66ac1efb5054068a104c4559b72d272.html)
590834311.title: Change of Default Value for Total Statement Thread Limit

590834312.text: Users are now assigned to spaces via scoped roles, they are no more members of spaces. The Members area in a space page has been renamed to Users.See [Create a Space](bbd41b82ad4d4d9ba91341545f0b37e7.html) and [Control User Access to Your Space](9d59fe511ae644d98384897443054c16.html).
590834312.title: No More Membership of Users in Spaces

590834313.text:
The area where you can manage space workload with workload classes has been simplified. You can now either leave the default configuration for your space or select the custom configuration and enter statement limits.
Note that the section Workload Class has been renamed to Workload Management and the Statement Limits section has been renamed to Workload Configuration.
See [Set Priorities and Statement Limits for Spaces or Groups](d66ac1efb5054068a104c4559b72d272.html).
590834313.title: Simplified Workload Management Area

590834314.text:
Starting with this version, you no longer create and manage connections in spaces but directly in the new dedicated app Connections. You can still open the new app from the Connections section in Space Management.
See [Create a Connection](c2165842082c43fc85bad9f0c97572bb.html).
590834314.title: Connections Removed from Space Management
